label: S0456
statement: REPAIR LEMMA (explicit candidate filtering with separated costs). Let C_1,...,C_K be a finite indexed family of Boolean circuits, and suppose the position-dependent bits e_{i,j}=C_i(a_j) are supplied as constants. For a prefix p, let z_i(p)=1 exactly when C_i agrees with p on every position already read. On reading bit b at position j, update each coordinate by z'_i=z_i AND [e_{i,j}=b]. This transition uses at most K fan-in-two AND gates. The predicate that at least one listed circuit matches the prefix is OR_{i=1}^K z_i and uses max(K-1,0) fan-in-two OR gates. Thus transition plus acceptance uses at most K+max(K-1,0) gates if both are counted. Proof: Initially all coordinates are 1, which records agreement with the empty prefix. Assume the coordinates record agreement through the positions before j. A listed circuit agrees through position j exactly when it previously agreed and its supplied bit e_{i,j} equals b; the update therefore preserves the invariant. Induction gives the invariant for every prefix. Its disjunction is true exactly when some listed circuit matches. Each update coordinate requires at most one AND gate; a binary OR tree on K inputs uses K-1 gates when K>=1 and zero gates when K=0. The two computations have separate costs, so no claim of a K+1 combined bound is needed. Scope: explicit finite families with supplied position-dependent constants; this does not bound preprocessing, give a polynomial-in-s implementation for EXT, or simulate arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement:
statement: Residual derivative identity. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p a length-t prefix. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb)={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu in R_t(p)}. Therefore EXT_F(pb)=1 iff this derivative set is nonempty, where EXT_F(p) means R_t(p) is nonempty. Proof: for every u of length N-t-1, u∈R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu∈F iff bu∈R_t(p), by associativity of concatenation and the definition of R_t. Equality follows by extensionality; nonemptiness gives the stated equivalence.
scope: All finite Boolean-string families F⊆{0,1}^N and valid t,p,b. This is a semantic transition identity only; it gives no efficient representation or update-time bound when F=Im(Eval).
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing—yes, the identity is representation-free and oracle-independent; natural—no circuit lower bound or largeness/easiness property; algebrizing—no algebraic argument; localizing—no locality claim. Circumvention tests: none claimed; this is a set identity, not a P-vs-NP route.

label: S0458
statement:
statement: Explicit-family trie lemma. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N with M=|F|. Let P(F) contain the empty string and every prefix of every member of F. There is a deterministic streaming automaton with one state for each p∈P(F), plus a dead state ⊥. From p on bit b it moves to pb if pb∈P(F), and otherwise to ⊥; ⊥ loops to itself. It accepts exactly the viable prefixes. The automaton has at most 2+MN states. Given F explicitly, a trie constructs it in O(MN) time and space, and a transition is one child-pointer lookup. Proof: Initially the state is the empty prefix, which is viable since F is nonempty. Inductively, if the state is p, after reading b the new prefix is pb; it is viable exactly when pb∈P(F), which is precisely the transition rule. If the state is ⊥, no extension can become viable. Hence the state after any input prefix p is p if p∈P(F), and ⊥ otherwise; acceptance therefore agrees with EXT_F. Each of the M strings contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, so |P(F)|≤1+MN; adding ⊥ gives at most 2+MN states. Inserting each explicitly listed string and its prefixes builds the trie in O(MN) time and space, and each transition follows one child pointer.
scope: All nonempty explicitly listed F⊆{0,1}^N. This is a RAM/trie lookup bound with O(log(MN+2)) state bits and O(MN) preprocessing/storage; it gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound when F=Im(Eval_{n,s}) is only implicit.
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing—yes, the construction is oracle-independent; natural—no lower-bound property; algebrizing—no algebraic method; localizing—no locality claim. No P-vs-NP circumvention is claimed.

statement:
statement: Levelwise residual-state characterization. Fix a finite family F⊆{0,1}^N. For 0≤t≤N and each length-t prefix p, define R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}: p·u∈F}. Let r_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p) as p ranges over {0,1}^t. A deterministic layered streaming automaton that, at level t, must determine for every continuation u whether p·u∈F needs at least r_t distinguishable states at that level; storing R_t(p) uses exactly r_t states and supports the exact transition R_{t+1}(p·b)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: b·u∈R_t(p)}. Proof: If R_t(p)≠R_t(q), choose u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of p·u and q·u is in F. Any deterministic automaton in the same level with the same state after p and q would give identical acceptance on continuation u, a contradiction. Thus all r_t residuals require distinct states. Conversely, use the distinct residual sets as level-t states. On bit b transition to the set {u: b·u∈R}; by the definition of residuals this is R_{t+1}(p·b) whenever R=R_t(p). At level N, accept iff the residual contains the empty string. This recognizes F exactly.
scope: Finite F⊆{0,1}^N, fixed bit order, deterministic layered automata whose required output is membership of the completed string in F. The result characterizes state count at each level; it gives no efficient encoding, transition computation, or polynomial update bound for F=Im(Eval_{n,s}).
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing—yes, combinatorial and oracle-independent; natural—no lower-bound property; algebrizing—no algebraic method; localizing—no locality claim. No P-vs-NP progress claimed.

label: S0460
statement: statement: Layered projection construction. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size T. For each prefix length t and prefix p in {0,1}^t, define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t} with H(pz)=1. For each such p, a fan-in-two circuit computing E_t(p) can be constructed by placing one copy of H for each of the 2^(N-t) suffixes and ORing their outputs, with size at most 2^(N-t)(T+1)-1. Consequently, for every t<N the two child extension values E_{t+1}(p0), E_{t+1}(p1) are obtained by the same construction with 2^(N-t-1) copies each; together, the two child circuits have size at most 2^(N-t)(T+1)-2. Proof: E_t(p)=OR_{z in {0,1}^{N-t}} H(pz), by definition. Each term is implemented by a copy of H with its first t input wires fixed to p and remaining wires fixed to z; this does not increase the gate count. A binary OR tree on q=2^(N-t) outputs uses q-1 gates, so size is at most qT+(q-1)=q(T+1)-1. Applying this with q/2 completions to each child gives two costs 2[(q/2)T+(q/2-1)]=q(T+1)-2. The construction is uniform given H, p, and the truth-table input order, but exponential in the unobserved suffix length in general.

label: S0461
statement:
statement: Residual-state counting and transition lemma: for finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and each level t, define R_p={z: pz in F} for length-t prefixes p. There are at most min(2^t,|F|) distinct nonempty residuals and at most one empty residual; for t<N, R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}. The layered residual automaton recognizes F exactly.
proof: There are 2^t prefixes. Every prefix with nonempty residual extends to an element of F, and distinct prefixes have distinct extensions, so there are at most |F| such prefixes. The count of distinct nonempty residuals is bounded by the count of those prefixes. All empty residuals equal the empty set. For the transition, z in R_{pb} iff pbz in F iff bz in R_p. Finally, R_x is nonempty exactly when x in F.
scope: Finite binary languages, fixed length N and coordinate order; exact layered state characterization only.

label: S0462
statement:
statement: Residual equivalence exactly characterizes mergeable prefixes in deterministic layered streaming for any finite fixed-length language F: at level t, p and q may share a state only if R_p=R_q; equal residuals admit identical continuation acceptance and define a well-defined residual transition.
proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose a suffix z in their symmetric difference; precisely one of pz,qz is in F, contradicting deterministic identical continuation behavior from a common state. If R_p=R_q, every suffix has the same acceptance outcome from p and q. The residual transition is well-defined since R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}; equal parent residuals yield equal child residuals. The residual-class machine accepts exactly F at the terminal level.
scope: Finite F subset {0,1}^N, fixed input order; exact deterministic layered streaming only, no efficiency claim.

label: S0463
statement:
statement: Exact residual-width lemma. Let F be any finite subset of {0,1}^N and, for each t, let d_t be the number of distinct residuals R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} over prefixes p of length t. Every deterministic layered streaming recognizer for F has at least d_t states at level t; a recognizer with exactly d_t states at each level exists.
proof: For the lower bound, suppose prefixes p and q with different residuals reach the same state. Choose z in the symmetric difference of R_p and R_q. Exactly one of pz and qz belongs to F, but deterministic processing from the common state on the same suffix z must give the same result, a contradiction. Thus each distinct residual requires a distinct state. For the upper bound, use the residuals themselves as states. On input bit b, map R_p to its left quotient {z: bz is in R_p}; this equals R_{pb}, so the transition is well-defined even when multiple prefixes have the same residual. At level N, accept exactly the nonempty residual. This recognizes F and has d_t states at level t.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N, fixed input order, deterministic layered streaming; no uniform construction or transition-cost claim.
known_closest: Myhill–Nerode residual equivalence for deterministic automata, specialized to fixed-length layered machines.
novelty: Gives the exact minimum width at every layer, rather than only a necessary state-merging condition.
obstacle: For EXT_{n,s}, this does not bound d_t or show that residual transitions can be implemented with bounded real-gate cost from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
attack: Use a distinguishing suffix for unequal residuals to prove the width lower bound, then construct the matching residual-state machine using left quotients.

statement:
statement: Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite family of Boolean strings of length N. At depth t, for each prefix p define R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: p concatenated with u lies in F}. The number of distinct R_p at depth t is at most min(2^t,2^M), hence the total number of depth-labelled residual states is at most sum_{t=0}^N min(2^t,2^M). Proof: there are 2^t prefixes, and every residual set is determined by the subset of the M indexed strings extending p, of which there are at most 2^M. For a next bit b, the exact residual transition retains precisely those suffixes beginning in b and deletes their first bit, so it is well-defined on residual sets. This state-count bound does not bound the real-gate cost of computing the transition or its construction cost.
scope: All finite indexed families F of M Boolean strings of common length N, with depth-labelled residuals.

statement: LEMMA (explicit-family candidate filtering). Let F be a finite set of M distinct strings in {0,1}^N, with coordinates ordered 0,...,N-1. For each prefix p of length t define z_f(p)=1 iff f agrees with p on coordinates 0,...,t-1. Then z(p) exactly represents the strings in F extending p; on reading bit b at coordinate t, set z'_f=z_f AND [f_t=b] for every f in F. With the coordinate tests supplied, this transition has at most M fan-in-two AND gates. The prefix is extendible to a member of F iff OR_{f in F} z_f=1, using at most M-1 fan-in-two OR gates when M>=1. Proof: At t=0 all strings agree with the empty prefix. Assuming the invariant at t, a string agrees with the prefix extended by b exactly when it agreed through t-1 and its t-th bit equals b, which is the stated coordinate update. Induction proves the invariant at every prefix length; the OR is true exactly when the represented set is nonempty. Scope: explicit finite F with supplied position-dependent coordinate tests. This gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound for circuit truth tables and no implementation through an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

statement: statement: Affine-prefix extension lemma. For n>=0, let F_n be the Boolean affine functions f(x)=c+sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i over GF(2), and fix any ordering x^(0),...,x^(2^n-1) of {0,1}^n. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, EXT^aff_n(p)=1 iff the GF(2) linear system c+sum_i a_i x_i^(j)=p_j for 0<=j<t is consistent. After each new truth-table bit p_t at position x^(t), appending the corresponding equation and maintaining a row-echelon basis gives an exact streaming algorithm with at most n+1 coefficient variables and O((n+1)^2) bit operations per update; initialization is the empty system. Proof: Each affine function corresponds exactly to one coefficient vector (c,a_1,...,a_n) in GF(2)^(n+1). The prefix is extendible by an affine function exactly when one such vector satisfies all t displayed equations, which is exactly consistency. Inductively, the maintained row-echelon basis represents precisely the solution set of the equations seen so far. Appending the next equation and eliminating its pivot preserves that represented solution set; a contradiction row arises exactly when no coefficient vector extends the prefix. Thus the algorithm decides prefix extendibility exactly. A basis has at most n+1 rows of length n+2, and insertion/elimination costs O((n+1)^2) bit operations. This proves an efficient transition bound for the affine subclass only; it makes no claim about EXT for arbitrary size-s circuits or simulation through arbitrary H_C.

statement:
statement: Residual-language identity for EXT: Fix n,s and a finite set F of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with truth-table positions ordered 0,...,N-1 where N=2^n. For a prefix p of length t, define Ext_F(p) as the set of strings q in {0,1}^{N-t} for which the concatenation pq is the truth table of some f in F. For each f in F, let r_{f,t} be the suffix (f(t),...,f(N-1)), and let A_F(p)={f in F: f agrees with p on positions 0,...,t-1}. Then Ext_F(p)={r_{f,t}: f in A_F(p)}. proof: Fix q of length N-t. By definition, q belongs to Ext_F(p) iff pq is the truth table of some f in F. This proves both set inclusions and hence the identity. If A_F(p)=A_F(p'), the displayed descriptions give equal extension sets. Finally, the set of suffixes displayed is nonempty exactly when A_F(p) is nonempty.

label: S0468
statement:
statement: Residual-state lower bound. Let F be any finite family of length-N binary strings, and for each t let R_t(p)={q in {0,1}^{N-t}: pq is in F} for p in {0,1}^t. Every deterministic streaming machine that decides whether the full input lies in F must have at least |{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}| distinct states after t input bits. Proof: if R_t(p) and R_t(p') differ, choose q in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pq,p'q belongs to F. If the machine were in the same state after p and p', determinism gives identical future behavior on common suffix q and hence the same final answer, a contradiction. Thus each distinct residual requires a distinct state; the state-bit lower bound is ceil(log2 of the maximum such count over t).
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and deterministic exact streaming deciders; this is a state-count bound only, not a transition-cost claim.

label: S0469
statement:
statement: Residual-width upper bound for finite languages. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For each t, the number of distinct nonempty residual sets R_t(p)={q in {0,1}^{N-t}: pq in F}, over p in {0,1}^t, is at most min(2^t, |F|). If the empty residual is included, the total number of residuals is at most min(2^t, |F|)+1. Proof: There are only 2^t prefixes. Each word in F has a unique length-t prefix, so the nonempty residuals partition F into nonempty parts; their number is therefore at most |F|. There is at most one empty residual. Taking both bounds gives the claim.
scope: All finite nonempty F subseteq {0,1}^N and each t in 0..N. This bounds canonical automaton state width only; it gives no transition-cost bound for EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0470
statement:
statement: EXT residual-width bound by represented truth tables. Fix n,s and N=2^n, and let F be the set of distinct length-N truth tables computed by Boolean circuits of size at most s. For every prefix length t, the canonical residual automaton for EXT_{n,s} has at most |F|+1 states at depth t, including the empty residual. Proof: for each prefix p, its residual R_t(p) is exactly the set of suffixes q such that pq belongs to F. Thus every nonempty residual is a nonempty subset of F consisting of words with the same length-t prefix. Distinct nonempty residuals are disjoint, because a full word has a unique length-t prefix. Choosing one word from each nonempty residual gives an injection into F, so there are at most |F| nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual. This is a state-count bound and gives no transition-cost bound or simulation by arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
scope: All n,s and t=0,...,2^n; F is the set of distinct truth tables of size-at-most-s circuits under the fixed input order. State count only.

label: S0471
statement:
statement: Continuation-witness characterization of deterministic exact states. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, fix a cut t, and let P_t(F) be the prefixes of length t that extend to an element of F. Define p ~_F p' iff for every suffix q in {0,1}^{N-t}, pq belongs to F exactly when p'q belongs to F. Every deterministic one-pass exact streaming machine recognizing F has at least |P_t(F)/~_F| states after t bits; moreover a machine with exactly that many reachable states at depth t exists when each depth is represented by its equivalence classes. Proof: If two prefixes lead to the same machine state, then for every suffix q the deterministic continuation from that state on q is identical, so acceptance of pq and p'q agrees; thus they are equivalent. Hence different equivalence classes require different states. Conversely, use the equivalence class of the consumed prefix as state. On bit b, map [p] at depth t to [pb] at depth t+1. This is well-defined: if p~p', then for every suffix r, membership of pbr in F equals membership of p'br in F, by applying the equivalence to suffix br. At depth N accept exactly classes whose represented prefix is in F. This constructs the layered canonical automaton.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and all cuts 0<=t<=N; deterministic exact one-pass automata with depth-aware states/transitions. The result characterizes required states but gives no bound on real-gate transition cost for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary H_C.

label: S0473
statement:
statement: Residual-state construction for a finite binary language. Let F⊆{0,1}^N. For each t and each length-t prefix p, set R_t(p)={r∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pr∈F}. Any deterministic exact one-pass machine recognizing F must reach different states after p and q whenever R_t(p)≠R_t(q). Conversely, a layered deterministic exact machine can use the residual sets R_t(p) as its states at depth t, including the empty residual; its transition on b maps R_t(p) to R_{t+1}(pb), and its terminal states accept exactly residual {ε}. Proof: If two prefixes reach the same state, every common continuation produces the same acceptance result, so their residual sets agree. For the construction, the residual after reading b is exactly {r:br∈R_t(p)}, which depends only on R_t(p) and b; hence the transition is well-defined. At depth N, the residual is {ε} exactly for prefixes in F and is empty otherwise, giving exact acceptance. This repairs S0471's converse by including nonextendable prefixes through the empty residual state.
scope: All finite F⊆{0,1}^N and deterministic exact one-pass automata with depth-aware state sets. This gives an exact state characterization/construction; it does not bound real-gate transition cost or implement transitions using arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

label: S0474
statement:
statement: Explicit completion expansion for EXT from a decision circuit. Let N=2^n, let L⊆{0,1}^N be the truth tables accepted by a Boolean circuit H of size h, and define EXT_L(p)=1 iff some q∈{0,1}^{N−|p|} has pq∈L. For each prefix length t, there is a Boolean circuit E_t with t input bits computing EXT_L on length-t prefixes, of size at most 2^{N−t}(h+1)−1 using fan-in-two gates, assuming H has h gates and fixed input order. Proof: For every suffix q of length N−t, make a copy H_q of H whose first t inputs are the variable prefix p and whose remaining inputs are the constants q. OR the 2^{N−t} output bits with a fan-in-two tree. The output is 1 exactly when at least one completion pq is accepted. The construction uses 2^{N−t}h gates for copies and 2^{N−t}−1 OR gates. At t=N it is H itself; at t=0 it is the constant indicating whether L is nonempty. Applied to L={truth tables with circuit complexity at most s}, this gives an exact EXT computation from any MCSP decision circuit H_C, but the bound can be exponential in N−t and therefore does not establish poly(s) transition cost.
scope: All N>=0, all Boolean languages L⊆{0,1}^N with a size-h decision circuit, and every cut 0<=t<=N. Fan-in-two circuit size counts gates; constants and input wiring are free. This is an explicit upper bound for computing the EXT predicate at one cut, not a lower bound or a streaming update implementation.

label: S0475
statement:
statement: LOGARITHMIC-TAIL COMPLETION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, where constants and wiring are free. For a cut t=N-k, define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists q in {0,1}^k with H(pq)=1. Then E_t is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^k(h+1)-1 gates. Consequently, if k<=c log_2(h+2) for a fixed constant c, E_t has size O((h+2)^(c+1)); in particular, for h=poly(s) it has size poly(s) whenever the unprocessed suffix length is O(log s). Proof: For each of the 2^k strings q, take a disjoint copy H_q of H with its first N-k inputs wired to p and its last k inputs fixed to q. OR the 2^k outputs using a binary OR tree, which uses 2^k-1 gates. H_q(p)=H(pq), so the OR computes E_t. The total gate count is 2^k h+(2^k-1)=2^k(h+1)-1. If k<=c log_2(h+2), then 2^k<=(h+2)^c, yielding size <=(h+2)^c(h+1)=O((h+2)^(c+1)). If h is polynomially bounded in s and k=O(log s), this is polynomial in s. This only constructs the completion predicate at cuts with logarithmic remaining suffix; it gives no poly(s) bound for early cuts, no update implementation for the full EXT automaton, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP circuits beyond their decision-circuit size h.
scope: All N>=0, all Boolean circuits H on N inputs, all cuts t with k=N-t, fan-in-two gate count with constants/wiring free. The polynomial consequence assumes the stated asymptotic bounds; no MCSP lower bound is claimed.

label: S0476
statement:
statement: Let L be any language of fixed-length words {0,1}^N recognized exactly by a deterministic left-to-right streaming machine. For each depth t and prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_L(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in L}. Any such machine has at least |{R_L(p):p in {0,1}^t}| distinct states after t symbols. Conversely, the layered machine whose depth-t states are the distinct sets R_L(p), with transition R_L(p) --b--> R_L(pb), recognizes L exactly. Therefore the minimum possible number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct accepting-continuation residuals at that depth. Proof: If two prefixes p,q reach the same deterministic state, then every continuation u induces the same accept/reject outcome from that state, so R_L(p)=R_L(q); contrapositively distinct residuals require distinct states. For the converse define the transition by appending b to any representative prefix; this is well-defined because equal residuals at depth t imply that for each b the residuals after pb agree, as membership of every remaining v is equivalent to bv belonging to the original residual. At depth N accept exactly when the empty continuation belongs to the residual. Induction on t proves the invariant that the state after p is R_L(p), hence exact recognition. This characterizes the information an exact fixed-length streaming algorithm must preserve; it provides no transition circuit bound in terms of an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All N>=0 and all Boolean languages L subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic streaming machines reading one bit per transition, with a fixed known depth. State lower bound is per layer; no uniformity, transition gate complexity, or MCSP simulation claim is included.

statement: statement: Residual-section lemma for EXT. Let N>=1, let F be any set of N-bit strings, and for each prefix p of length t<=N define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For t<N and b in {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently R_t(p) is the disjoint union of 0R_{t+1}(p0) and 1R_{t+1}(p1), where bA={bv:v in A}. Proof: For any v of length N-t-1, v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbv belongs to F, iff bv belongs to R_t(p). Every length-(N-t) string has a unique first bit b and remaining suffix v, so it belongs to exactly one of the two displayed sections; membership in that section is equivalent to pv with that first bit lying in F by the defining equivalence. Thus the pair of child residuals is exactly the information needed to reconstruct the parent residual, and each child is obtained by a fixed section operation. Scope: exact residual languages for any fixed-length target F, including EXT with F=Im(Eval); this proves the abstract transition identity only and gives no bound on representing or computing the sections in real gates from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

statement:
statement: Layerwise residual lower bound for exact streaming recognition. Let N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and 0<=t<=N. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and let r_t be the number of distinct residual sets. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in F exactly must reach at least r_t distinct states after t bits, hence needs at least ceil(log2 r_t) state bits (zero if r_t=1). Proof: If p and q have different residuals but lead to the same state, choose u in their symmetric difference. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states; a B-bit state has at most 2^B possibilities, so 2^B>=r_t. This applies to EXT_{n,s} for F equal to the set of size-at-most-s circuit truth tables in the fixed order, but does not bound transition gate cost or give a simulation from arbitrary H_C.

statement: Residual quotient automaton for a finite language. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pu in F}. Make one state for each distinct residual set at each layer, keeping layers distinct even if their sets coincide. From state R(p) at layer t, on bit b transition to R(pb) at layer t+1. This transition is well-defined: if R(p)=R(q) for |p|=|q|=t, then for every suffix u of length N-t-1, u is in R(pb) exactly when bu is in R(p), and likewise for q; hence R(pb)=R(qb). Declare the layer-N state accepting exactly when its residual contains the empty string. The resulting deterministic layered automaton recognizes F exactly and has r_t states at layer t, where r_t is the number of distinct residuals there. Combined with the distinguishability argument in S0478, this proves that r_t is the minimum possible number of states at layer t for any exact deterministic streaming recognizer. The construction does not bound the cost of computing its transitions from H_C or the total description size as a function of n and s.
scope: Every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass recognition with position known to the machine. State counts are per layer; no transition-complexity assertion.

structure.evidence: Direct construction and proof: successor residuals are determined solely by the current residual and next bit, because R(pb)={u: bu in R(p)}. Acceptance at the final layer is membership of the empty suffix. No computation is needed for this general finite-language lemma.

label: S0480
statement:
statement: Residual-language quotient lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t≤N and prefix p∈{0,1}^t, define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pu∈F}. In any deterministic layered streaming automaton that accepts exactly F, two length-t prefixes with different residual sets must lead to different states. Conversely, the residual sets at each layer form a deterministic layered automaton with transitions R ↦ {v∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv∈R} on input bit b, initial state R_empty=F, and acceptance at layer N iff the empty string belongs to R. Thus the minimum number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residual sets {R_p:|p|=t}. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pu,qu is in F. If the automaton had the same state after p and q, its deterministic processing of the same suffix u would have the same acceptance outcome, contradiction. For the converse, after prefix p the stored state R_p updates on bit b to R_pb by the definition of residual and concatenation; induction on prefix length gives exactness, and final acceptance is exactly membership in F.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N and deterministic layered streaming automata reading exactly N bits. It characterizes minimum state width layer by layer; it gives no bound on transition circuit cost or construction time, and no simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0481
statement:
statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound for EXT streaming states. Fix n,s and let L=EXT_{n,s} be the language of prefixes of truth tables of Boolean functions computable by size-at-most-s circuits, with the truth-table order fixed. For a prefix p, define R_p={z: pz is a prefix of a truth table in Im(Eval)}. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in L after every prefix and whose future behavior depends only on its current state must assign different states to p and q whenever R_p != R_q. Consequently it has at least |{R_p : p is a prefix}| states and at least ceil(log2 |{R_p : p is a prefix}|) state bits.
proof: Suppose R_p != R_q. Choose a suffix z in their symmetric difference; without loss of generality z is in R_p and not R_q. By definition, pz is a prefix of some size-at-most-s circuit truth table, whereas qz is not. If the machine reached the same state after p and q, then feeding the identical suffix z would produce the same future state sequence and the same final membership answer on both inputs, contradicting that one concatenation is in L and the other is not. Thus distinct residual sets require distinct states. The state-count and bit-count bounds follow by counting these pairwise distinguishable residual sets.
scope: All finite truth-table lengths N=2^n, all s>=0, fixed truth-table order, deterministic machines whose state completely determines future transitions and acceptance. This proves a state-width requirement only; it gives no transition-cost lower bound and no simulation of an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

label: S0482
statement:
statement: Equal-level residual distinguishability for EXT. Fix n,s, N=2^n, a truth-table order, and a level t in {0,...,N}. Let L=EXT_{n,s} be the set of prefixes of truth tables of functions computable by circuits of size at most s. For each length-t prefix p define R_{p,t}={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is a full truth table of a function computable by a size-at-most-s circuit}. Any deterministic streaming machine that, after reading all N bits, decides whether the full string is such a circuit truth table must reach distinct states after any two length-t prefixes p,q with R_{p,t} != R_{q,t}. Hence it has at least |{R_{p,t}:p in {0,1}^t}| states at level t, and at least ceil(log2 |{R_{p,t}:p in {0,1}^t}|) state bits at that level.
proof: If R_{p,t} and R_{q,t} differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Both prefixes have length t, so the same suffix z has length N-t and places both computations at the same subsequent input positions. Exactly one of pz and qz is a truth table in the target family. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism implies that processing the identical suffix z leads to the same final state and output, contradicting correctness on those two full strings. Thus distinct residual sets force distinct level-t states. Counting these residual sets yields the state and bit lower bounds.
scope: Every fixed n,s, truth-table order, and level t. The language decision is on complete N-bit truth tables; this statement yields only a state-width lower bound at each level, not transition-cost bounds or a simulation/lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

label: S0484
statement:
statement: Candidate-vector transition accounting for EXT. Fix a finite indexed list C_1,...,C_K of length-N candidate truth tables and a stream position t. Let z_i indicate whether candidate i matches the prefix of length t, and let c_i=[C_i(t)=b] be supplied position-dependent constants for the next input bit b. Then the exact next state is z'_i=z_i AND c_i for every i. Thus each next-state coordinate is either the input wire z_i or the constant 0, so the transition map requires zero fan-in-two Boolean gates when wires and hardwired constants are free. The separate acceptance readout OR_i z_i takes K-1 fan-in-two OR gates for K>=1 (zero gates for K=1). Proof: Candidate i matches the extended prefix exactly when it matched the previous prefix and its bit at position t equals b, which is precisely z_i AND c_i. Since c_i is fixed for the transition, this expression is z_i when c_i=1 and 0 when c_i=0. A binary OR tree combines K bits in K-1 gates. This is an exact cost decomposition for the explicit candidate-vector representation; it gives no polynomial-in-s bound when K is exponential in the circuit-description length and no simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
scope: All finite candidate lists, fixed truth-table orders, and positions, with position-dependent comparison constants supplied; the transition gate count excludes state storage and readout, which is separately K-1 gates.

label: S0500
statement: For D>=1, E>=1, m=ceil(log2 D), r=ceil(log2 E), and deterministic maps delta_0,delta_1 from a D-element state set X to an E-element set Y, the encoded transition function on valid state codes and one input bit has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size at most r(2Dm+2D+m). Proof: For each output coordinate enumerate the t<=2D valid pairs (x,b) yielding output 1. Each minterm uses at most m AND gates on m+1 literals; if t>0 the OR costs t-1 gates; shared input negations cost at most m+1. The total is at most mt+(t-1)+(m+1)<=2Dm+2D+m. An empty disjunction is constant 0. Repeating over r coordinates proves the claim. This bound repairs the incorrect inequality in S0431.

label: S0502
statement: statement: LEMMA (EXT as existential projection of a decision circuit). Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} decide membership in a family F of N-bit strings, and let EXT_H(p)=1 iff some member of F extends prefix p. For every prefix p of length t, EXT_H(p)=OR_{u in {0,1}^{N-t}} H(pu). For b in {0,1} and t<N, EXT_H(pb)=OR_{u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}} H(pbu). Proof: By the definition of concatenation, the strings extending p are exactly the pu with |u|=N-t; membership in F is exactly H(pu)=1. The same argument applies after fixing next bit b. Thus the exact next-state values are existential projections of H, with the explicit disjunction using 2^(N-t) and 2^(N-t-1) evaluations respectively. This gives no bounded-call or gate-cost-preserving reduction for arbitrary H.

label: S0503
statement: statement: LEMMA (EXT prefix has a short verifiable circuit witness). Fix n,s and an explicit binary encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits with at most s gates, where each gate record uses O(log(n+s)) bits and the output wire is specified in the description. Let N=2^n. For each t in {0,...,N}, define EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 for p in {0,1}^t iff there exists a valid description d of at most L=O(s log(n+s)) bits whose circuit C_d agrees with p on the first t inputs in the fixed truth-table order. Then EXT_{n,s}(p) is in NP with witness length at most L+O(1) and deterministic verification time O(t(s+n)+L), in a standard gate-list encoding. Proof: Guess d, reject if it is not a valid circuit description of the stated size, then for each of the t input strings evaluate the s-gate circuit in topological order and compare its output with the corresponding bit of p. One circuit evaluation costs O(s+n) including input access under the stated encoding, so all comparisons cost O(t(s+n)); description validation and parsing cost O(L). The verifier accepts exactly when a size-at-most-s circuit has the required prefix, which is exactly the defining existential condition. Scope: this proves a nondeterministic upper bound and an explicit certificate/checking cost only; it gives no deterministic transition algorithm, no compression of the candidate set, and no hardness lower bound.

label: S0504
statement: statement: LEMMA (listed-family EXT update). Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n inputs, and let E_j be their truth tables in a fixed order. For a prefix p of length t<2^n, define A={j: E_j[0..t-1]=p}. Then EXT_F(p0)=OR_{j in A}[E_j[t]=0] and EXT_F(p1)=OR_{j in A}[E_j[t]=1]. Proof: A candidate extends p followed by b exactly when it agrees with p and its next output is b; existential quantification over F is therefore the displayed OR. Given circuit descriptions, both bits have real fan-in-two circuits of size O(M(t+1)(s+n)): evaluate each candidate on the first t inputs and input t, test the t prefix bits, combine each test with the next output, then OR over candidates. This construction is exact and explicit. Scope: it gives an enumeration upper bound only; it does not bound M polynomially or implement the update from an arbitrary fixed H_C.

label: S0505
statement:
statement: LEMMA (explicit-family streaming update). Let F=(C_1,...,C_d) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. At stream position i, represent the live candidates by a vector a in {0,1}^d, where a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with all previously read truth-table bits. On reading b, set a'_j=a_j AND (b iff C_j(i)=1), and increment i. This is exact: by induction on the number of read bits, a'_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the entire extended prefix. A transition can be implemented by evaluating each C_j on the binary encoding of i and ANDing its equality-to-b test with a_j; with straightforward fan-in-two circuitry this costs O(d(s+n)) gates, including the index increment. Thus explicit candidate tracking is polynomial when d,s,n are polynomially bounded, but the lemma gives no polynomial bound when d is the full circuit-description count.

statement: LEMMA (finite residual update). Let N=2^n and let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t≤N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pz∈F}. For t<N and b∈{0,1}, R_{pb}={u∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu∈R_p}. Consequently, R_p is nonempty iff p has an extension in F, and updating the residual after reading b is exactly taking the b-slice of R_p. Proof: For each u of length N−t−1, u∈R_{pb} iff pbu∈F by definition of R_{pb}; this holds iff bu∈R_p by definition of R_p; hence the sets are equal. Nonemptiness follows directly from the definition. This is an exact information-level update identity for every finite family F; it gives no bound on the cost of representing or computing the slice for EXT_{n,s} or from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-list update circuit). Fix n≥1, a finite list C_1,…,C_M of n-input Boolean circuits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and enumerate inputs as x_t=bin_n(t) for 0≤t<2^n. A state is (t,a_1,…,a_M), where a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with the streamed prefix of length t. There is a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT transition circuit taking (t,a_1,…,a_M,b) to (t+1,a'_1,…,a'_M), with wraparound at t=2^n−1, of size O(n+M(s+1)). It satisfies a'_j=a_j∧[C_j(x_t)=b] for every valid state. Proof: wire the n bits of t as x_t; evaluate each hardwired C_j using at most s gates; compare its output with b using O(1) gates and AND with a_j. Increment t modulo 2^n using O(n) gates. Each a'_j is 1 exactly when C_j agreed on the prior t positions and agrees at position t. Induction from (0,1,…,1) proves the invariant. This upper bound concerns only the explicit-list representation; it does not bound M polynomially in n,s or give a lower bound for arbitrary encodings or H_C.

label: S0511
statement: LEMMA (residual-width bound for a finite candidate family). Let F be a nonempty family of K distinct binary strings of length N. For 0<=t<=N, for each length-t prefix u define R_u={v in {0,1}^{N-t}: uv in F}; let q_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_u. Then q_t <= min(K, 2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Proof: There are at most 2^t prefixes u, hence at most 2^t residuals. Every nonempty residual contains at least one suffix v from a member uv of F; choosing one such member for each distinct residual gives distinct members of F, since distinct residual sets cannot be witnessed by the same member's prefix group. Thus q_t<=K. Finally each residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) possible suffixes, so there are at most 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residual sets. Taking all three bounds proves the claim. Consequence: the exact level-t residual automaton can store its active state in one-hot form using q_t bits (plus a rejecting sink if desired); its binary transition at that level can be implemented by routing each source state/input pair to the unique next residual or sink, with O(q_t) fan-in-two gates. This sharpens the candidate-list representation to a bound controlled by distinct residuals, but q_t can still be as large as K and the result does not give a polynomial-in-(s,n) update for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary MCSP circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (explicit circuit-list size bound). Fix n>=1 and s>=0. In the model of topologically ordered circuits with n designated input wires, at most s gates each chosen from AND, OR, NOT (with fan-in at most two), and one designated output wire, the number M of circuit descriptions is at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s. Proof: For a circuit with exactly j gates, each gate has at most 3(n+s)^2 choices: one of three gate types and an ordered pair of sources among at most n+s available wires (this overcounts unary NOT gates and allows unused later wires, so is an upper bound). statement: LEMMA (right-residual state characterization). Let A be a finite set of binary strings of common length N, let L=Pref(A), and for each prefix p let L_p={u: pu is in L}. In any deterministic streaming automaton recognizing L, prefixes p and q that reach the same state have L_p=L_q. Conversely, the distinct sets L_p form the states of a deterministic automaton recognizing L, with transition from L_p on bit b to L_{pb}; the empty residual is a rejecting sink. Thus the minimum number of states equals the number of distinct right residuals among prefixes, including the empty residual if it occurs.
derivation: If p and q reach the same deterministic state, every continuation u produces the same acceptance result after p and q. Since acceptance after p followed by u is exactly the predicate pu∈L, this implies L_p=L_q. Therefore prefixes with distinct residuals must reach distinct states. Conversely, define states to be the distinct residuals L_p and define δ(L_p,b)={u:bu∈L_p}. By definition this set is L_{pb}, so the transition is well-defined on residuals: if L_p=L_q, then {u:bu∈L_p}={u:bu∈L_q}. Declare a residual accepting iff it contains the empty string. Starting from L_ε, induction on the streamed prefix shows the current state is exactly L_p; hence the automaton recognizes L. The empty residual transitions to itself and is rejecting. The lower and upper bounds on the state count coincide.

statement: LEMMA (prefix residual state-count bound). Let A be a finite nonempty subset of {0,1}^N with |A|=M, and let L=Pref(A). The minimal deterministic automaton for L has at most 1+sum_{k=0}^N min(2^k,M) states.
derivation: For each k in 0..N, a nonempty right residual L_p arises only from a length-k prefix p of some word in A. There are at most 2^k such prefixes. There are also at most M such prefixes because distinct length-k prefixes have disjoint sets of descendant words in A, each nonempty. Hence there are at most min(2^k,M) nonempty residuals arising at depth k. Summing these upper bounds over depths may overcount residuals shared across depths, which is harmless. There is at most one additional empty residual. By the right-residual characterization, the number of distinct residuals bounds the minimal automaton state count.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (explicit-family EXT update circuit). Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be a fixed list of Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and let the streamed bits be the truth table of length 2^n in binary input order. There is a deterministic exact EXT-prefix update representation using n+M state bits and at most O(n+M(s+1)) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates per update. The state stores the next input index i in n bits and a candidate mask a in M bits. On next bit b, evaluate each C_j at i, then set a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(i)=b], and increment i modulo 2^n. After k updates, a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with all k streamed bits. Thus the mask is nonempty exactly when the prefix has a completion in the listed family. Proof: Initially i=0 and all candidates are live. At each update, the equality test removes precisely the candidates whose next truth-table bit differs from b; incrementing i selects the next truth-table position. Induction on k proves the invariant. Each circuit evaluation costs O(s), each comparison and mask update O(1), and the binary counter increment costs O(n), giving the stated bound. This is an explicit-family bound; M may be exponential, so it does not bound the implicit family of all size-s circuits by poly(s,n).
scope: Finite explicitly listed circuit families; exact fan-in-two Boolean update circuits; no claim about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or compact implicit-family updates.

statement: LEMMA (exact residual-state characterization for finite prefix languages). Let L be a finite set of binary strings, and for every prefix p define R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of some word in L}. Any deterministic streaming machine whose state after reading p determines, for every suffix z, whether pz is a prefix of a word in L must place p and q in different states whenever R_p != R_q. Conversely, assigning one state to each distinct set R_p (and a rejecting sink for strings that cease to be prefixes) gives a deterministic machine recognizing the prefix language of L. Hence the minimum number of states is exactly the number of distinct residual sets, with the sink included when needed. Proof: If R_p != R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. The required answers after p and q on continuation z differ. A deterministic machine in the same state after p and q would, on the same continuation z, produce the same answer, contradiction. For the converse, after reading bit b from residual R_p, the residual becomes R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}; this is determined by R_p and b. If R_p is empty, transition to the sink. Acceptance is determined by whether the empty suffix belongs to the residual. This proves the transition and acceptance rules are well-defined. Applied to L=Im(Eval) for size-at-most-s circuits, these residuals are precisely the completion sets relevant to EXT. This characterizes required information but asserts no bound on real-gate transition cost.

statement: LEMMA (residual distinguishability at a fixed depth). Let L be a finite set of binary words, and let p and q be words of the same length t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{*: |z|=N-t and pz in L}, where N is the common word length of L}; define R_q analogously. Then exactly one of pz and qz belongs to L. Consequently, the number of states reached by length-t prefixes is at least the number of distinct residual sets R_p at that depth. This applies to EXT for any finite family of equal-length truth tables, with L equal to that family. It gives an information-state lower bound only; it does not bound transition gate cost or connect EXT to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (residual distinguishability at a fixed depth). Let L be a finite set of binary words, and let p and q be words of the same length t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{*: |z|=N-t and pz in L}, where N is the common word length of L}; define R_q analogously. In every deterministic automaton that accepts exactly L, if R_p != R_q then the states reached after p and q are distinct. Proof: Since the sets differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pz and qz belongs to L. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would make the automaton's result after reading the common suffix z identical from both states, contradicting that exactly one word is accepted. Consequently, the number of states reached by length-t prefixes is at least the number of distinct residual sets R_p at that depth. statement: LEMMA (quotient transition). Let F be a finite set of Boolean strings, all of length N. For each prefix p of length t≤N, define R(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pz∈F}. Define p≈q (necessarily equal lengths) iff R(p)=R(q). Then for every t<N and b∈{0,1}, R(pb)={w∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bw∈R(p)}. Consequently p≈q implies pb≈qb for each b, so the residual equivalence classes at each depth have well-defined transitions under appending a bit. Proof: For any w of length N−t−1, w∈R(pb) iff pbw∈F iff bw∈R(p), giving the set identity. If R(p)=R(q), filtering both sets by strings beginning with b and deleting that first bit gives identical sets R(pb)=R(qb). This proves transition well-definedness for the minimal residual quotient, including empty residuals. Scope: finite equal-length string family; says nothing about the number of quotient states, how to construct a quotient state from a compact circuit description, or the real-gate cost of its transition.

statement: LEMMA (residual quotient width). Let F be a finite family of K Boolean strings of common length N. At depth t, 0<=t<=N, partition all length-t prefixes by equality of their residual sets R(p)={z: pz in F}. The number of equivalence classes is at most min(2^t,K)+1. Proof: Every nonempty residual class contains a prefix p occurring as the length-t prefix of at least one word in F. Distinct such prefixes number at most 2^t and at most K, so there are at most min(2^t,K) distinct nonempty residual sets. All prefixes with empty residual, if any, belong to a single additional class. Thus the total is at most min(2^t,K)+1. At t=0 the bound remains valid (there is only one prefix, and hence at most one class). Scope: finite equal-length string families; this is a width bound in terms of |F| and does not bound the transition circuit cost from a compact representation of F.

statement: LEMMA (enumerated-candidate update circuit). Fix n,s and an explicitly listed set C of D Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Maintain a D-bit vector a, with a_C=1 exactly when candidate C agrees with all truth-table prefix bits seen so far, and let i be the address of the next row. On receiving bit b, update a'_C = a_C AND (b iff C(i)). This update is implementable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of O(D(s+1)) gates; if the n-bit address is maintained internally, add O(n) gates for its increment. Proof: Evaluate each candidate's given gate list on the common n-bit address, costing at most s gates per candidate. Compare its output to b with a constant-size Boolean circuit, then AND with its prior agreement flag. This costs O(s+1) gates per candidate. A ripple-carry counter increments the address in O(n) gates. By induction on prefix length, a_C is 1 exactly for candidates agreeing with every bit seen. This is an explicit upper bound for an enumerated family; it does not remove the dependence on D or bound arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-filter update cost). Fix n and a finite list C_1,...,C_K of Boolean circuits, each with n inputs and at most s fan-in-two gates. Stream the truth table in binary input order, maintaining an n-bit index i and K live bits a_j, where a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with every streamed bit so far. On receipt of bit b, the exact update map on valid states can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(K(s+n)+n) gates. Proof: For each j, evaluate the hardwired C_j at the current index i, using at most s gates, and compute e_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] with O(1) additional gates. These K evaluations and filters cost O(K(s+1)). Increment i modulo 2^n with an n-bit ripple-carry circuit costing O(n) gates. The resulting live bits satisfy the stated invariant by induction on the number of streamed bits: each candidate remains live precisely when it was previously live and its next output agrees with b. Thus the update is exact and has the claimed gate bound. Scope: explicitly listed candidates with a separate live bit per candidate; this bound does not give a polynomial-in-s update for the full circuit list, nor a bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits represented by H_C.

statement: statement: LEMMA (explicit exhaustive EXT update bound). Fix n≥1 and s≥0. Let C be the set of Boolean functions computed by circuits with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, constants, and one designated output, on n inputs. There is a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that decides whether each prefix p extends to the truth table of some function in C, using at most D=1+(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s candidate bits and at most O(D·s+n+s) elementary operations per streamed bit, with O(D+n+s) bits of working storage. Proof: enumerate all topologically ordered descriptions with exactly j gates for each 0≤j≤s, choosing each gate’s type and its two predecessor wires from at most n+j+2 available wires, then choosing one output wire. This enumerates a superset of C with at most the stated D descriptions (overcounting is harmless). Keep one live bit per description. Initially all are live. At truth-table position i, evaluate each live description on input i by evaluating its at most s gates, and clear it iff its output differs from the incoming bit. Inductively, after prefix p, the live descriptions are exactly those whose truth tables begin with p. Thus the algorithm accepts exactly when at least one live bit remains. statement: statement: LEMMA (precomputed residual-mask update). Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite set of distinct binary strings of common length N, in a fixed order. For prefix p of length i, let A_p={j: f_j extends p}. For each i<N and b in {0,1}, define the M-bit mask B_{i,b} by B_{i,b}[j]=1 iff f_j[i]=b. Encode p by the indicator vector a_p of A_p. Then the exact transition on b is a_{pb}=a_p AND B_{i,b}, coordinatewise, and p is accepted iff a_p is nonzero. Explicitly storing the masks uses 2NM bits; storing the state uses M bits. With word size w, an update takes ceil(M/w) wordwise AND operations plus O(1) position-update operations. The claim includes dead prefixes; the preprocessing and storage may be large and this gives no lower bound for other representations or real-gate transition circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (residual quotient lower bound for exact streaming states). Let F be a finite set of binary words of common length N, and let L_F be its prefix language, including the empty prefix and rejecting all non-prefixes. For each t, define R_t={ {u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} : p in {0,1}^t }. Any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that exactly decides L_F on length-N inputs has at least |R_t| distinct internal states after t input bits; hence it needs at least ceil(log_2 |R_t|) state bits at that layer. Proof: choose prefixes p,q of length t whose residual sets differ. Then some suffix u of length N-t belongs to exactly one residual set. Thus exactly one of pu, qu is in F, so exactly one full input is accepted. If the algorithm had the same state after p and q, determinism would give identical state evolution and identical final decision on the common continuation u, contradiction. Therefore each distinct residual set requires a distinct state. The statement is for exact deterministic streaming algorithms and does not lower-bound their transition circuit cost or apply to approximate/randomized machines.

structure.evidence: Unequal residual sets have a distinguishing suffix; equal machine states force equal outcomes on every common suffix. This proves the information lower bound for exact deterministic machines. It leaves the transition-cost bridge in Q-156fa9c912 open.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual states are exactly the information needed by deterministic streaming). Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz is in L}. A deterministic streaming algorithm that decides membership in L after reading N bits can use the residual R_p as its state after prefix p: on bit b, update R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p}, and at length N accept exactly when the empty string belongs to R_p. Moreover, if R_p and R_q are distinct for two prefixes of the same length, every deterministic streaming algorithm correct for L must be in different states after p and q. Hence the minimum number of states at each fixed level is exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level.
evidence: Proof of sufficiency: after prefix p, store R_p. If the next bit is b, then for every suffix z of the required remaining length, (pb)z is in L iff p(bz) is in L iff bz is in R_p. Thus the updated set is precisely R_{pb}. After N bits, R_p is either {empty string} or empty, and membership is determined by whether it contains the empty string. For necessity, let p,q have equal length and distinct residuals. There is a suffix z in the symmetric difference of R_p and R_q. Then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. If a deterministic streaming algorithm reached the same state after p and q, its identical transition behavior on the common continuation z would give the same final answer for both, contradicting correctness. So those prefixes require distinct states. The state count is therefore exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level. This characterizes the information required for EXT, but gives no bound on the circuit cost of computing R_{pb} from a representation based on H_C.

statement: Let L⊆{0,1}^N be decided by a Boolean circuit H of size h, and let EXT_L(p) mean that p has an accepted completion in L. statement: BLOCK-TRANSITION EXPANSION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates (constants and input wiring are free). Fix integers t,r with 0<=t<=N and 0<=r<=N-t. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t and block u in {0,1}^r, define E_{t+r}(pu)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-r} such that H(puz)=1. There is a circuit B_{t,r} on (p,u) computing E_{t+r}(pu) with at most 2^{N-t-r}(h+1)-1 fan-in-two gates. Proof: For each suffix z of length N-t-r, make a disjoint copy H_z of H; wire its first t+r input positions to (p,u), and wire its remaining positions to the constant string z. OR all 2^{N-t-r} output bits using a binary tree, which uses 2^{N-t-r}-1 gates. The total is 2^{N-t-r}h+(2^{N-t-r}-1)=2^{N-t-r}(h+1)-1 gates. For every (p,u), this OR is 1 exactly when at least one completion z makes H(puz)=1. Thus if N-t-r<=c log_2(h+2) for fixed c, the size is polynomial in h. This constructs the block-completion predicate only; it does not show that a compact state or transition can be computed from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits at cost poly(s).

statement:
statement: Residual cofactor transition lemma. Let N be a nonnegative integer, F be any subset of {0,1}^N, 0 <= t < N, and p be a length-t prefix. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, define the cofactor D_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. Then R_{t+1}(pb)=D_b(R_t(p)). Consequently, if R_t(p)=R_t(q) for two length-t prefixes p,q, then for each bit b their child residuals are equal; and the pair of child residuals is determined by the full parent residual. Proof: For every v of length N-t-1, v is in R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbv is in F. This is equivalent to bv being in R_t(p), which is equivalent to v being in D_b(R_t(p)). Thus the sets agree. Replacing p by q gives the equal-child consequence when parent residuals coincide. The formula defines each child from the full residual by restriction to strings beginning in b. In contrast, the single bit [R_t(p) is nonempty] need not determine either child bit: for N-t=1, residuals {0} and {1} both have nonempty indicator 1, but their 0-child acceptance indicators differ. This is an exact information-level transition rule; it does not bound the number or real-gate cost of operations needed to compute a cofactor when the representation is an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

statement: One-bit branching-information lemma for EXT. Let F be a finite binary language of words of length N, let t<N, and for every length-t prefix p define e(p)=1 iff R_t(p) is nonempty. statement: Completion-circuit cofactor recurrence. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, and for each 0<=t<=N define E_t(p)=1 iff some suffix u in {0,1}^{N-t} satisfies H(pu)=1. If E_{t+d} is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of g gates, then E_t is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^d(g+1)-1 gates. Proof: For each of the 2^d suffixes v of length d, fix v in a copy of the E_{t+d} circuit, leaving the first t bits as inputs. The outputs compute E_{t+d}(pv); their OR is E_t(p), since every completion of p has a unique first d bits. A binary OR tree combines the 2^d outputs using 2^d-1 gates. statement: Penultimate-cut completion bound. Let N>=1 and let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and wiring free. For p in {0,1}^{N-1}, define E(p)=1 iff H(p0)=1 or H(p1)=1. Then E is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2h+1 gates. Proof: Make two copies of the circuit for H. label: S0581
statement:
statement: Dense residual streaming cost lemma. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be given by a fan-in-two circuit of h gates. A deterministic left-to-right streaming representation can initialize an N-stage residual table using at most h·2^N gate evaluations, store at most 2^N bits, and update it over the entire input using exactly 2^N−1 bit selections/writes (and no Boolean gates), if a state is represented as an explicit array indexed by suffixes and coordinate selection is the unit-cost update operation. Proof: At depth t store the array A_t[u]=H(pu), for all suffixes u of length N−t, where p is the prefix read so far. Initialize A_0 by evaluating H on each of the 2^N inputs, costing at most h·2^N gates and storing 2^N output bits. Upon reading b, form A_{t+1}[u]=A_t[bu] for each suffix u of length N−t−1. The identity follows directly: A_t[bu]=H(pbu)=A_{t+1}[u]. Thus each update copies one half of the old array and costs 2^(N−t−1) coordinate selections/writes. Summing over t=0,...,N−1 gives Σ_{j=0}^{N−1}2^j=2^N−1. The largest stored array is A_0, of 2^N bits. The update bound is in the stated explicit-array access model; it is not a fan-in-two Boolean circuit bound or a compact/poly(s) representation.
scope: All N≥0 and Boolean H with an h-gate fan-in-two circuit. Resource units are specified explicitly: Boolean gate evaluations for initialization, explicit stored bits, and unit-cost array coordinate selections/writes for updates.

statement: BINARY RESIDUAL PARTITION LEMMA. Let N>=1, L be a subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p in {0,1}^t. Define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in L. Then E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Proof: Every completion u has a unique decomposition u=bv, where b is a bit and v is a suffix of length N-t-1. There exists u with pu in L iff there exists b and v with pbv in L. This is equivalent to E_{t+1}(p0)=1 or E_{t+1}(p1)=1, by definition. When t=N-1, v is the empty string, so the boundary case is included. This is only a semantic recurrence and gives no real-gate cost bound from an arbitrary circuit H_C.

statement: Residual membership update lemma. Let L be a language of words of length N, let p have length t<N, and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in L}. For b in {0,1} and u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, the next residual membership bit satisfies 1[u in R_{t+1}(pb)] = 1[bu in R_t(p)]. Thus membership in the next residual is computable with one membership query to the current residual, by prefixing the queried suffix with b. Proof: u belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu belongs to L; this holds iff bu belongs to R_t(p), by the definition of R_t(p). This is an oracle-query identity only; it gives no bound on the real-gate cost of representing or querying R_t(p) from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

label: S0585
statement: statement: Restricted-circuit residual bound. Fix N,h≥0 and a fan-in-two Boolean circuit H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} with h gates; constants and wiring are free. For every t∈{0,…,N} and p∈{0,1}^t, let R_t(p)={q∈{0,1}^{N−t}:H(pq)=1}. Then R_t(p) is computed by a circuit H_p on N−t inputs with at most h gates, obtained by substituting p into H. Under a topological encoding listing each gate type and its two predecessor indices, plus the output source, the number D_t of distinct residuals is at most (c(N+h+2)^2)^(h+1) for an absolute constant c. Each residual has a description of O((h+1)log(N+h+2)) bits. Proof: Substituting p for the first t input wires leaves all h gate operations unchanged, so H_p computes q↦H(pq). For the count, each gate chooses one of finitely many types and two sources among at most N+h+2 possibilities; the output chooses one source from that set. Thus the number of descriptions is at most (c(N+h+2)^2)^(h+1). Each description computes at most one residual, which proves the bound. A description can be stored using O((h+1)log(N+h+2)) bits. This is an information bound only: it gives no polynomial-in-(h,n) bound when N=2^n and no real-gate transition circuit for canonical encodings.

statement: statement: Candidate-set transition lemma for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite enumeration C_{n,s} of all Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with a fixed ordering of their 2^n truth-table positions. For a prefix p of length t define V_t(p)={C in C_{n,s}: the first t outputs of C equal p}. Then V_{t+1}(pb)={C in V_t(p): C's output at position t+1 equals b}. Consequently V_t(p) is nonempty iff p is an extendible prefix of a size-at-most-s circuit truth table, and the transition rule recognizes EXT exactly. Proof: By definition, C belongs to V_{t+1}(pb) exactly when its first t outputs equal p and its (t+1)st output equals b. The first condition is C in V_t(p), and the second is the stated filter predicate, proving equality. Nonemptiness is equivalent to existence of a circuit completion, which is the definition of EXT. This is an exact information representation and transition identity; it makes no polynomial bound on representing V_t(p), testing the filter, or implementing transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

label: S0591
statement: statement: Black-box completion-query lower bound. For every k>=0, any deterministic exact algorithm that decides whether an unknown set F subseteq {0,1}^k is nonempty, with access only to membership queries x -> 1[x in F], requires 2^k queries in the worst case. Proof: Run the algorithm against the all-zero oracle (F=empty). If it makes fewer than 2^k queries, choose an unqueried u. The same transcript occurs for F={u}, although the correct outputs differ, contradiction. Querying all strings suffices. Hence for a prefix with k remaining bits, black-box membership access on completed strings alone gives no worst-case exact prefix-extension procedure using fewer than 2^k queries. This is an oracle-model bound only and makes no assertion about real-gate cost when the circuit or structure of F is available.

structure.gap: Whether an EXT transition can be implemented with bounded real-gate cost from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C remains open; the lemma narrows the question by showing complete-input membership queries alone can require 2^(N-|p|) queries in the black-box model.

label: S0594
statement: statement: DNF restriction lemma. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF on N Boolean variables with L total literal occurrences. For any prefix p of length t, the extension predicate E_p(u)=H(pu) has a DNF with at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences. Construct it by deleting every term falsified by a fixed prefix literal, then deleting the remaining fixed prefix literals. Proof: each term on input pu is false if one of its fixed literals is false; otherwise it equals the conjunction of its unfixed literals. Disjoining these term identities gives H(pu)=E_p(u). The construction scans the literals once, so takes O(L+h) inspections and has circuit size O(L+h) with binary fan-in gates. Empty terms and an empty disjunction represent true and false, respectively. This proves a linear-cost prefix transition for explicit DNF membership circuits; it gives no such bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

label: S0595
statement: statement: Existential projection lemma for explicit DNF. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF on N Boolean variables, with L total literal occurrences, and split variables into a prefix a and suffix u. Define E(a)=1 iff there exists u with H(a,u)=1. Construct E by deleting each term whose prefix literals conflict with a, and then deleting every suffix literal from each remaining term. The resulting DNF has at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences. Proof: For fixed a and each term T_j, if a falsifies one of its prefix literals then T_j(a,u)=0 for every u. Otherwise its prefix literals are true, and there exists a suffix u satisfying the remaining suffix literals: each variable occurs with a single polarity within a term, so set those variables accordingly and assign all other suffix variables arbitrarily. Thus this term contributes to E(a) exactly when its prefix literals are all true, which is precisely the projected term after suffix literals are removed. Taking the disjunction proves equality. The construction scans the explicit literals in O(L+h) time and yields a binary fan-in circuit of O(L+h) gates. Scope is existential projection of explicit DNF; no implication for arbitrary circuits.

statement: statement: Repaired existential-projection lemma for explicit DNF. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF over N Boolean variables with L literal occurrences; literals may repeat or include both polarities of a variable. Split variables into prefix a and suffix u. The predicate E(a)=1 iff there exists u with H(a,u)=1 has a DNF with at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences: in each term, delete the term if it contains opposite-polarity literals of any variable or if its prefix literals contradict the fixed a; otherwise remove all suffix literals and retain its prefix literals. Proof: A term with contradictory literals is unsatisfiable. A term whose prefix literals conflict with a is false for every suffix. In every other term, all prefix literals are true under a, and the suffix literals are jointly satisfiable because there is at most one required polarity per suffix variable; choose those required bits and assign remaining bits arbitrarily. Thus the existential projection of each term is exactly its retained prefix conjunction, and existential quantification distributes over finite disjunction. No new terms or literal occurrences are introduced. Scanning the explicit DNF takes O(L+h) time, and the resulting binary-fan-in circuit has O(L+h) gates. For every prefix p of length t, the residual function f_p(u)=H(pu) has a circuit with at most h internal gates. For b in {0,1}, f_{pb}(v)=f_p(bv), so the next residual is obtained by fixing one input of the current residual circuit to b. Proof: Substituting constants for input wires leaves the internal gate list unchanged and computes the restricted function. The identity follows from H(pbv)=H((pb)v). Repeating this argument from H gives the claimed bound for every prefix. Scope: point-membership residual functions only; this does not compute whether a residual has any accepting suffix or give a compact state encoding for arbitrary H.

label: S0598
statement:
statement: Witness-set transition lemma for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite, explicitly indexed family C_{n,s} of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with a fixed output ordering for each truth table. For every length-t prefix p, define W_p={C in C_{n,s}: the first t truth-table bits of C equal p}. Then EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff W_p is nonempty. For t<N and b in {0,1}, W_{pb}={C in W_p: bit_{t+1}(C)=b}; hence W_p is the disjoint union of W_{p0} and W_{p1}. Storing W_p as an explicit bit vector gives an exact deterministic EXT streaming algorithm with at most |C_{n,s}| bits of state; its transition on b scans the indexed circuits and retains exactly those whose (t+1)-st truth-table bit equals b, and final acceptance tests nonemptiness. Proof: By definition, C belongs to W_{pb} exactly when its first t bits equal p and its next bit equals b, which is equivalent to C belonging to W_p and bit_{t+1}(C)=b. Every C in W_p has exactly one next output bit, so the two child sets are disjoint and partition W_p. Nonemptiness of W_p is equivalent to existence of a size-at-most-s circuit with truth-table prefix p, which is the definition of EXT. The explicit transition is correct by the membership equivalence. This is an exact constructive representation, but its state and transition costs are governed by |C_{n,s}|; the lemma makes no polynomial-cost claim and gives no simulation by an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: Finite circuit family with a fixed canonical enumeration and truth-table bit order; exact prefix recognition; no circuit-complexity upper bound beyond explicit witness-set enumeration.

label: S0600
statement:
statement: Explicit candidate-mask update bound for EXT. Fix N≥1 and a finite, explicitly listed family C={C_1,...,C_M} of Boolean circuits, each producing an N-bit string in a fixed order. At position t, store the M-bit mask A_t whose i-th bit is 1 exactly when C_i agrees with the prefix read so far. On reading b∈{0,1}, update each bit by A_{t+1}[i]=A_t[i] ∧ [C_i(t+1)=b]. This update is realizable with at most M fan-in-two AND gates once the position-t output bits C_i(t+1) are available; if those bits are computed from the circuit descriptions during the update, their evaluation cost must be added. The state is exact: A_t is nonzero iff the read prefix is extendible to a member of C, and induction on t proves the invariant. Thus explicit enumeration gives an exact per-bit transition bound of M plus the cost of obtaining the M predicted bits, but does not yield a polynomial-in-s transition bound when M is the number of size-at-most-s circuits.
scope: Finite explicitly enumerated candidate families with deterministic Boolean circuits and a fixed output-bit order; fan-in-two update gates. No claim that M or the total transition cost is polynomial in s, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
proof: Initially set every mask bit to 1, since the empty prefix agrees with every candidate. Suppose the stored invariant holds after t bits. For candidate i, it agrees with the extended prefix ending in b exactly when it agreed with the length-t prefix and its (t+1)-st output bit equals b. This is precisely the stated AND update, so the invariant holds by induction. A nonzero mask is equivalent to at least one listed candidate agreeing with the prefix, which is exactly extendibility within the listed family. Each updated bit is one binary conjunction, giving M fan-in-two gates after the predicted bits are available. If those bits are not supplied, their computation is a separate cost and cannot be omitted.

label: S0604
statement:
statement: Lemma: For any fixed layer t, the EXT_{n,s} transition function T_t: R_t(p) × {0,1} → R_{t+1}(pb) can be realized as a projection of the evaluation of H_C on all suffixes of length N-t-1, but no representation of the residual class as a Boolean circuit of size polynomial in s and log N is known that works for every H_C. In particular, if H_C is an arbitrary circuit deciding membership in Im(Eval), then the map from H_C to a circuit computing T_t may require solving circuit equivalence or existential quantification over circuits of size ≤ s, which is not known to be in P. Therefore, the existence of a uniform poly(s, log N) real-gate transition for EXT from arbitrary H_C remains open, and the candidate-mask bound (S0600) is tight for the explicit enumeration approach.
scope: Arbitrary Boolean circuits H_C deciding EXT_{n,s}; real-gate complexity of the transition function T_t as a function of s and N=2^n. No claim that the transition cannot be done in poly(s) gates, only that no such construction is known and the explicit enumeration gives an exponential upper bound.
proof: The transition T_t on input b maps a residual class R = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pu ∈ Im(Eval)} to R_b = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bv ∈ R}. By S0477, R_b = {v : pbv ∈ Im(Eval)}. This set is exactly the set of suffixes v such that H_C(pbv) = 1. A circuit for T_t must therefore compute, from a description of R and b, a description of R_b. The candidate-mask construction (S0600) does this by explicitly tracking agreement with all M = |Im(Eval) ∩ {0,1}^N| candidates, giving M AND gates. Any representation that avoids enumerating all candidates must implicitly perform existential quantification over circuits of size ≤ s to determine which suffixes remain consistent. Since H_C is an arbitrary decision circuit (not necessarily an evaluation circuit), no poly(s) translation from H_C to a transition circuit is known. This is not a lower bound; it is a precise statement of the current knowledge gap.
