label: S0630
statement: LEMMA (exact residual characterization for a finite fixed-length language). Let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and L=A, viewed as a language over {0,1}. For each prefix p of length k≤N define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-k}: pu∈A}. The minimal deterministic finite automaton for L has exactly 1+Σ_{k=0}^N |{R_p : p∈{0,1}^k, R_p≠∅}| states, where the additional state is the rejecting sink. Proof: For any prefix p, its right language {u:pu∈L} equals R_p, and is empty exactly when p is not a prefix of any word in A. Two prefixes p,p' are equivalent in the Myhill–Nerode relation precisely when their right languages agree. If their lengths differ, their nonempty right languages contain words of different fixed lengths, so they cannot agree; an empty right language is shared by all non-prefixes and is the sink. At a fixed length k, equivalence is exactly equality of the sets R_p. Every nonempty R_p is reached by reading p, and the empty right language is reached by any non-prefix (or, if none exists, the transition from a length-N accepting state on either further bit). Thus the stated count is exact. Consequently, the upper bound in S0520 can be sharpened by replacing min(2^k,|A|) with the exact number of distinct nonempty suffix sets at level k; any two prefixes at that level with different residual sets require distinct automaton states. This is an exact characterization for explicit finite A only and gives no lower bound on the gate cost of an implicit EXT transition or on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (residual derivative gives the exact EXT transition). Let N≥1 and A⊆{0,1}^N. At level k<N, for p∈{0,1}^k define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-k}:pu∈A}. For b∈{0,1}, define D_b(R_p)={u∈{0,1}^{N-k-1}:bu∈R_p}. Then R_{pb}=D_b(R_p). Hence the deterministic prefix automaton transition from residual state R_p on b goes to D_b(R_p) if nonempty, otherwise the rejecting sink. At level N both outgoing transitions go to the sink. Proof: for each u of length N−k−1, u∈R_{pb} iff (pb)u∈A iff p(bu)∈A iff bu∈R_p iff u∈D_b(R_p). Thus equality holds pointwise. In particular, equal residual sets at the same level have equal b-successors. This characterizes the exact information and abstract update for an explicit finite language, but gives neither a compact encoding nor a low-cost update circuit for implicit EXT_{n,s}, and implies nothing about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0632
statement:
statement: LEMMA (exact residual states of a finite word family). Let N be a nonnegative integer and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Let Pref(A) be the set of all prefixes of words in A, including the empty word, and let L=Pref(A). For each k in {0,...,N} and each length-k prefix p occurring in a member of A, define S(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-k}: pu in A}. Then the minimal DFA recognizing L has exactly 1 + sum_{k=0}^N |{S(p): p is a length-k prefix of a member of A}| states. Proof: For any such p, its left quotient p^{-1}L consists exactly of Pref(S(p)): pw is a prefix of some a in A iff w is a prefix of the unique length-(N-k) suffix u with pu=a. At a fixed k, the words of maximum length N-k in Pref(S(p)) are exactly S(p), so different S(p) yield different quotients. For nonempty S(p), Pref(S(p)) has maximum word length N-k; hence quotients from different depths k are distinct. Every prefix in L has one of these quotients, while any non-prefix has empty quotient and all such prefixes share the rejecting sink. By Myhill-Nerode, the stated count is exact. This is a theorem about explicitly specified finite word families; it makes no assertion about compact transition circuits for implicitly represented families.
derivation: The quotient identity follows from the definition of prefix closure. Recovering the suffix set from maximum-length words proves injectivity within a level; maximum accepted continuation length distinguishes levels. The only quotient outside those represented by prefixes is the empty quotient, giving one sink.
scope: All finite nonempty A subset {0,1}^N; exact DFA state count for Pref(A), no circuit complexity or PNP transfer claim.

label: S0633
statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual languages are necessary streaming state information). Let L be any language of finite binary strings, and let a deterministic one-pass streaming machine decide, after each prefix p, whether p is a prefix of some word in L. Define R_p={z : pz is in L}. If two prefixes p,q lead the machine to the same internal state, then R_p=R_q. Consequently the machine has at least as many reachable states as there are distinct residual languages R_p. Proof: for every suffix z, deterministic processing from the same state on z has the same final outcome. The machine accepts pz exactly when z∈R_p, and accepts qz exactly when z∈R_q. Equality of states therefore implies, for every z, z∈R_p iff z∈R_q, hence R_p=R_q. Contrapositively, distinct residuals require distinct states. This is a necessary-information bound; it makes no gate-cost claim and does not imply that an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit exposes or updates the residuals efficiently.
derivation: The state-equality implication follows by applying the same continuation z to equal deterministic states and using exact correctness on both completed streams.

label: S0635
statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual information for prefix extendibility). Let L⊆{0,1}* and P=Pref(L)={p: there exists w with pw∈L}. Suppose a deterministic streaming machine, after reading each string p, outputs 1 exactly when p∈P. For each p define R_p^P={z∈{0,1}*: pz∈P}. If p and q lead to the same machine state, then R_p^P=R_q^P. Proof: fix any z. Starting from the equal states after p and q, deterministic processing of the same continuation z ends in the same state and hence gives the same output. By correctness, that output is 1 exactly when pz∈P, and also exactly when qz∈P. Thus pz∈P iff qz∈P for every z, so the residual sets are equal. Consequently distinct residuals of Pref(L) require distinct reachable states. This is an information requirement only; it gives no gate-cost bound for transitions.
derivation: Corrected the observable language from L to its prefix closure Pref(L), because EXT outputs whether a prefix has some completion rather than whether a specified continuation completes it.

label: S0636
statement: statement: LEMMA (candidate-set to EXT-residual map). Fix a finite indexed family F of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, and stream each function's truth table in the same fixed input order. For a prefix p of length k, let L_p be the functions agreeing with p on the first k inputs, and let R_p be the set of their remaining truth-table suffixes. Then R_p is exactly the EXT continuation residual after p. For the next truth-table position i_k and bit b, L_{pb}={f in L_p:f(i_k)=b}, and R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}. Thus candidate sets are exact sufficient states, while the minimal residual states identify candidate sets precisely when they induce the same suffix set. Proof: A suffix z completes p to a prefix of a family truth table exactly when some function in L_p has remaining suffix z, which is the definition of R_p. A function remains live after reading b exactly when it was live before and its value at i_k equals b. A suffix z completes pb exactly when bz completes p, giving the residual identity. Therefore continuation behavior depends only on R_p; distinct candidate sets need not be distinct states if their suffix sets agree.

label: S0637
statement: statement: LEMMA (reachable candidate sets are exactly EXT residuals for duplicate-free functions). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with truth tables read in a fixed order. For every prefix p of length k, let L_p={f∈F: f agrees with p on the first k inputs}, and let R_p={z∈{0,1}^{2^n-k}: pz is a prefix of the truth table of some f∈F}. Then the map f↦the remaining truth-table suffix of f is a bijection from L_p to R_p. In particular |L_p|=|R_p|, and two reachable prefixes p,q have the same live-function set if and only if their residual suffix sets (viewed at their respective stream positions) agree after identifying the remaining coordinates. Proof: If f∈L_p, its remaining suffix z satisfies that pz is the full truth table of f, so z∈R_p. Conversely, if z∈R_p, by definition some f∈F has truth table beginning pz, and so f∈L_p maps to z. For injectivity, if f,g∈L_p map to the same z, then both truth tables consist of the same length-k prefix p followed by z; hence their truth tables agree at all 2^n inputs, so f=g, using extensional equality of Boolean functions. This gives a canonical identification of reachable candidate sets with residual sets; it does not bound the gate cost of computing the update for the implicit family of all size-s circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (exact fixed-position residual count). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on a finite domain of size N, with truth-table entries streamed in a fixed order. Fix k with 0≤k≤N. Proof: Define φ_k(f) to be the suffix of f after its first k entries. On F, φ_k is injective: if φ_k(f)=φ_k(g) and both match the same prefix p, then f and g agree on the first k entries (both equal p) and on the remaining entries (their suffixes agree), hence f=g. For every p, R_p=φ_k(L_p). Thus if L_p=L_q, then R_p=R_q. Therefore the two collections of sets have the same number of distinct members. This is an exact state-count identity at one fixed stream position; it gives no transition-circuit bound for an implicit circuit family.

label: S0643
statement: LEMMA (done-bit repair for an explicitly listed finite truth-table family). Let C_1,...,C_M be explicitly listed Boolean circuits on n input bits with fan-in-two gate counts s_1,...,s_M, M>=1, and let N=2^n. A deterministic streaming recognizer for Pref({TT(C_j):1<=j<=M}) has state (i,a_1,...,a_M,d), where i is an n-bit address, a_j records agreement with candidate j, and d is a done bit. It uses O(n+M+sum_j s_j) fan-in-two gates per input-bit update. Initially i=0, every a_j=1, d=0. While d=0, on bit b set a_j to a_j AND [C_j(i)=b]. If i=N-1, set d=1 and hold i; otherwise increment i. When d=1, any further input clears every a_j and leaves d=1. Accept iff some a_j=1. Proof: Before each of the first N updates, induction gives that i is the next truth-table address and a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the prefix already read. The update checks the next bit and preserves this invariant; at the final address it sets d, and otherwise advances i. Hence a prefix of length at most N is accepted exactly when some listed truth table extends it. Once d=1, any extra bit clears the mask permanently, so all longer strings reject. Evaluating the listed circuits costs sum_j s_j gates; comparisons and mask updates cost O(M), and address increment plus terminal detection cost O(n). This applies only to an explicitly listed family and gives no compact transition bound for minimized EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0646
statement: LEMMA (exact suffix-expansion circuit for EXT transitions). Let N>=1, let C be a Boolean circuit of size L on N inputs, and let 0<=t<N and b in {0,1}. Define T_{t,b}(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} such that C(p||b||z)=1, for p in {0,1}^t. Then T_{t,b} has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^{N-t-1}(L+1)-1, assuming input fixing and wiring are free. Proof: For each suffix z, make one copy of C, wire p||b to its first t+1 inputs, and fix the remaining inputs to z. OR the 2^{N-t-1} outputs with a binary tree, requiring 2^{N-t-1}-1 gates. The result is 1 exactly when some completion is accepted by C. When C recognizes the size-at-most-s truth tables, this computes the EXT next-bit predicate. This is an exact, generally exponential upper bound; it provides neither a compact encoding of all residual states nor a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP circuits. Barrier diagnostic: the construction relativizes (copies and OR only); it is not a natural-proofs lower-bound argument; Boolean wiring raises no algebrization issue; locality is not asserted. It passes none of the circumvention tests as a compression: it retains suffix enumeration and supplies no re-coding bound, adaptive rule, new resource, or transfer to arbitrary MCSP circuits.

label: S0647
statement: LEMMA (two-output suffix-expansion bound). Let C:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size L, and let p be a fixed prefix of length t<N. For b in {0,1}, define T_b(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with C(p||b||z)=1. The pair (T_0(p),T_1(p)) is computable by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^{N-t}(L+1)-2 gates, using independent copies of C and fixed-input wiring. Proof: Let k=2^{N-t-1}. For each b and each suffix z, use a copy of C with p||b wired to its fixed inputs; this uses at most 2kL gates total. For each b, OR its k outputs with a binary tree using k-1 gates; total OR cost is 2(k-1). Thus the total is 2k(L+1)-2=2^{N-t}(L+1)-2. Each output equals the existential disjunction over precisely the suffixes in its branch, so it computes T_b(p).

statement: LEMMA (block transition composition for an explicitly represented candidate family). Let D={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on a finite domain X, and let a_0,...,a_{N-1} be a fixed ordering of X. Suppose u∈{0,1}^M marks the candidates consistent with the truth-table prefix before position t. For a block w=(w_0,...,w_{d-1}), define F_{t,w}(j)=1 iff C_j(a_{t+r})=w_r for every 0≤r<d. The updated mask is u'=u∧F_{t,w}, coordinatewise. For consecutive blocks w,v, F_{t,wv}=F_{t,w}∧F_{t+d,v}; thus block updates compose associatively. If each C_j is given by a fan-in-two circuit of at most s gates, a direct implementation uses O(Md(s+1)) gates, plus input-address handling.
derivation: Candidate j survives the extended prefix exactly when it survived the old prefix and agrees at every new block position. This is the stated coordinatewise conjunction. Splitting the conjunction for wv at the boundary between w and v proves the composition identity; associativity of conjunction makes the result independent of parenthesization. For the gate bound, evaluate each C_j at each of the d fixed points, compare with the corresponding fixed bit, AND the d comparisons, then AND with u_j. This uses O(d(s+1)) gates per candidate, hence O(Md(s+1)) total, plus address handling. This result is limited to explicitly represented families; it gives no compact update for the full size-s circuit family, no transition bound through H_C, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP deciders.

label: S0649
statement: statement: LEMMA (prefix projection of a deterministic circuit’s trace relation). Let C:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be a Boolean circuit with gates ordered topologically as g_1,...,g_m, and let T_i(x,y_{<i}) be the Boolean function computed at gate i from input x and earlier gate values. Define H_C(x,y)=T_out(x,y) AND ∧_{i=1}^m (y_i ↔ T_i(x,y_{<i})), where T_out is the circuit’s output wire interpreted using x and y. For every fixed x there is exactly one y with all trace equations true, namely the vector of gate values obtained by evaluating C on x. Consequently, for every prefix p of length t≤N, EXT_C(p):=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^{N−t} satisfies C(pz)=1 is equivalent to ∃z∈{0,1}^{N−t}∃y∈{0,1}^m H_C(pz,y)=1. Proof: Induct on i. Once x and y_1,...,y_{i−1} are fixed, the i-th equation forces y_i to the unique value T_i(x,y_{<i}); hence the equations have exactly one solution y, and that solution is the actual gate-evaluation trace. On this unique trace, T_out equals C(x), so H_C(x,y)=1 exactly when C(x)=1. Existentially quantifying the suffix z therefore yields the stated prefix equivalence.

statement: statement: LEMMA (precomputed candidate-mask update). Let D={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with fixed input order a_0,...,a_{N-1}, N=2^n. Define u_j=1 iff C_j agrees with the observed prefix p_0,...,p_{t-1}. If v_t=(C_1(a_t),...,C_M(a_t)) is available as fixed circuit constants, then after observing b the exact updated mask is u'_j=u_j AND [v_{t,j}=b] for j=1,...,M. It takes at most M+1 fan-in-two gates (one shared NOT of b, then one AND per candidate). Direct preprocessing of all N columns by evaluating M circuits of at most s gates costs O(MN(s+n)) Boolean operations and stores MN bits. Proof: Since v_{t,j} is a fixed bit, [v_{t,j}=b] is b when v_{t,j}=1 and NOT b otherwise. Thus each updated bit is computed with one AND after the shared complement is formed. It is 1 exactly when candidate j matched all earlier bits and matches the new bit. Induction on t proves the mask is exactly the consistent candidate set. The result separates preprocessing/storage from per-symbol transition cost and is restricted to an explicit finite family.

statement: LEMMA (exact suffix-projection transition for a decision circuit). Let N≥1 and let H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size h. For every prefix p∈{0,1}^t with 0≤t<N, define E_H(p)=1 iff there exists z∈{0,1}^{N-t} such that H(pz)=1. Then for b∈{0,1}, E_H(pb)= OR_{z∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}} H(pb z). This transition predicate has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^{N-t-1}h + (2^{N-t-1}-1), up to O(N) input wiring per copy if input wiring is charged as gates. Proof: By definition, E_H(pb)=1 iff there exists a suffix w of length N-t-1 with H(pbw)=1, which is exactly the displayed disjunction. Construct one copy of H for each such w, hardwire the first t+1 inputs to pb and the remaining inputs to w, and combine their outputs by a binary OR tree. statement:
statement: LEMMA (polynomial real-gate suffix projection for affine predicates). Let A be an r×N matrix over GF(2), c∈GF(2)^r, and H(x)=1 iff Ax=c. Fix a cut t<N and write A=(A_<t | D), where D consists of columns t,...,N−1. Let U be an r×k matrix whose columns form a basis of ker(D^T). For p∈{0,1}^t, define E_H(p)=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^{N−t} satisfies H(pz). Then E_H(p)=1 iff U^T(c+A_<t p)=0. In particular, the next-bit transition E_H(pb) is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(kr) gates (with A,c,U hardwired), hence O(r²) gates, and the formula is exact. Proof: H(pz) holds exactly when Dz=c+A_<t p, since subtraction equals addition over GF(2). A vector y lies in im(D) iff it is orthogonal to ker(D^T): inclusion follows from λ^T Dz=(D^Tλ)^Tz=0; equality follows from rank-nullity, since im(D) has dimension rank(D), while ker(D^T)^⊥ also has dimension r−dim ker(D^T)=rank(D). Thus a completion exists iff U^T(c+A_<t p)=0. For pb, substitute p concatenated with b in this identity. Each of the k output parities is a dot product of a fixed row of U^T A_<t and p plus a fixed constant and a fixed coefficient times b. A parity of at most r+1 bits uses O(r) fan-in-two XOR gates, each XOR implementable with three AND/OR/NOT gates; combine the k parity outputs by an AND tree using at most k−1 gates. This is O(kr) gates and k≤r, giving O(r²). All preprocessing (finding U) is outside the per-transition circuit and is computable by Gaussian elimination in polynomial time. This proves a real-gate transition bound for affine predicates only; it does not establish such a bound for EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (column-factored candidate-mask transition). Let D=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on a finite domain X, let a_0,...,a_{N-1} be a fixed input order, and define the M-bit consistency state u_j(p)=1 iff C_j(a_i)=p_i for all i<t, for a prefix p of length t. Define the column v_t∈{0,1}^M by (v_t)_j=C_j(a_t). For next bit b, the unique correct updated mask is u'_j=u_j AND NOT((v_t)_j XOR b). Given v_t, all M output bits are computed with O(M) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates; the column itself can be computed by evaluating all listed circuits in O(M(s+n)) gates when each C_j has at most s fan-in-two gates and inputs are explicitly supplied. Thus transition cost separates into an O(M) mask-update circuit and an O(M(s+n)) column-generation circuit; correctness holds for every prefix by induction. Proof: For each j, consistency with the extended prefix is equivalent to consistency with p and agreement C_j(a_t)=b. This is exactly u_j AND NOT((v_t)_j XOR b). The Boolean expression costs a constant number of gates per coordinate, and evaluating each listed circuit at a_t costs at most s gates plus input handling; summing gives the stated bounds. This lemma is limited to the explicit family representation and yields no transition bound for succinct EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0672
statement: statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and fix t. Write R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. For any deterministic exact one-pass left-to-right streaming machine deciding membership in F, distinct residuals R_t(p) correspond to distinct machine states after t bits. Hence if there are d distinct residuals at level t, at least d states and ceil(log2 d) bits of state are necessary. Proof: if R_t(p) and R_t(p') differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pz,p'z belongs to F. If p and p' led to the same machine state, determinism on the identical remaining suffix z would force the same output, contradicting exact membership. Scope: state information only; no gate-transition-cost or arbitrary-MCSP-circuit simulation claim.

statement: RESIDUAL SECTION IDENTITY. For every finite F ⊆ {0,1}^N, every 0 ≤ t < N, prefix p ∈ {0,1}^t, and bit b ∈ {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb) = {u : bu ∈ R_t(p)}, where R_t(p) = {z : pz ∈ F}. Moreover R_t(p) is the disjoint union over b of {bu : u ∈ R_{t+1}(pb)}.
proof: For any suffix u of length N−t−1, u ∈ R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu ∈ F, which by definition holds iff bu ∈ R_t(p). Every suffix z of length N−t has a unique decomposition z=bu, so the two first-bit sections are disjoint and their union is R_t(p).

label: S0675
statement: statement: BATCHED EXPLICIT-FAMILY TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F be an explicitly listed set of M distinct words in {0,1}^N, represented by their M×N bit table. Given a current prefix p of length t and its candidate index set L(p)={i: f_i has prefix p}, the next-bit candidate sets L_b(p)={i in L(p): f_i[t+1]=b}, b∈{0,1}, are computed by one scan of the table column t+1 restricted to L(p), using at most M Boolean tests and O(M) workspace. For a block u of r bits, the candidate set is obtained in at most Mr Boolean tests. These candidate sets are exact sufficient statistics: for every suffix z of length N-t-1, p b z belongs to the prefix language of F iff some i∈L_b(p) has suffix z after position t+1. Proof: membership in L_b is precisely agreement with p followed by b; each listed word has a unique remaining suffix, so existential membership is equivalent to the stated condition. Thus explicit enumeration gives an exact update bound linear in M per bit, but this bound depends on the explicit table and does not transfer to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0676
statement: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY MASK TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a fixed list of distinct words in {0,1}^N. At cut t, encode the candidates matching prefix p by the mask L(p) in {0,1}^M, where L_i(p)=1 iff f_i[1..t]=p. For each b in {0,1}, define the hardwired mask C_b by (C_b)_i=1 iff f_i[t+1]=b. Then L(pb)=L(p) AND C_b, coordinatewise. The two child masks can be computed with M fan-in-two AND gates total per child, or with zero nonconstant gates if the list-dependent masks are applied as fixed coordinate selection in the representation. The update uses M state bits. For a block u of r bits, define C_u by (C_u)_i=1 iff f_i[t+1..t+r]=u; then L(pu)=L(p) AND C_u, again coordinatewise, for each u. Proof: For each index i, L_i(pb)=1 exactly when f_i has prefix p and its next bit is b. This is equivalent to L_i(p)=1 and (C_b)_i=1, which is the i-th coordinate of the claimed intersection. The block statement follows by the same equivalence for the next r positions. Thus the mask is an exact sufficient state for an explicitly listed family, with O(M) bits and O(M) Boolean update gates per requested child; it gives no polynomial-in-succinct-description bound when M is exponential in that description.

statement: COFACTOR REPRESENTATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N -> {0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. statement:
statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound for exact prefix streaming. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N, and at depth t let R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in L} for each p in {0,1}^t. Any deterministic streaming machine that reads the N bits in order and correctly decides membership in L must be in different states after prefixes p and q whenever R_p != R_q. Proof: Since R_p and R_q are unequal sets, their symmetric difference is nonempty; choose u in it. Then exactly one of pu, qu belongs to L. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism gives the same state after reading the common suffix u, and hence the same final answer, contradicting correctness. Conversely, storing R_p itself as the state is sufficient: upon reading b, replace R_p by R_{pb}={v: bv in R_p}, and accept at depth N exactly when the residual contains the empty string. Therefore the minimum number of states at depth t equals the number of distinct residual languages {R_p}; any exact streaming algorithm needs at least ceil(log2 D_t) bits there, and this residual-state machine attains that bound. Applied to EXT_{n,s}, the relevant residual is the set of suffixes that complete the prefix to a truth table realizable by a size-s circuit. This characterizes necessary information, but gives no bound on the real-gate cost of computing the update from H_C.
scope: All deterministic exact one-pass streaming algorithms for a fixed language L subset {0,1}^N with fixed input order; depth-wise state count. It does not address randomized or multi-pass streaming, nor simulate transitions from a circuit H_C.
proof: Included in the statement; the lower bound follows by choosing a distinguishing suffix in the symmetric difference, and the matching construction stores the residual set and updates it by left-cofactoring on the next bit.

statement:
statement: Distinct-cofactor projection lemma. Let H(a,z) be a Boolean function computed by a fan-in-two circuit with h internal gates, where z ranges over {0,1}^r and a denotes the remaining inputs. Let k=|{H(·,w):w∈{0,1}^r}|, counting distinct Boolean functions of a. Then E(a)=1 iff there exists z H(a,z)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit of at most kh+(k−1) gates. Proof: choose one representative w_j from each of the k equivalence classes of suffix assignments under H(·,w)=H(·,w_j). Substituting w_j for z in H gives a circuit H_j on a of at most h gates. By definition E(a)=OR over all suffix assignments w of H(a,w), and replacing each assignment by its representative preserves the OR because equivalent cofactors agree pointwise. A binary OR tree over the k outputs uses k−1 gates. Total at most kh+k−1. For r=0, k=1 and the bound is h. The lemma is an existential circuit-size bound; finding representatives or testing cofactor equivalence may itself be expensive, so it is not an efficient transition algorithm.
scope: All fan-in-two Boolean circuits H(a,z), all r≥0; k counts exact functional equality over all assignments a. No poly(s,log N) transition bound follows unless k and representative-construction costs are separately controlled.

statement:
statement: Suffix-projection transition bound. Let H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two circuit with h gates. For each k<N and prefix p∈{0,1}^k, define E_{p,b}=1 iff some y∈{0,1}^{N-k-1} satisfies H(pby)=1. Then E_{p,b} is computed by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^{N-k-1}h+(2^{N-k-1}-1) gates. Proof: for every suffix y of length N-k-1, substitute the constants p,b,y into H, obtaining a circuit on no inputs with at most h gates whose output is H(pby). OR these 2^{N-k-1} outputs with a binary tree using 2^{N-k-1}-1 gates. The resulting output is 1 exactly when at least one suffix makes H(pby)=1. This holds also when N-k-1=0, where there is one cofactor and no OR gates.
scope: All N≥1, k<N, prefixes p and bits b, and all fan-in-two Boolean circuits H on N inputs. This bounds the real-gate cost of the explicit projection for each fixed p,b; it gives no uniform compact state encoding or polynomial-in-s transition bound.

statement: statement: LEMMA (explicit-list block update). Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be listed Boolean circuits on an ordered N-point domain, of sizes s_j. label: S0729
statement:
statement: REPAIRED AFFINE SUFFIX-PROJECTION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let A be an r by N matrix over GF(2), c in GF(2)^r, and H(x)=1 iff Ax=c. Fix 0<=t<N, write A=(A_<t | a_t | D_+), and let V have columns forming a basis of ker(D_+^T). For p in {0,1}^t and b in {0,1}, E_H(pb)=1 iff V^T(c+A_<t p+b a_t)=0. This predicate has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(r(t+1)) gates when A,c,V are hardwired. Proof: A completion z after pb exists exactly when D_+z=c+A_<t p+b a_t. A vector y is in im(D_+) iff it is orthogonal to ker(D_+^T): inclusion follows from lambda^T D_+z=0 for every lambda in that kernel; equality follows by rank-nullity, since both spaces have dimension rank(D_+). Thus completion is equivalent to V^T y=0. There are at most r parity equations, each on at most t+1 variable bits, implementable with O(t+1) fan-in-two Boolean gates using XOR and its constant-size Boolean implementation. An AND tree combines the equations, giving O(r(t+1)) gates. Gaussian elimination finds V in polynomial time. This repairs the gate estimate by including dependence on all prefix bits; it proves no transition bound for arbitrary EXT or MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Use the exact solvability criterion y in im(D_+) iff V^T y=0, then compute each resulting parity over the t prefix bits and next bit b and conjoin the at most r equations.

label: S0731
statement:
statement: FULL-RESIDUAL-TABLE UPDATE LEMMA. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. Encode the residual R_t(p) after prefix p by the vector B_p indexed by z in {0,1}^{N-t}, with B_p[z]=1 iff pz is in F. After reading b in {0,1}, the exact next residual encoding satisfies B_{pb}[u]=B_p[b||u] for every u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}. As a fan-in-two Boolean circuit taking B_p and b as inputs and outputting all bits of B_{pb}, this update has O(2^{N-t-1}) gates, using one constant-size mux per output bit; for fixed b, it is a wire projection. Proof: For each suffix u, B_{pb}[u]=1 iff pbu is in F, which by definition is equivalent to B_p[b||u]=1. The indexing map u -> b||u is injective and selects exactly one half of the coordinates. A mux per coordinate selects the b-indexed half when b is an input; for fixed b each output is a copy of one input coordinate. The statement is an exact cost bound for the full residual truth-table representation only, and says nothing about compressed state encodings or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: The residual definition gives the coordinate identity directly; implement each coordinate selection with a two-input mux.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL WIDTH RECURRENCE. For F subset {0,1}^N, let d_t count distinct R_t(p)={z:pz in F} over prefixes p of length t. For 0<=t<N, d_t<=d_{t+1}^2 and d_{t+1}<=2d_t. Proof: Each level-t residual R has sections R_b={u:bu in R}, which are level-(t+1) residuals. The pair (R_0,R_1) determines R, so d_t<=d_{t+1}^2. Every level-(t+1) residual is a section of its parent, which has two sections, so d_{t+1}<=2d_t. The statement concerns residual counts only and implies no transition circuit-cost bound under arbitrary encodings.
derivation: A residual is uniquely determined by its two first-bit sections, and every child residual is a section of a parent.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL STRUCTURE OF EXT_{n,s}. Let N = 2^n. For the language EXT_{n,s} ⊆ {0,1}^N where EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff ∃ circuit C of size ≤ s with truth table starting with p, the residual sets R_t(p) = {z ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pz ∈ EXT_{n,s}} have the property that for each t, the equivalence relation p ~ q iff R_t(p) = R_t(q) has at most 2^{O(s log(n+s))} classes. Moreover, the transition structure (R_t(p) → (R_{t+1}(p0), R_{t+1}(p1))) forms a deterministic automaton isomorphic to the prefix trie of Im(Eval) restricted to prefixes of length t. Proof: By MMW19 Thm 1.2, the prefix automaton of EXT_{n,s} has O(log N + s log(n+s))-bit states. The residual equivalence classes correspond exactly to states of the minimal deterministic automaton. The transition structure is exactly the trie transition. Any deterministic streaming algorithm deciding EXT_{n,s} must distinguish these equivalence classes (S0672), so needs at least this many states.
derivation: Direct from MMW19 Thm 1.2 (prefix automaton construction) and the residual distinguishability lower bound (S0672). The residual classes are the Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes for EXT_{n,s}.

label: S0736
statement:
statement: LEMMA (compiled explicit-list prefix recognizer). Let A=(a_1,...,a_M) be a listed multiset of N-bit strings. There is a deterministic prefix recognizer with M state bits q_j, initialized to 1, updated on input bit b at position i by q'_j=q_j AND [a_j(i)=b], and accepting exactly when OR_j q_j=1. Each update uses at most M two-input AND gates when the constants are fixed, and acceptance uses at most max(M-1,0) two-input OR gates. Compiling all N position-specific update circuits from A takes O(MN) constant occurrences and O(MN) gates in total. The procedure is exact even with repeated candidates and for M=0, when it rejects every prefix.
derivation: For each j, induction on prefix length gives q_j=1 iff the read prefix equals the corresponding prefix of a_j: it holds initially, and the update retains q_j exactly when the next listed bit equals the read bit. Thus OR_j q_j is true precisely when at least one listed string extends the read prefix. Each coordinate update is one AND with a fixed Boolean constant, and there are M coordinates at each of N positions, yielding the stated per-position and total costs. For M=0 the OR is false and the empty vector remains empty.
scope: Explicit list A is the input representation; state size is M bits and transition-table construction is O(MN). This gives no polynomial bound when M is exponential, and does not simulate an arbitrary decision circuit for MCSP.

label: S0741
statement:
statement: LAYERED RESIDUAL MINIMALITY LEMMA. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t in {0,...,N}, define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for p in {0,1}^t, and let r_t be the number of distinct sets among {R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}. In any deterministic length-N streaming recognizer whose transition at position i may depend on i, distinct residual sets at depth t must reach distinct states; conversely, the recognizer whose depth-t states are exactly the distinct residual languages recognizes L. Hence the minimum number of states required at depth t is exactly r_t, and the minimum total number of state labels across the layered machine is sum_t r_t.
derivation: Necessity: if two prefixes p,p' at depth t reach the same state, determinism gives the same outcome for every common suffix z, so correctness implies pz∈L iff p'z∈L for every z and R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Sufficiency: use the current residual R_t(p) as the state. On bit b, transition to its b-section, which equals R_{t+1}(pb); this is well-defined because equal residuals have equal b-sections. At depth N accept exactly when the residual contains the empty string. Thus exactly r_t states are necessary and sufficient at each layer, and the layered count is their sum.
scope: Finite Boolean language L and fixed length N; deterministic streaming recognizers with position-dependent transitions. This characterizes information/state complexity only; it gives no gate bound for computing transitions from a succinct description such as H_C and no lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. Diagnostic barriers: the identity relativizes; no natural, algebrizing, or localizing lower-bound method is asserted. Circumvention tests are inapplicable because this is not a P!=NP argument.

statement: statement: EXISTENTIAL PREFIX COFACTOR LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N × {0,1}^r→{0,1} be any Boolean relation and define L(x)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. For every prefix p of length t, define R_p(z)=1 iff there exists w H(pz,w)=1, where z has length N−t. Then for each next bit b, R_{pb}(z')=R_p(bz') for every z'∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}. If H is represented by a fan-in-two circuit of h gates, a circuit for (z',w)↦H(pb z',w) uses at most h gates by input substitution, and the projected residual is still exactly its existential projection over the same r witness bits. Proof: substitute the fixed prefix bits in H; for every z', R_{pb}(z')=1 iff ∃w H(pb z',w)=1 iff ∃w H(p(bz'),w)=1 iff R_p(bz')=1. Input substitution adds no gates and does not alter the witness domain. Thus cofactoring the witness relation is cheap and exact; eliminating/projecting the witness while retaining a Boolean circuit for R_p is a separate complexity question.

label: S0743
statement: statement: EXPLICIT WITNESS-ELIMINATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, with constants and input wiring free. Define G(x)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r such that H(x,w)=1. Then G has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)−1 gates. For every prefix p, its cofactor G_p(z)=G(pz) has a circuit within the same bound, and each next cofactor G_{pb} is obtained from G_p by fixing one input, adding no gates. Proof: For each w∈{0,1}^r, take a copy of H and substitute the constants w into its witness inputs. Each copy computes x↦H(x,w) with at most h gates. Combine the 2^r output bits by a binary OR tree, using 2^r−1 OR gates. The resulting circuit computes G and has at most 2^r h+(2^r−1)=2^r(h+1)−1 gates. Substituting the prefix constants p in this circuit cannot increase its gate count. Substituting the next input b into that cofactor likewise cannot increase its gate count and computes G_{pb}. This is an explicit witness-elimination construction and exact cost bound; it does not establish a matching lower bound or a polynomial bound in r.

statement:
statement: WITNESS-RELATION COFACTOR LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^{N}×{0,1}^{r}->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, and let L={x∈{0,1}^N: ∃w∈{0,1}^r H(x,w)=1}. For a prefix p∈{0,1}^t define H_p(z,w)=H(pz,w) and L_p={z:∃w H_p(z,w)=1}. For b∈{0,1}, H_{pb} is obtained from H_p by fixing its first z-input to b, uses at most h gates, and L_{pb}={v:∃w H_{pb}(v,w)=1}={v:bv∈L_p}. Thus the exact projected residual can be represented by a cofactored h-gate witness relation at every prefix; this is a representation/update lemma, not an algorithm for canonicalizing or evaluating the projection.
proof: Fix p and b. The circuit H_{pb}(v,w)=H(pbv,w) is obtained from H by substituting constants for the |p|+1 fixed x-coordinates, leaving v and w as the remaining inputs. Substitution changes no gate count: retain each original gate and replace its input wires by constants or the appropriate remaining inputs (constant propagation can only reduce the count). Hence H_{pb} has at most h gates. For every suffix v, membership in L_{pb} means ∃w H(pbv,w)=1. By the definition of L_p, this is equivalent to bv∈L_p. This proves both equalities, with the same witness domain {0,1}^r and without eliminating or modifying witness variables.

statement:
statement: LITERAL-PREFIX RELATION TRANSITION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be any Boolean circuit with h gates, and let L(x)=1 iff ∃w∈{0,1}^r H(x,w)=1. Represent the residual after prefix p∈{0,1}^t by the pair (H,p), with residual L_p(z)=1 iff ∃w H(pz,w)=1. On reading b∈{0,1}, the transition (H,p)↦(H,pb) is exact, uses zero additional Boolean gates in the represented circuit, and stores t+1 prefix bits. The relation circuit remains h gates; this representation is not asserted to be compact or canonical.
proof: Fix any prefix p of length t and bit b. The residual represented after the transition is L_{pb}(v)=1 iff ∃w H(pbv,w)=1. By definition, L_p(bv)=1 iff ∃w H(pbv,w)=1, so L_{pb}(v)=L_p(bv) for every suffix v. Thus the update is exact. The transition changes only the stored binary string p to pb; it neither alters nor extends H, so the circuit gate count remains h and the additional gate cost is zero. statement: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At level t let the distinct residuals be R_1,...,R_d and at level t+1 let them be U_1,...,U_e. Encode a valid current residual R_i by the one-hot vector q in {0,1}^d. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit that, given q and next bit b, outputs the one-hot encoding of the residual after appending b, using at most O(d+e) gates. Proof: For each i and b, the child R_i^b={u:bu in R_i} is one of the e level-(t+1) residuals; let j(i,b) denote its index. Compute a_i0=q_i AND NOT b and a_i1=q_i AND b for each i. For each j output q'_j as the OR of all a_ib with j(i,b)=j (empty OR is constant 0). The children of each parent are defined by residual sections, so for any valid one-hot q selecting i, exactly a_i,b is 1, at j(i,b), and every other output is 0. There are 2d conjunction terms and 2d total incidences across the output ORs; implementing each OR by a binary tree costs at most 2d gates, hence O(d+e) including input negation/constants. This establishes a real fan-in-two gate bound for canonical one-hot states, not for arbitrary compressed encodings or H_C transitions.

label: S0753
statement: statement: FINITE-IMAGE RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N with |F|=M, and for 0<=t<=N let R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} for p in {0,1}^t. The number d_t of distinct sets R_t(p) is at most M+1, and the number of distinct pairs (t,R_t(p)) over all levels is at most (N+1)(M+1). Proof: At fixed t, every nonempty residual R_t(p) is witnessed by an element y in F extending p. Distinct prefixes of length t have disjoint extension sets. Distinct residuals cannot arise from the same prefix, so choosing one prefix and one witness for each distinct nonempty residual yields distinct witnesses in F. Thus there are at most M nonempty residuals. The empty residual contributes at most one more. Summing over N+1 levels gives (N+1)(M+1) level-tagged states. Hence the layered exact residual automaton for F has an encoding using ceil(log2((N+1)(M+1))) bits. This is a state-count bound only; it gives no bound on Boolean circuit cost of computing transitions from an arbitrary representation.

label: S0754
statement: statement: EXPLICIT-LIST RESIDUAL LOOKUP BOUND. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on an ordered N-point domain, each with a representation allowing evaluation cost at most s_j gates per point. For each prefix p of length t, let R_t(p) be its exact residual set of completions, and assign a distinct binary code to each residual at each level. The transition (code(R_t(p)),b) -> code(R_{t+1}(pb)) can be implemented by a nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(M log(M+1)) gates per level, after the family’s evaluations and transition table have been computed. Proof: For each listed f_j, store a bit a_j indicating whether f_j agrees with p on the first t points. The next agreement vector has coordinates a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. Each predicate [f_j(t)=b] is a constant in the level-specific transition circuit because the family and t are fixed. Thus the agreement-vector update uses O(M) gates. Encode the residual by its agreement vector (or map each distinct vector to a residual code); translating between a packed binary residual code and the M-bit agreement vector by arbitrary lookup tables costs O(M log(M+1)) gates using one-hot equality tests and OR trees. The transition table can be constructed from the explicit list in O(sum_j N s_j + MN) evaluation and bookkeeping time. This result concerns explicit lists and nonuniform level-specific circuits only; it gives no bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or implicit circuit families.

statement: statement: EXPLICIT-LIST SURVIVOR-STATE UPDATE. Let f_1,...,f_M be explicitly represented Boolean strings of length N. At level t encode prefix p by a in {0,1}^M, where a_j=1 exactly when f_j agrees with p on its first t coordinates. For next bit b, set a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. Then a' encodes exactly the strings agreeing with pb. The level-t transition uses at most 2M fan-in-two gates because each bracket is a hardwired constant. Initially a=1^M; induction on t proves the invariant. The circuit is constructible in O(MN) time by scanning the explicit strings. This applies only to the explicit survivor-vector representation, not packed residual codes, implicit families, or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0757
statement:
statement: WITNESS-VERIFICATION FORM OF EXT TRANSITIONS. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size s on N-bit strings, let p be a prefix of length t<N, and let b in {0,1}. Define EXT_C(pb)=1 iff some completion x=p||b||q is accepted by C. There is a nondeterministic verifier with witness (q,y), where q has N-t-1 bits and y has one bit per gate of C, that accepts exactly when C(p||b||q)=1 and y is the consistent gate-value tableau. The verifier uses O(s+N) fan-in-two Boolean gates and O(s+N) witness/input bits. Proof: On input p,b and guessed q,y, check each gate equation in topological order, check that the output bit is 1, and check the fixed prefix and b are the designated input bits. Each gate equation has constant-size Boolean circuitry; conjunction over the s equations and output check costs O(s), while input/witness wiring and prefix handling costs O(N). If EXT_C(pb)=1, choose an accepting q and its uniquely induced tableau y; conversely an accepting verifier assignment supplies a completion on which C outputs 1. Thus the transition has a polynomial-size nondeterministic representation, while this argument gives no deterministic circuit bound after existentially eliminating q,y.
derivation: A suffix q plus the deterministic gate tableau y is an accepting witness iff the transition predicate is true; local gate consistency is checked independently per gate and conjoined.

statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-MASK EXT UPDATE LEMMA. Let C be a finite family of Boolean circuits, each computing a string w_C in {0,1}^N. After reading prefix p of length t, encode q_C=1 iff w_C begins with p. On reading b at position t, update q'_C=q_C AND [w_C(t)=b]. This exactly encodes candidates consistent with pb and is implementable by O(|C|) fan-in-two Boolean gates when the family and position are hardwired. Proof: A candidate matches pb iff it matched p and its position-t bit equals b, giving the stated bitwise update. Since w_C(t) is hardwired, comparison is b or NOT b; one AND gate per candidate suffices. Therefore the updated mask is exact and costs O(|C|) gates. For the family of all size-at-most-s circuit descriptions this gives an exact EXT prefix process but no compact-state transition bound, since the mask has one bit per description.
derivation: Maintain one candidate bit per circuit description. Filter by the next hardwired output bit and prove the filtered set equals precisely those descriptions whose output begins with the longer prefix.

label: S0760
statement:
statement: AFFINE RESIDUAL COUNT AND TRANSITION TEST. Let A=[A_<t|D_t] be an r by N matrix over GF(2), c in GF(2)^r, and F={x:Ax=c}. For prefix p in GF(2)^t, let R_t(p)={z:D_t z=c-A_<t p}. Then R_t(p) is nonempty iff c-A_<t p lies in im(D_t), and R_t(p)=R_t(q) iff A_<t p=A_<t q. The number of distinct nonempty residuals is either zero or 2^d, where d=dim(im(A_<t) intersect im(D_t)); it is nonzero exactly when c lies in im(A_<t)+im(D_t). Proof: For fixed D_t, fibers with distinct right-hand sides are disjoint, hence equal iff the right-hand sides are equal. A right-hand side c-A_<t p is attainable exactly when A_<t p lies in c+im(D_t). If this intersection is nonempty, it is an affine translate of im(A_<t) intersect im(D_t), so it contains 2^d distinct right-hand sides, each giving one distinct residual. Finally, membership is tested by V^T(c-A_<t p)=0 for a basis V of ker(D_t^T), using at most r parity tests and O(r(t+1)) fan-in-two gates. This applies only to affine solution sets and does not bound transitions for arbitrary EXT or MCSP circuits.
derivation: Fibers of a fixed linear map are disjoint unless their right-hand sides coincide; the attainable right-hand sides form the intersection of an affine coset with the prefix image, whose nonempty size is the size of their linear-space intersection.

statement: statement: AFFINE RESIDUAL FIBER COUNT. Let A=[B|D] be an r by N matrix over GF(2), let c be in GF(2)^r, and fix a cut with B the first t columns. For each prefix x in GF(2)^t, the residual set R_x={z in GF(2)^(N-t): Dz=c-Bx} is either empty or has cardinality 2^d, where d=dim(im(B) intersect im(D)). Proof: For any y, the solution set {z:Dz=y} is empty if y is not in im(D); otherwise it is a coset of ker(D), hence has size 2^(N-t-rank(D)). Across prefixes, the right sides c-Bx range over the affine coset c+im(B). The nonempty fibers therefore correspond to (c+im(B)) intersect im(D). If nonempty, this intersection has size 2^d because im(B) intersect im(D) is its translation space. Every rhs in it contributes 2^(N-t-rank(D)) suffixes. This proves the exact formula |R_x| is either 0 or 2^(N-t-rank(D)); and the number of prefixes with nonempty residual is either 0 or 2^(rank(B)-d), depending on c+im(B) meeting im(D).

statement: statement: AFFINE RESIDUAL FIBER AND PREFIX COUNT. Let A=[B|D] be an r by N matrix over GF(2), with B having t columns, and let c be in GF(2)^r. For x in GF(2)^t let R_x={z in GF(2)^(N-t): Dz=c-Bx}. Every nonempty R_x has size 2^(N-t-rank(D)). The number of x with R_x nonempty is zero if c is not in im(B)+im(D), and otherwise is 2^(t-rank(B)+d), where d=dim(im(B) intersect im(D)). Proof: D z=c-Bx is solvable exactly when c-Bx belongs to im(D), equivalently c belongs to im(B)+im(D). For any solvable right-hand side, its solution set is a coset of ker(D), so it has 2^(N-t-rank(D)) elements. Define L={y in im(B): c-y is in im(D)}. If nonempty, L is a translate of im(B) intersect im(D), hence has size 2^d. The linear map B:GF(2)^t -> im(B) is onto and every fiber has size 2^(t-rank(B)); thus the number of prefixes mapping into L is 2^(t-rank(B)+d).

label: S0764
statement:
statement: RESIDUALS FORCE DISTINCT SAME-LEVEL STATES. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix t in {0,...,N}. For p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. In every exact deterministic left-to-right streaming decider for L, if p and q reach the same state after t bits, then R_t(p)=R_t(q). Therefore at least |{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}| distinct states are necessary at level t. Proof: if the residual sets differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. From the same state, the deterministic continuation on z is identical, so the algorithm gives the same answer on pz and qz, contradicting exact decision since exactly one is in L. This proves the exact information requirement at a fixed level; it gives no real-gate transition-cost bound and no transfer to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: At a fixed prefix length, the continuation behavior from a state is a function only of that state and the remaining suffix. Exactness identifies this function with the residual-language membership function. Equal states therefore imply equal residual languages; taking the contrapositive gives the state lower bound.

statement: EXPLICIT CANDIDATE-FILTER UPDATE FOR EXT. Fix n,s and a finite encoding family C_{n,s} of all Boolean circuits of size at most s, with M descriptions and a defined output at each truth-table index i in [N], N=2^n. For prefix p of length t, store the M-bit vector v_p with v_p[j]=1 iff description C_j outputs p_i at every i<t. On reading b at index t, update v_{pb}[j]=v_p[j] AND [C_j(x_t)=b], where x_t is the t-th input in the fixed truth-table order. The initial vector is all ones; each update is computable by a fan-in-two circuit of O(M(s+n)) gates given the descriptions and t hardwired; and EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff some coordinate of v_p is 1. Proof: the invariant is exactly consistency with all previously read bits; adjoining b imposes precisely the additional equality C_j(x_t)=b. Induction on t proves the invariant, and at t=N nonemptiness is equivalent to the existence of a size-at-most-s circuit with that truth table. This exact construction does not yield a polynomial-in-s transition bound or an arbitrary-MCSP-circuit bridge.
derivation: Enumerate all size-at-most-s circuit descriptions; maintain one consistency bit per description and filter it by that circuit's output on the newly revealed truth-table input.

Find a compact representation with polynomial-in-s state and charged update cost, or establish a limitation.

statement:
statement: EXT RESIDUALS ARE SETS OF CONSISTENT CIRCUIT SUFFIX TABLES. Fix n,s, let N=2^n and let C_s be the finite set of circuit descriptions of size at most s. For 0<=t<=N and p in {0,1}^t, define A_p={C in C_s : the first t truth-table bits of C equal p} and T_C^(t) as the suffix of C's truth table after those t bits. For EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of a size-at-most-s circuit truth table, its residual R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in EXT_{n,s}} satisfies R_t(p)={T_C^(t): C in A_p}. Thus R_t(p)=R_t(q) iff the sets of distinct suffix tables generated by A_p and A_q are equal, even if A_p and A_q differ as sets of descriptions. Hence the number of distinct residuals at level t is at most min(2^{|C_s|},2^{2^{N-t}}). Proof: z belongs to R_t(p) iff pz is the truth table of some C in C_s, which is equivalent to C in A_p and T_C^(t)=z. Taking all such z gives the equality. The equivalence and cardinality bounds follow immediately from equality of sets and the two ambient set sizes. This gives an exact semantic quotient of the candidate-filter state; it does not give a compact representation or a real-gate transition bound for arbitrary MCSP circuits.
derivation: For each prefix p, existential completion by a size-at-most-s circuit is exactly membership in the set of suffix truth tables of circuits consistent with p. Quotient consistent descriptions by equality of their suffix tables; residual equality is equality of the resulting sets. Count subsets in either finite universe.

label: S0767
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY FOR DETERMINISTIC STREAMING RECOGNIZERS. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic exact left-to-right streaming recognizer whose state after reading a prefix p determines its final accept/reject result for every continuation z of the appropriate length. At any fixed prefix length t, if two prefixes p,q in {0,1}^t have different residuals R_t(p)={z:pz in F} and R_t(q)={z:qz in F}, then the recognizer must be in different states after p and q. Consequently, its number of states at layer t is at least the number of distinct residuals at that layer. Proof: Since R_t(p) and R_t(q) differ, there exists a suffix z in their symmetric difference. Without loss of generality, pz is in F and qz is not. If the states after p and q were equal, determinism implies that processing the same suffix z from that state produces the same final state and hence the same output. That contradicts exact recognition of F on pz and qz. Thus the states differ for every pair of distinct residuals, yielding the stated injection from residual classes to states. This lower bound concerns information/state count only; it gives no transition-circuit or update-time lower bound.
derivation: A suffix in the symmetric difference of two residuals distinguishes the prefixes. Determinism makes equal current states behave identically on that suffix, contradicting exact recognition. Therefore each residual class requires a distinct state.

label: S0768
statement: statement: RESIDUAL-COUNT WORKSPACE LOWER BOUND. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and let a deterministic exact one-pass recognizer process all N input bits. At layer t, let d_t be the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}, over p in {0,1}^t. If the recognizer uses at most S state bits at every point, then S >= ceil(log_2 d_t). Proof: By exactness and determinism, prefixes with distinct residuals must lead to distinct machine states: if R_t(p) != R_t(q), choose z in their symmetric difference; processing z from equal states would give equal outputs, contradicting that exactly one of pz,qz lies in F. Thus the map from residual classes at layer t to machine states is injective. There are at least d_t states, while S bits encode at most 2^S states. Hence 2^S >= d_t and S >= ceil(log_2 d_t). The bound concerns workspace only; it gives no lower bound on the circuit size or time to compute the next encoded state.

statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION CIRCUIT. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and let D_t be the set of distinct residuals R_t(p)={z:pz in F} at depth t, with d_t=|D_t|. For each t<N, an exact fan-in-two Boolean circuit takes a valid one-hot encoding e_R in {0,1}^{d_t} of R in D_t and the next bit b, and outputs the one-hot encoding of R_b in D_{t+1}, where R_b={u:bu in R}. It has at most 3d_t+3d_{t+1} gates, counting NOT, AND, OR gates. The construction is uniform from the explicit residual transition table. Proof: For each R in D_t and b in {0,1}, R_b belongs to D_{t+1}: if R=R_t(p), then R_b=R_{t+1}(pb). Hence each pair (R,b) has a unique target tau_b(R) in D_{t+1}. For each target Q and bit b, form g_{Q,b}=OR_{R:tau_b(R)=Q} e_R, with an empty OR equal to 0. Since e is valid one-hot, g_{Q,b}=1 exactly when the selected source transitions to Q on b. Output o_Q=(NOT b AND g_{Q,0}) OR (b AND g_{Q,1}). These outputs are one-hot and encode the correct target. Across Q and both b, each source appears in exactly one OR-list, so the OR trees take at most 2d_t gates total; each target uses at most three further gates; and NOT b costs one gate. The total is at most 2d_t+3d_{t+1}+1, which is at most 3d_t+3d_{t+1} because d_t>=1. This bound is for the one-hot representation and explicit transition table; it does not imply a small transition circuit for a logarithmic-bit encoding or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Construct target indicators by OR-ing one-hot source indicators grouped according to each section map tau_b, then select the corresponding transition with b. Count the OR trees by total source incidences (2d_t) and the selectors by targets (3d_{t+1}), plus one shared NOT.

label: S0771
statement:
statement: BINARY-CODED EXPLICIT RESIDUAL TRANSITION BOUND. Let D and E be nonempty finite sets of sizes d and e. Let tau_0,tau_1:D->E be given explicitly, with distinct binary codes of lengths k=ceil(log2 d) and l=ceil(log2 e). On valid source codes x and input bit b, the map (x,b)->code(tau_b(x)) has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(d(k+1)+e(l+1)) gates. Proof: For each a in D, form I_a=[x=code(a)] by AND-ing the k appropriate literals; for k=0 the sole indicator is constant 1. This costs O(d(k+1)). For each q in E and j in {0,1}, form G_{q,j}=OR_{a:tau_j(a)=q} I_a, with empty OR equal to 0. For each j, the source lists partition D, so all these OR trees cost O(d+e). Form H_q=(NOT b AND G_{q,0}) OR (b AND G_{q,1}) for each q, costing O(e). For valid x exactly one I_a is 1, hence exactly one H_q is 1, at q=tau_b(a). For each of the l output coordinates, OR the H_q whose assigned target code has that coordinate equal to 1; this costs O(e*l+l). The total is O(d(k+1)+d+e*l+e)=O(d(k+1)+e(l+1)). The construction is correct on valid source codes and is uniform given the explicit transition table and code assignments.
derivation: Decode the valid source code to one-hot indicators, group them by each explicit successor map, select the successor using b, then encode the unique target.

label: S0774
statement:
statement: WITNESS-FILTER UPDATE LEMMA. Let F be the set of distinct length-N words generated by a finite indexed family C_1,...,C_M, with fixed output bits y_{i,j} at positions j=0,...,N-1. For a prefix p of length t define S_t(p)={i: C_i has prefix p}. On reading b at position t, S_{t+1}(pb)={i in S_t(p): y_{i,t}=b}. If the state is the M-bit incidence vector of S_t(p), its update has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(M) gates, uniformly in t; the state is empty exactly when p has no completion in F. Proof: For each i, set z_i'=z_i AND [y_{i,t}=b]. Since y_{i,t} is fixed, the equality test is either b or NOT b; share the NOT across candidates. Thus each updated bit is 1 exactly for a previously live candidate matching the new bit, which is precisely S_{t+1}(pb).
derivation: Filter the exact indexed witness set by its next output bit. Applied to size-s circuits, this gives an exact but potentially exponential-size state and update circuit; it does not bound arbitrary compressed encodings.

statement:
statement: AFFINE RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let A=[P|D] over GF(2), with P having t columns, and let H={x:Ax=c}. For a prefix p∈GF(2)^t define R(p)={z:Dz=c−Pp}. Let φ:GF(2)^t→GF(2)^r/im(D) be φ(p)=Pp+im(D). If c+im(D) is not in im(φ), there are zero nonempty residuals. Otherwise, for any p₀ with φ(p₀)=c+im(D), the distinct nonempty residuals are in bijection with P(ker φ), so their number is 2^rank(P|ker φ). Proof: R(p) is nonempty exactly when φ(p)=c+im(D), whose solutions are p₀+ker φ. The residual is the fiber of D over c−Pp. Two nonempty fibers of D are equal only if their right-hand sides agree: any shared z gives D z equal to both right-hand sides. Thus residuals are indexed injectively by the values Pp for p∈p₀+ker φ. Those values form Pp₀+P(ker φ), which has cardinality |P(ker φ)|=2^rank(P|ker φ).
derivation: Use the quotient by im(D) to characterize consistent prefixes, then count distinct right-hand sides of the suffix system over that prefix fiber.

statement: statement: AFFINE RESIDUAL STATE BOUND. Let A be an r×N matrix over GF(2), c∈GF(2)^r, and F={x∈{0,1}^N: Ax=c}. At a cut t, write A=(A_<t | D_+), where A_<t consists of the first t columns and D_+ the remaining columns. For prefix p∈{0,1}^t, its exact residual is R_t(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}:D_+z=c+A_<t p}. The number of distinct residuals over all p is at most 2^r. They admit an exact r-bit state y(p)=c+A_<t p, with next-bit update y(pb)=y(p)+b a_t, where a_t is column t of A; the update uses O(r) fan-in-two Boolean gates. Proof: The displayed residual identity follows by splitting Ax=c into prefix and suffix terms; subtraction equals addition over GF(2). Each prefix maps to one of at most 2^r vectors y∈GF(2)^r, and y determines its residual set by the displayed equation, so there are at most 2^r residuals. Appending b changes the prefix contribution by b a_t, proving the update formula. Each output coordinate is either the corresponding input bit or its XOR with the fixed bit (a_t)_i when b=1; implementing the r conditional XORs costs O(r) fan-in-two gates. This is an exact bound for the affine language subclass only; it gives no transition bound for arbitrary EXT or MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL UPDATE BOUND. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and 0≤t<N. Let D_t be the set of distinct residuals R_t(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pz∈F} over prefixes p∈{0,1}^t, and d_t=|D_t|. Encode a current residual R∈D_t by its one-hot indicator vector indexed by D_t. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit, depending only on F and t, that on this vector and next input bit b outputs the one-hot encoding of R_b={u∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}:bu∈R}; its size is at most 6d_t+1. Proof: For every R∈D_t and b∈{0,1}, form token q_{R,b}=x_R∧ℓ_b, where ℓ_1=b and ℓ_0=¬b. This uses 2d_t AND gates and at most one NOT gate. For each R'∈D_{t+1}, output y_{R'} as the OR of all tokens q_{R,b} whose section R_b equals R'; if there are none, output constant 0. Each pair (R,b) has exactly one section in D_{t+1}, since R is itself a residual R_t(p), and R_b=R_{t+1}(pb). Hence the token groups partition the 2d_t tokens. Binary OR trees use at most 2d_t additional gates in total. For a one-hot input x_R*, exactly the token for R* and the actual b is 1, so exactly its successor output is 1 and all others are 0. Total size is at most 4d_t+1, hence at most 6d_t+1. Let D_t be the set of distinct residuals R_t(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pz∈F} over prefixes p∈{0,1}^t, and d_t=|D_t|. Encode a current residual R∈D_t by its one-hot indicator vector indexed by D_t. Proof: For every R∈D_t and b∈{0,1}, form token q_{R,b}=x_R∧ℓ_b, where ℓ_1=b and ℓ_0=¬b. This uses 2d_t AND gates and at most one NOT gate. For each R'∈D_{t+1}, output y_{R'} as the OR of all tokens q_{R,b} whose section R_b equals R'; if there are none, output constant 0. Each pair (R,b) has exactly one section in D_{t+1}, since R is itself a residual R_t(p), and R_b=R_{t+1}(pb). Hence the token groups partition the 2d_t tokens. Binary OR trees use at most 2d_t additional gates in total. For a one-hot input x_R*, exactly the token for R* and the actual b is 1, so exactly its successor output is 1 and all others are 0. Total size is at most 4d_t+1, hence at most 6d_t+1. label: S0778
statement: statement: FIXED-ORACLE STREAMING STATES BOUND RESIDUALS. Let F be a language of fixed-length strings {0,1}^N. Suppose a deterministic streaming decider M reads input left to right, has at most 2^w internal configurations at every cut (including all persistent work-tape contents and control state), and may make queries to one fixed oracle O. For each cut t, the number d_t of distinct residuals R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} is at most 2^w. Proof: Associate to each length-t prefix p the complete configuration c(p) reached after reading p. If c(p)=c(q), then for every suffix z, the future computation on z from that configuration is identical for pz and qz: the machine is deterministic, and every oracle query receives the same answer from the same fixed O. Hence pz is accepted iff qz is accepted for every z, so R_t(p)=R_t(q). Thus the map from reachable configurations at cut t onto residuals is well-defined and surjective, giving d_t≤|configurations|≤2^w. Scope: this is an exact state-count implication for deterministic fixed-oracle streaming deciders. It does not bound the cost of an oracle transition, does not imply a polynomial-size ordinary circuit for EXT or MCSP, and does not transfer a streaming state lower bound to general circuits.

label: S0780
statement: statement: TIME-VARYING TRANSITION UNROLLING. Let M be a deterministic machine reading inputs x_1,...,x_N in order, with a w-bit state after each step. Suppose for each i its state update from (state,x_i) to the next state is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most T gates, and its final accept/reject output from the last state is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most T gates. Then M's decision function on {0,1}^N has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most NT+T gates. Proof: Construct a layered circuit with one copy of the i-th update circuit at each position i, wiring its state inputs to the preceding layer and its input-bit input to x_i; initialize the first layer with M's fixed initial-state constants. By induction on i, the wires after layer i equal M's state after reading x_1,...,x_i. Apply the final decision circuit to the last layer. The resulting circuit computes M's decision function, and its gate count is at most the sum of N update-circuit sizes plus T, hence at most NT+T. Scope: this is conditional on ordinary fan-in-two circuits for every transition. It does not simulate oracle transitions or establish such circuits for the MMW19 EXT prefix machine.

label: S0781
statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-FILTERING AUTOMATON FOR EXT. Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be any finite indexed family of words in {0,1}^N, allowing duplicates, and let L_F={f_i:i<=M}. At depth t and prefix p in {0,1}^t, store q_p in {0,1}^M with q_p[i]=1 iff f_i has prefix p. The residual of L_F after p is exactly {f_i[t:N]:q_p[i]=1}. On reading b, update q_p to q_pb by q_pb[i]=q_p[i] AND [f_i(t)=b]. Thus the update is a stage-specific fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most M AND gates (the selectors [f_i(t)=b] are constants), and EXT acceptance at a prefix is the OR of the M state bits. Proof: For each i, f_i has prefix pb iff it has prefix p and its t-th coordinate equals b, proving the update coordinatewise. A suffix z is in the residual iff some i with q_p[i]=1 has suffix f_i[t:N]=z, precisely the definition of membership in L_F after prefix p. The disjunction of state bits is true iff at least one listed word extends p. For EXT_{n,s}, take F to be the indexed list of truth tables of all size-at-most-s circuits; this gives an exact, generally exponential-state representation and an O(M)-gate update after stage-specific candidate bits are available. It does not bound transition cost by a bounded number of operations on H_C or imply a statement about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Maintain one live bit per candidate truth table. Inductively q_p[i]=1 iff candidate i matches the consumed prefix. After b, candidate i remains live exactly when q_p[i]=1 and its fixed t-th output equals b. This establishes the update, residual characterization, and acceptance test.

statement: statement: EXACT EXT ACCEPTANCE FROM CANDIDATE FILTERING. Let N,M be positive integers and F=(f_1,...,f_M) an explicitly specified indexed family in {0,1}^N. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, 0<=t<=N, define q_p in {0,1}^M by q_p[i]=1 iff f_i[1..t]=p. Then p is an extendable prefix of F (that is, there exists f in F with prefix p) if and only if OR_i q_p[i]=1. For t<N and b in {0,1}, q_{pb}[i]=q_p[i] AND [f_i[t+1]=b]. Given the stage-t candidate-output bits a_i=[f_i[t+1]=b], this transition and acceptance test have Boolean circuits of O(M) fan-in-2 gates. Proof: By definition, q_p[i]=1 exactly for indices whose word agrees with p on the first t positions. Such a word exists precisely when at least one coordinate is 1, proving the acceptance equivalence. An index agrees with pb exactly when it agrees with p and its next bit equals b, which is the displayed coordinatewise conjunction. Implement M conjunction gates and an OR tree with M-1 gates (with the M=1 boundary handled by a wire); total O(M). The argument gives a uniform construction from the explicit family and stage bits, but makes no claim that those bits or the family can be constructed in polynomial time from an arbitrary circuit class H_C.

label: S0783
statement: statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY FOR EXACT STREAMING STATES. Let F be a language of binary strings of length N and fix 0<=t<=N. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}, and let d_t be the number of distinct such residual sets. Any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that decides F exactly after reading all N bits must have at least d_t distinct internal states after t input bits. Proof: If prefixes p and q lead to the same internal state, then determinism implies that for every common suffix z the algorithm has the same final state and output on pz and qz. Exactness therefore implies pz in F iff qz in F for every z, so R_t(p)=R_t(q). Thus prefixes inducing distinct residuals must induce distinct internal states, giving at least d_t states. Consequently the workspace is at least ceil(log2 d_t) bits. This is a representation-independent workspace bound; it gives no lower bound on update time and does not establish that d_t is large for EXT_{n,s}.

label: S0785
statement: REPAIR: AFFINE SUFFIX-PROJECTION CIRCUIT BOUND WITH EMPTY-SYSTEM COST. Let A be an r by N matrix over GF(2), c in GF(2)^r, and H(x)=1 iff Ax=c. Fix 0<=t<N; write A=(A_<t | a_t | D_+), and let V have columns forming a basis of ker(D_+^T). Then E_H(pb)=1 iff V^T(c+A_<t p+b a_t)=0, and this predicate has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(1+r(t+1)) gates with A,c,V hardwired, counting constants/output as O(1). Proof: A completion z exists iff D_+z=c+A_<t p+b a_t. By orthogonality and rank-nullity, im(D_+)=(ker(D_+^T))^perp, so completion is equivalent to the displayed parity equations. There are at most r equations, each an affine parity of at most t+1 input bits, computable with O(t+1) fan-in-two gates. Their conjunction costs O(r) gates; add O(1) for the output/constant boundary case. Gaussian elimination computes V in polynomial time. This concerns only affine GF(2) suffix projection, not arbitrary EXT or MCSP transitions.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL QUOTIENT TRANSITION LEMMA. For every finite L subseteq {0,1}^N and t<N, the map from a depth-t residual class [p] and bit b to the depth-(t+1) class [pb] is well-defined. Its residual is exactly the b-section of R_t(p). Therefore the layered minimal deterministic recognizer has r_t states at depth t, where r_t is the number of distinct residual sets.
derivation: If R_t(p)=R_t(q), then for every suffix u of length N-t-1, u is in R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu is in L iff bu is in R_t(p). Equality of the parent residuals makes this equivalent to qbu in L, hence u is in R_{t+1}(qb). Thus child residuals agree and the transition is representative-independent. Distinct residuals require distinct states, since a suffix in their symmetric difference distinguishes the prefixes; storing the residual and updating by taking sections suffices.
scope: Finite fixed-length Boolean languages and position-dependent deterministic streaming recognizers. This is an information/state characterization only; no gate-cost bound for succinct transitions follows.

statement:
statement: TRACE-COFACTOR UNIQUENESS LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with g gates, input x in {0,1}^N, and designated output gate o. Introduce one witness bit y_i per gate and define H_C(x,y) as the conjunction of y_o=1 and, for each gate i, y_i equals gate_i(x,y_{<i}), with gates in topological order. Then (i) for every x there is exactly one y satisfying all gate equations, namely C's evaluation trace; (ii) H_C(x,y)=1 exactly when C(x)=1 and y is that trace; (iii) fixing any input prefix p gives H_{C,p}(z,y)=H_C(pz,y), with the same gate equations and a unique trace for every z. Thus exists y H_{C,p}(z,y)=C(pz).
derivation: Induct in topological gate order. Given x and the earlier witness bits, gate i has a uniquely determined Boolean value, so its equation forces exactly one y_i. This proves existence and uniqueness of the complete trace. The output conjunct holds exactly when the trace's output bit is 1, proving (ii). For (iii), substitute the fixed prefix constants into the input wires. This changes no gate equation and adds no witness choices, so the same induction gives one trace for each suffix z. Existentially quantifying that trace accepts exactly when C(pz)=1. This establishes exact cofactoring of the verifier relation; it does not bound the cost of compiling its existential projection from H_C alone.
scope: Finite fan-in-two Boolean circuits with a fixed topological gate order, any input length, and any fixed prefix. No bound is claimed for compiling the projection z -> exists y H_{C,p}(z,y) from a succinct H_C description, nor for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
diagnostic_barriers: Relativizing: the identity relativizes, including oracle gates with their answers in the trace. Natural: no lower-bound argument is claimed. Algebrizing: no algebraic extension is used or ruled out. Localizing: the local gate equations are compatible with locality; no lower-bound mechanism is claimed. Circumvention tests are inapplicable because this is not a P!=NP result.

statement:
statement: REPAIRED LAYERED RESIDUAL IMPLEMENTATION BOUND. For any L subset {0,1}^N, let r_t be the number of distinct residual languages after length-t prefixes. A deterministic length-N recognizer with position-dependent transitions uses max_t r_t state labels, and at least r_t labels are necessary at each fixed depth t.
derivation: Set W=max_t r_t. For each t, inject the residuals at depth t into [W] using a code c_t. Initialize at c_0(L). At layer t, on bit b, send c_t(R) to c_{t+1}(R_b), where R_b={z:bz in R}. This is well-defined because the source code identifies R and R_b is determined by R. Define transitions arbitrarily on labels unused at layer t. At depth N accept c_N(R) exactly when the empty string belongs to R. By induction the state after prefix p is c_t(R_t(p)), so the machine recognizes L. Reuse across layers is valid because the transition function may depend on t and acceptance is terminal. Conversely, two distinct residuals at the same depth cannot share a state: a suffix distinguishing them would then have to produce the same acceptance. Hence at least r_t labels are necessary at depth t.
scope: Finite Boolean language of fixed length N; deterministic recognizer with position-dependent transitions and terminal acceptance. This bounds state labels only and says nothing about gate cost for succinctly implementing transitions.

statement: BOUNDED-SUFFIX PROJECTION LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with g gates, input x=(u,z) where z has k bits, and output C(u,z). Define P(u)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^k with C(u,z)=1. Then P has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^k g + 2^k - 1: take one copy of C(u,z) for each fixed assignment a to z, substitute z=a, and OR the 2^k outputs in a binary tree. In particular, for fixed k this is O(g) and the construction is uniform given C and k.
derivation: For each a in {0,1}^k, let C_a(u)=C(u,a), formed by substituting constants on the z-input wires. Substitution preserves correctness and uses at most g gates. The circuit P'(u)=OR_{a in {0,1}^k} C_a(u) accepts exactly when at least one suffix assignment makes C(u,z)=1, which is precisely the definition of P. A binary OR tree combines 2^k outputs using 2^k-1 fan-in-two gates. Thus the total is at most 2^k g+2^k-1. The construction does not provide polynomial size when k grows as an unrestricted input parameter, and it says nothing about eliminating an existential trace of an arbitrary succinct relation unless the relation is represented by the circuit C itself.
scope: Boolean circuits with a designated set of k existentially quantified input bits; fixed k gives linear-size projection. No general polynomial bound in g and k, no lower bound, and no conclusion for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits when k is large.
