statement: RESIDUAL AUTOMATON CHARACTERIZATION. Let L be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. In any deterministic exact streaming recognizer whose state after reading p determines acceptance for every continuation z, prefixes with distinct residuals R_p must reach distinct states. Conversely, the residuals at all depths form an exact recognizer: on bit b, R_p transitions to D_b(R_p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R_p}, and this equals R_{pb}; at depth N, accept iff the empty string belongs to R_p. Proof: If R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. A deterministic recognizer in the same state after p and q would give the same acceptance on continuation z, contradicting the definition of residual. For the converse, if R_p=R_q, then for each b and z, bz belongs to R_p iff z belongs to D_b(R_p), so D_b(R_p)=D_b(R_q); hence transitions are well-defined on residual classes. The identity D_b(R_p)=R_{pb} follows directly from p(bz)=(pb)z. Induction on the number of remaining bits shows that the residual state accepts exactly the continuations completing a word of L. The terminal rule is precisely membership of the empty continuation. For L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), this characterizes the exact information an EXT prefix state must preserve, but does not bound the Boolean gate cost of computing a transition from H_C or imply anything about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Distinct residuals are separated by a continuation in their symmetric difference, so exact deterministic recognition requires distinct states. Equality of residual sets is a right congruence under the left-derivative operation D_b; direct concatenation gives D_b(R_p)=R_{pb}. The terminal empty-string test and induction establish exact recognition.
scope: All finite N and all L subset {0,1}^N; deterministic exact one-pass recognition of fixed-length words. Applied to EXT with L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), it identifies required residual information only; no transition circuit or general MCSP lower bound is claimed.

label: S1013
statement: statement: FULL PREFIX REGISTER UPDATE LEMMA. Fix N>=1 and a time layer t in {0,...,N-1}. Encode a length-t prefix p as an N-bit vector q with q_i=p_i for 0<=i<t and q_i=0 for t<=i<N; the layer t is part of the recognizer's control (so this is a layered transition, not one time-homogeneous map). On input b, the next encoded prefix is q'_i=q_i for i<t, q'_t=b, and q'_i=0 for i>t. Each output bit is computed by a fan-in-two {AND,OR,NOT} circuit of at most one gate (indeed q'_i=q_i for i<t, q'_t=b, and q'_i=0 for i>t, so constants/wires suffice); hence total transition circuit cost is O(N), with zero nontrivial gates if wires and constants are free. The encoding is exact: induction on t gives q=(p,0^{N-t}) after every legal prefix. Given any fixed Boolean relation H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, the represented continuation predicate R_q(z)=1 iff exists w H(qz,w) is therefore updated exactly to R_{pb} by this transition. Proof: the coordinate equations copy the old prefix, append b at the unique next coordinate, and zero all unused coordinates; the induction establishes the invariant, and substitution into the definition gives R_{q'}(z)=exists w H(pb z,w). This result only bounds updates for the redundant full-prefix representation; it gives no bound for transitions on the succinct residual-state encoding of EXT, nor for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1014
statement:
statement: REPAIRED PADDED-PREFIX UPDATE LEMMA. Let N>=1, let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, and at layer t in {0,...,N} encode p in {0,1}^t by q=(p,0^{N-t}) in {0,1}^N. Define comp_t(q,z) in {0,1}^N for z in {0,1}^{N-t} by comp_t(q,z)_i=q_i for i<t and comp_t(q,z)_i=z_{i-t} for t<=i<N. Define F_t(q,z)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(comp_t(q,z),w)=1. For t<N and b in {0,1}, define q' by q'_i=q_i for i<t, q'_t=b, and q'_i=0 for i>t. Then q'=(pb,0^{N-t-1}) and for every z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, F_{t+1}(q',z')=F_t(q,bz'). The update on legal layer-t encodings has coordinate outputs that are wires/constants except coordinate t, which is b; its circuit uses zero nontrivial gates when wires and constants are free, or O(N) gates if output copies/constants are charged. Proof: Since q=(p,0^{N-t}), coordinatewise definition gives comp_t(q,bz')=pbz'=comp_{t+1}(q',z'). Existential quantification over the same w therefore gives equality of the F values. The coordinate formula for q' establishes the invariant at layer t+1. This is only a redundant full-prefix encoding; it makes no claim about bounded-cost updates on a succinct residual-state encoding or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: For legal q=(p,0^{N-t}), the first t coordinates of comp_t(q,bz') are p, and the remaining coordinates are bz'. Thus comp_t(q,bz')=pbz'. The updated legal register q' stores pb followed by zeros, so comp_{t+1}(q',z')=pbz' as well. H receives identical input vectors and the same witness domain {0,1}^r, hence the existential predicates are equal. The update coordinate equations give the stated gate cost.
scope: All finite N>=1, layers t<N, Boolean relations H with arbitrary fixed witness length r; deterministic layered updates on the padded-prefix register. No succinct-state or arbitrary-MCSP lower-bound implication.

label: S1015
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-COUNT TWO-SIDED BOUND. Let N>=0, L be a subset of {0,1}^N, and for t in {0,...,N} define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for each p in {0,1}^t. Let d_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_p. Then d_t <= min(2^t, |L|). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so d_t<=2^t. For each distinct nonempty residual R choose one prefix p_R realizing it. Distinct residuals have distinct chosen prefixes, since one fixed prefix determines exactly one set R_p. Choose any z_R in R. The words p_R z_R are distinct because their length-t prefixes p_R are distinct, and each belongs to L. This injects the d_t residuals into L, giving d_t<=|L|. Thus d_t<=min(2^t,|L|). This does not imply d_t<=2^{N-t}: residuals are subsets of the suffix universe, not suffixes.
derivation: Count the 2^t prefixes. Then choose one realizing prefix for each distinct nonempty residual; these prefixes must be distinct. Choosing one accepted suffix for each residual maps each residual to a distinct word in L, proving d_t<=|L|. Combining the bounds gives the result.
scope: All finite binary languages L subseteq {0,1}^N and all cut depths t. This bounds nonempty residual-state count but not transition circuit cost or the size of the bound for circuit-truth-table languages.

label: S1016
statement:
statement: LAYERED RESIDUAL RECOGNIZER LEMMA. Let N>=0 and L be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each t=0,...,N and p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}; let D_t={R_p:p in {0,1}^t}, including the empty residual if it occurs. There is an exact layered deterministic recognizer for L whose states at layer t are D_t and whose transition on b in {0,1} is delta_t(R,b)={z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz' in R} for t<N. Its terminal state R at layer N accepts iff the empty word belongs to R. At each layer |D_t|<=min(2^t,|L|)+1, so the total number of layer-state pairs is at most (N+1)(|L|+1). Proof: For each reachable state R=R_p, delta_t(R_p,b)={z': bz' in R_p}={z': pbz' in L}=R_{pb}; thus the transition is well-defined on residual sets, independent of which prefix represents the state, and induction on t shows the state after p is exactly R_p. At t=N the suffix universe consists only of the empty word, so membership of that word in R_p is equivalent to p in L. For the count, the nonempty residuals number at most min(2^t,|L|) by S1015's injection argument; there is at most one additional empty residual. Summing the per-layer bounds gives at most (N+1)(|L|+1) layer-state pairs. This is a state-count and semantic-transition result; it does not bound the Boolean circuit cost of implementing delta_t on a succinct encoding.
derivation: For any p,b, membership z' in delta_t(R_p,b) is equivalent in sequence to bz' in R_p, pbz' in L, and z' in R_{pb}; hence delta_t(R_p,b)=R_{pb}. This proves well-defined transitions and the recognizer invariant by induction. Terminal acceptance follows from the definition at suffix length zero. The per-layer bound follows from at most min(2^t,|L|) nonempty residuals plus at most one empty residual; summing N+1 layers yields the stated total.
scope: All finite fixed-length binary languages L and N>=0. Counts layered state pairs; no ordinary-gate transition-cost or MCSP implication is asserted.

label: S1017
statement:
statement: BINARY DFA TRANSITION CIRCUIT UPPER BOUND. Let A=(Q,{0,1},δ,q0,F) be any deterministic finite automaton with q≥1 states, and encode states by distinct k-bit strings where k=ceil(log2 q) (with k=0 if q=1). For each input symbol b∈{0,1}, the map δ_b on valid state codes, extended arbitrarily to unused k-bit codes, is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(qk+q) gates; hence one transition circuit taking (state,b) and outputting the next state uses O(q log(q+1)) gates. Proof: For each valid state code a and output coordinate j, form its equality indicator e_a(state)=∧_{i=1}^k (state_i if a_i=1 else ¬state_i), using O(k) gates per code. For each output coordinate j, form y_j=∨_{a∈Q: δ(a,b)_j=1} e_a(state), requiring O(q) gates after the indicators. Compute both b-specific outputs and select by b with one mux per output coordinate, O(k) additional gates. Total O(qk+q); q=1 is constant. The circuit agrees with δ on every valid code; unused codes may be assigned arbitrary behavior. This gives a general construction but for EXT, q may be as large as the number of distinct prefix residuals, which is not shown polynomial in n,s, so it does not close the arbitrary-MCSP transition-cost gap.
derivation: One-hot equality tests for all q valid k-bit codes cost O(qk). For each symbol and coordinate, OR the indicators of states whose transition output has that coordinate set; this costs O(qk) total over k coordinates and two symbols. The transition symbol selects between the two output words with O(k) gates. Overall O(qk+q), and valid-state correctness follows because exactly one equality indicator is true.
scope: All finite DFAs over a binary alphabet, ordinary fan-in-two Boolean circuits, binary state encoding; no assertion on the size of the EXT residual automaton.

label: S1018
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL SUFFICIENCY AND CHILD UPDATE LEMMA. Let N,r be nonnegative integers and H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1}. For each prefix p∈{0,1}^t, 0≤t≤N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: ∃w∈{0,1}^r H(pz,w)=1}. Then for every p of length t<N and b∈{0,1}, R_{pb}={z∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bz∈R_p}. Consequently R_p alone is sufficient to determine the next residual set after reading b: the update is the left quotient b^{-1}R_p. Proof: Fix p,b,z. By definition, z∈R_{pb} iff ∃w H(pb z,w)=1. Since bz is a length-(N−t) string, the definition of R_p says exactly that bz∈R_p iff ∃w H(p(bz),w)=1. These predicates are identical for every z, so the sets are equal. The right side depends only on R_p and b, hence equal residual sets have equal child residuals for each common next bit. This proves exact semantic state sufficiency for the projection automaton. It does not bound the cost of representing R_p or computing its quotient from a circuit description H in an ordinary fan-in-two circuit model.
derivation: Pointwise membership equivalence: z∈R_{pb} iff ∃w H(pb z,w) iff bz∈R_p. Extensional equality follows; the quotient is a function of R_p and b.
scope: All finite N,r, all Boolean relations H, all prefixes shorter than N; semantic residual states only, with no circuit-cost assertion.

label: S1019
statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-AGREEMENT FILTERING LEMMA. Let N be a positive integer and let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be any fixed finite list of Boolean functions f_j:{0,1}^N->{0,1}. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, define A_p={j in [M]: f_j(pz)=p_i for every i in [t], where z is the suffix completing pz to length N}; equivalently, j is live iff f_j agrees with p on the t queried inputs. After observing the next input string x_t (the t-th point in a fixed ordering x_1,...,x_{2^N} of {0,1}^N) and its target bit b_t, update each flag a_j to a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(x_t)=b_t]. Then the updated flags encode exactly A_{p'} for the extended observation prefix p'=(p,b_t). A synchronous fan-in-two Boolean circuit implements this update using at most 2M gates when the comparison bits [f_j(x_t)=b_t] are fixed constants for this time step. Proof: Initially all flags are 1, so A_empty=[M]. Suppose inductively that a_j=1 exactly for candidates agreeing with all earlier observed pairs (x_i,b_i), i<t. The update sets a'_j=1 exactly when that condition holds and f_j(x_t)=b_t, which is precisely agreement on all pairs through t. Each coordinate is one AND with a fixed bit (or a wire/constant); even charging one equality-to-constant AND and one combining AND gives at most 2M fan-in-two gates. This establishes the invariant by induction. Scope: fixed finite candidate list and fixed time-step comparison constants. The bound is O(M), with no assertion that M is polynomial in n,s, that comparisons can be generated cheaply, or that the state represents arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Induct on the number t of observations. Base: no observations leaves every candidate live. Step: retain candidate j exactly when it was previously live and its fixed prediction on x_t equals the observed b_t. This is exactly the defining condition for agreement on the extended prefix. Coordinatewise AND with a fixed comparison bit gives a fan-in-two implementation using at most 2M gates.

label: S1020
statement:
statement: REPAIRED CANDIDATE-AGREEMENT FILTERING LEMMA. Let X be a finite set, let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be a fixed finite list of functions f_j:X->{0,1}, and let H_t=((x_1,b_1),...,(x_t,b_t)) be any finite history in X×{0,1}. Define a_j(0)=1 and a_j(t+1)=a_j(t) AND [f_j(x_{t+1})=b_{t+1}]. Then for every j and t, a_j(t)=1 iff f_j(x_i)=b_i for every i≤t. Consequently the vector (a_1(t),...,a_M(t)) exactly represents the set of candidates consistent with H_t. If each comparison bit [f_j(x_{t+1})=b_{t+1}] is supplied as a constant, the update is implemented by at most M fan-in-two AND gates. Proof: Induct on t. statement: FIXED-WIDTH PREFIX SHIFT-REGISTER LEMMA. Let N>=1 and H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1} be any Boolean relation. A layered machine with state (a,u) in {0,1}^N x {0,1}^{N+1}, initialized (0^N,e_0), after t bits p=b_1...b_t stores a=0^{N-t}p and u=e_t. On input b its transition is a'=a_2...a_N b and u'=shift(u), so every next-state output is a current bit, input bit, or constant: zero fan-in-two Boolean gates when wires/constants are free. At layer t, decode p as the last t bits of a and represent R(z)=1 iff exists w in {0,1}^r H(pz,w). This is exactly the existential prefix residual, and the transition on b represents the child residual. Proof: induction on t; the initial state stores the empty prefix. Shifting and appending b transforms 0^{N-t}p into 0^{N-t-1}pb and shifts e_t to e_{t+1}. The residual identity follows by substitution into its definition. This gives zero-gate transitions only for an explicit O(N)-bit encoding. For EXT, N=2^m, so it implies neither a poly(m,s)-bit state bound nor a transition bound for compact residual encodings or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1022
statement:
statement: LAYERED DFA TRANSITION-CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let q>=2 and let a layered deterministic automaton over alphabet {0,1} have at most q states in each layer, with a specified initial state and a specified accepting subset at the final layer. There is an encoding of each layer's states by r=ceil(log2 q) bits such that each layer transition and the final acceptance test are computed by fan-in-two Boolean circuits using O(q log q) gates per layer. Proof: Pad each layer to q states and define transitions arbitrarily from padded states. For each state i, compute the equality selector e_i on the r state bits; each selector uses O(r) gates, so all q selectors use O(qr) gates. For each input symbol b and each next-state output bit k, OR the selectors e_i for which the transition from i on b has output bit k. The total number of selector appearances over the r output bits is at most qr for each b, so these ORs cost O(qr) gates per b. The symbol b can be included as a literal in each selector or the two symbol cases can be combined with O(qr) gates. The final acceptance bit is the OR of e_i over accepting states and costs O(qr). As r=ceil(log2 q), all stated bounds are O(q log q).
derivation: Explicit one-hot equality decoders from the binary state encoding feed ORs for each next-state bit; gate count is O(qr) for decoder construction and O(qr) for all output-bit ORs, with r=ceil(log2 q).
scope: All finite layered deterministic automata with binary alphabet and at most q states per layer, under fan-in-two Boolean circuits; this is an implementation upper bound only and makes no claim that the EXT residual automaton has polynomially many states in its parameters.

label: S1023
statement:
statement: FINITE-LANGUAGE LAYERED TRANSITION CIRCUIT. For every integer N>=0 and every fixed finite language L subseteq {0,1}^N, put M=|L|. There is a layered deterministic automaton recognizing L with at most M+1 states at every depth t in {0,...,N}, and its transitions and final acceptance test have fan-in-two Boolean circuit implementations of total size O(N(M+1) log(M+1)), with the convention log(M+1) is replaced by 1 when M=0. Proof: At depth t, a state is a residual R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for some p in {0,1}^t; include the empty residual if it occurs. There are at most M distinct nonempty residuals: for each prefix p with nonempty R_p choose z_p in R_p. The words pz_p are distinct for distinct prefixes p, so there are at most M such prefixes and hence at most M distinct nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual, giving at most M+1 states. The transition on b in {0,1} maps R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p}; this is well-defined on residuals because equal sets have equal cofactors, and the empty residual maps to itself. At each layer encode its q<=M+1 states by distinct r-bit strings, r=ceil(log2(M+1)) when M+1>=2 and r=1 otherwise. For a fixed input bit b and output bit j, form the OR over all source states u whose b-successor has jth code bit 1 of the equality selector [state_code=u]; an equality selector is an AND of r literals. Fan-in-two trees implement each equality selector and OR using O(qr+q) gates for that input symbol, hence O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates per layer under the stated convention. At depth N, the residual is either {epsilon} or empty, and a state equality test outputs acceptance exactly in the former case, using O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates. Summing over N layers proves the bound. For L=empty the sole state is empty and a constant-zero output suffices. This is a finite-language construction; applied to L=Im(Eval_{n,s}) its bound remains exponential unless M is independently controlled, and it gives no representation theorem for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Residuals form the canonical layered DFA; each nonempty residual has a distinct witnessing word in L, so each layer has at most |L|+1 states. A transition table on q encoded states is implemented by equality selectors and OR trees in O(q log q) fan-in-two gates per symbol. Summing across N layers yields the claimed bound.
scope: All N>=0 and all fixed finite L subseteq {0,1}^N; gate bound is parameterized by |L| and is not claimed polynomial in a succinct description of L.

statement: CANDIDATE-MASK UPDATE LEMMA. Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits, each with N input bits and a fixed truth-table ordering 0,...,N-1. For a prefix p in {0,1}^t define q_i(p)=1 iff C_i's truth table agrees with p on positions 0,...,t-1. On receiving b at position t<N, the next mask is q'_i=q_i(p) AND [C_i(t)=b] for i=1,...,M. Given the M bits a_i=C_i(t), all next-mask bits are computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most M+1 gates: share NOT b once, then use one AND gate per i, selecting b when a_i=1 and NOT b when a_i=0. The mask is exact: q_i(p)=1 iff C_i agrees with p; hence q'_i=1 iff C_i agrees with pb. Consequently, after t updates, q_i=1 exactly for listed circuits whose truth tables extend p, so q is nonzero iff p is extendible within F. The update uses M state bits and O(M) Boolean gates; it does not give a poly(log M) bound in general. The cost of producing constants a_i from circuit descriptions is excluded. This does not solve the arbitrary MCSP-decider transition problem.
derivation: Induct on t. Initially all q_i=1 for the empty prefix. For each listed circuit i, let a_i=C_i(t). Agreement at the new coordinate requires b=a_i as well as q_i=1. Thus q'_i=q_i AND b when a_i=1, and q'_i=q_i AND NOT b when a_i=0. Compute NOT b once and use one AND gate for each i. Therefore q'_i=1 exactly when C_i agrees with all t+1 coordinates. Induction proves the invariant and the nonzero-mask characterization.
scope: Every finite explicitly listed circuit family F and every prefix length t<N. Fan-in-two Boolean circuits over AND/OR/NOT; the vector a_i=C_i(t) is supplied to the update, and its production cost is excluded.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL COFACTOR UPDATE LEMMA. Let N>=1, L be any subset of {0,1}^N, and for a prefix p of length t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. For b in {0,1} and t<N, R_{pb}={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu in R_p}. Thus the exact residual after reading b is the b-cofactor of the previous residual. Moreover, prefixes p,q of the same length have R_p=R_q if and only if for every suffix z of length N-t, pz∈L iff qz∈L. Proof: For every u, u∈R_{pb} iff pbu∈L iff bu∈R_p, proving the identity pointwise. Equality of residual sets is by extensionality exactly equality of these membership predicates for every suffix. Consequently R_p is a sufficient state for deciding all future completions, and no coarser state that merges unequal residuals can preserve every future answer: if R_p≠R_q choose u in their symmetric difference, which distinguishes the continuation. The lemma gives exact information and the canonical distinguishability criterion, but asserts no efficient encoding or transition circuit for R_p.
derivation: Expand the definition of R_p and concatenate the next bit b with the remaining suffix u. The cofactor identity follows pointwise. Extensional equality gives the iff characterization. If two residuals differ, their symmetric difference contains a suffix whose completion answer differs, so any state representation preserving all completion answers must keep them distinct.
scope: All finite binary languages L subset {0,1}^N, every prefix depth t<N. This is an information-theoretic statement only; no size or cost bound is claimed.

structure.gap: This closes only the exact residual-information subclaim: the residual is necessary and sufficient as a semantic state, and its transition is cofactoring. It leaves open the assigned bridge: represent and compute these cofactors from arbitrary MCSP decision-circuit H_C with poly(s,n) workspace and worst-case update time, charging all operations and output generation.

statement:
statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY TRACKER WITH OUTPUT-GENERATION COST. Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates and N input bits, with a fixed truth-table ordering indexed by 0,...,2^N-1. A streaming tracker processes a proposed truth table y in that order. Its state consists of M candidate bits q_i and an N-bit coordinate counter. Initially all q_i=1 and the counter is 0. On each incoming bit b at coordinate t, evaluate every C_i(t), set q_i'=q_i AND [C_i(t)=b], and increment the counter. The update can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(Ms+N) gates. After t updates, q_i=1 iff C_i agrees with the first t bits of y; hence some q_i=1 iff the prefix extends to the truth table of a member of F.
derivation: Evaluating all M listed circuits on the current N-bit coordinate uses O(Ms) gates. Each equality-to-b test and candidate-bit conjunction uses O(1) gates per circuit, hence O(M) gates. A binary increment of the N-bit counter uses O(N) gates. Thus one update uses O(Ms+N) gates. Initially the invariant holds vacuously. At coordinate t, the update preserves q_i precisely when its next truth-table bit matches b; induction proves the invariant after every prefix. Therefore nonzero mask is equivalent to extendibility within F.
scope: Explicit finite listed families; gate count excludes storage-cell implementation and assumes the candidate circuits are given. No polynomial-in-s bound follows when M is large; this does not establish a transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL SPLIT AND RECONSTRUCTION LEMMA. Let N be a nonnegative integer, L subseteq {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p in {0,1}^t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, and for b in {0,1}, R_{pb}={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: pbu in L}. Then R_p = ({0} x R_{p0}) disjoint-union ({1} x R_{p1}). In particular, the ordered pair (R_{p0},R_{p1}) uniquely determines R_p, and for any p,q of length t, R_p=R_q implies R_{pb}=R_{qb} for each b. Proof: For any z in {0,1}^{N-t}, write its first coordinate uniquely as b and its remaining suffix as u, so z=bu. By definition, z in R_p iff pbu in L iff u in R_{pb}. Thus z lies in {b}xR_{pb}, establishing both inclusions in the displayed union. The union is disjoint because its members have distinct first coordinates. This identity reconstructs the parent set from its two child sets. If R_p=R_q, then for each b and u, u in R_{pb} iff bu in R_p iff bu in R_q iff u in R_{qb}, hence the child residuals are equal.
derivation: Split every suffix z according to its first bit; membership in the resulting child suffix set is exactly membership in the corresponding child residual. Disjointness follows from the distinct leading bit. Equality of parent residuals therefore implies equality of each bit-slice.
scope: All finite binary languages and all nonterminal prefix depths. This is a semantic transition/decomposition lemma; it gives no bound on the circuit cost of computing a represented child residual.

statement: RESIDUAL SPLIT AND RECONSTRUCTION LEMMA. Let N be a nonnegative integer, L subseteq {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p in {0,1}^t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, and for b in {0,1}, R_{pb}={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: pbu in L}. Then R_p = ({0} x R_{p0}) disjoint-union ({1} x R_{p1}). In particular, the ordered pair (R_{p0},R_{p1}) uniquely determines R_p, and for any p,q of length t, R_p=R_q implies R_{pb}=R_{qb} for each b. Proof: For any z in {0,1}^{N-t}, write its first coordinate uniquely as b and its remaining suffix as u, so z=bu. By definition, z in R_p iff pbu in L iff u in R_{pb}. Thus z lies in {b}xR_{pb}, establishing both inclusions in the displayed union. The union is disjoint because its members have distinct first coordinates. This identity reconstructs the parent set from its two child sets. If R_p=R_q, then for each b and u, u in R_{pb} iff bu in R_p iff bu in R_q iff u in R_{qb}, hence the child residuals are equal.
derivation: Split every suffix z according to its first bit; membership in the resulting child suffix set is exactly membership in the corresponding child residual. Disjointness follows from the distinct leading bit. Equality of parent residuals therefore implies equality of each bit-slice.
scope: All finite binary languages and all nonterminal prefix depths. This is a semantic transition/decomposition lemma; it gives no bound on the circuit cost of computing a represented child residual.

statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE PREFIX FILTER CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let N,k>=0 and W=(w_1,...,w_k) be an explicit list in {0,1}^N. At layer t encode prefix p by v_i=1 iff p=w_i[0:t]. On bit b, set v_i'=v_i AND [w_i[t]=b]. With W hardwired, this uses at most k fan-in-two AND gates per layer, Nk total across N layers, and masks are constructible in O(Nk) time and bits. At t=N, OR_i v_i accepts exactly the listed words. This gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound for W=Im(Eval_{n,s}) unless that image is explicitly listed at polynomial cost.
derivation: Induct on t. At t=0 every word matches the empty prefix. If v_i indicates agreement through positions <t, then AND with [w_i[t]=b] indicates agreement through positions <t+1, exactly the prefix pb. At t=N some coordinate is 1 iff p is listed. Each update is one AND with a fixed bit; there are k coordinates per layer. Constructing all masks by scanning W takes O(Nk) time and bits.
scope: All finite N,k and explicit ordered lists W of N-bit strings; stage-dependent constants and fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits. Repetitions allowed. No succinct-family bound is implied.

label: S1030
statement:
statement: PREFIX-REGISTER CIRCUIT UPDATE / ENDPOINT-SEPARATION LEMMA. Let N>=1 and L be any subset of {0,1}^N. At layer t, 0<=t<=N, represent the observed prefix p in an N-bit register P, with P_i=p_i for i<t and P_i=0 for i>=t; the layer index t is supplied by the layered machine. Given next input bit b, copy P_0,...,P_{t-1}, write b into coordinate t, and zero coordinates t+1,...,N-1. This update has O(N) fan-in-two circuit cost (in fact it is only wires and constants, if those are free). After N inputs, acceptance is exactly the predicate P in L. Thus transition cost is O(N) for every L, independently of endpoint-membership complexity; the lemma does not bound the acceptance circuit for L or give an efficient uniform decider for L.
derivation: Induct on t. Initially P is all zero and encodes the empty prefix. If P_i=p_i for i<t and P_i=0 for i>=t, the described update encodes pb at layer t+1. At t=N, P is the complete input word x, so testing P in L is precisely membership x in L. The update only routes old register wires, the new input bit, and constants; it performs no membership computation.
scope: All finite length-N languages in a layered model with the layer index available; transition circuit cost only, with endpoint acceptance cost excluded.

label: S1033
statement:
statement: SURVIVING-DESCRIPTION RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION. Let D be any finite set of descriptions, each describing a word Eval(d) in {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t, let A_p={d in D: Eval(d) begins with p}, and let R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in {Eval(d):d in D}}. Then R_p={suffix_{N-t}(Eval(d)):d in A_p}. Consequently, two prefixes p,q of the same length have identical residual languages iff the sets of suffix words produced by their surviving descriptions are equal; the surviving-description sets themselves need not be equal. Proof: If z in R_p, then pz=Eval(d) for some d, so d belongs to A_p and its remaining suffix is z. Conversely, if d belongs to A_p, Eval(d)=pz for its unique remaining suffix z, so pz is in the image and z belongs to R_p. Equality of residual languages is therefore exactly equality of these projected suffix-image sets, and does not imply equality of A_p and A_q.
derivation: Both inclusions follow directly from the definitions: a suffix in the residual is witnessed by a description whose word has prefix p; every surviving description's word factors uniquely as p followed by its suffix. Thus residual equivalence quotients surviving descriptions by equality of their suffix-image sets.
scope: All finite description families and each fixed prefix length t. This is a semantic characterization; it gives no efficient representation, update algorithm, or bound for transitions of arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1034
statement:
statement: TOTAL PREFIX-RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N. For each depth t in {0,...,N}, and each prefix p in {0,1}^t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. Let d_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_p at depth t. Then sum_{t=0}^N d_t <= (N+1)|L|. If the empty residual is counted at each depth, the total number of distinct residual states over all depths is at most (N+1)(|L|+1). Proof: For each depth t, let P_t={p in {0,1}^t:R_p is nonempty}. For each p in P_t choose one word w_p in L extending p. Distinct prefixes at the same depth yield distinct chosen words, so |P_t|<=|L|. Since every distinct nonempty residual at depth t is realized by at least one p in P_t, d_t<=|P_t|<=|L|. Summing over the N+1 depths gives the first bound. At each depth there is at most one empty residual, so adding at most N+1 gives the second bound.
derivation: At each fixed depth, choose one extending word for each nonempty prefix. The chosen words are distinct because their length-t prefixes differ. Thus the number of nonempty prefixes, and hence distinct nonempty residuals, is at most |L|. Sum over depths; add at most one empty residual per depth.
scope: Every finite N>=0 and every L subset of {0,1}^N. This counts states in the depth-layered prefix residual representation and asserts no bound on transition computation cost.

label: S1035
statement:
statement: TAGGED CHILD-DECOMPOSITION OF PREFIX RESIDUALS. Let N>=0, let L⊆{0,1}^N, and for every prefix p of length t≤N define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pz∈L}. For t<N, R_p = {0z:z∈R_{p0}} ∪ {1z:z∈R_{p1}}, and these two sets are disjoint. Consequently, |R_p|=|R_{p0}|+|R_{p1}|. Proof: If z∈R_p, then pz∈L. Its first bit a∈{0,1} is unique; write z=aw. Then p a w∈L, so w∈R_{pa}, and z belongs to the corresponding tagged child set. Conversely, if w∈R_{pa}, then p a w∈L, hence aw∈R_p. The tagged sets are disjoint because their first bits differ. Their cardinalities therefore add. This is a recursion for the semantic residual sets and does not bound the gate cost of computing them.
derivation: Partition extensions of p according to the next input bit. Removing that bit gives exactly the child residual, while restoring it tags the child suffixes by 0 or 1. The tags make the union disjoint.
scope: Every finite N, every L⊆{0,1}^N, and every prefix p with |p|<N. No circuit complexity or PNP separation conclusion.

label: S0001
statement:
statement: Let f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}. If every cut matrix M_t^π of f has rank at most 1 over a field K, for a fixed variable order π, then every cut has at most two distinct residual functions, and the ordered decision diagram under π has width at most 2.
proof: At a cut, the rows of M are the residual truth tables. Rank zero means every row is zero, so there is one distinct residual. If rank is one, choose a nonzero row u. Every row is λu for some λ∈K. Since rows and u are Boolean and u has a coordinate equal to 1, inspecting that coordinate shows λ∈{0,1}. Thus there are at most two distinct rows. The number of distinct residual functions is exactly the width of the reduced layered OBDD at that cut. Applying this at every cut proves the width bound.
scope: Finite Boolean functions, one fixed variable order, with all cut-matrix ranks at most one over the same field K.

statement: Counting lemma: for a basis of g binary ops, |Im_{n,s}| <= (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s. Hence for (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s < 2^N a random y in {0,1}^N avoids Im_{n,s} with probability >= 1 - (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s/2^N. Proof: a circuit with k gates is a sequence of k triples (op,i,j) with g*(n+s)^2 choices each; sum over k<=s.

label: S0010
statement:
statement: Randomized restricted range avoidance. Fix n>=1, N=2^n, and the fan-in-two Boolean circuit model on n named inputs with one output and at most s gates over {AND, OR, NOT}, with constants allowed if included in the encoding. Let K be the number of valid encoded circuits. If K <= N^a for a fixed constant a and K/2^N <= 1/2, there is a uniform Las Vegas algorithm that outputs a truth table outside the size-s circuit image, with expected running time O(N(K+1)) circuit-table operations and O(N) bits of candidate storage, plus the space needed to enumerate one circuit. Proof: independently sample a uniformly random y in {0,1}^N; enumerate all valid circuits, evaluate each on the N input assignments, and reject y if any output table equals y. If rejected, resample. Each trial accepts exactly when y is outside the image. At most K tables are in the image, so acceptance probability is at least 1-K/2^N >= 1/2. The expected number of trials is at most 2. Each trial evaluates at most K circuits on N inputs and compares their tables to y, costing O(N(K+1)) Boolean operations. Accepted y is outside the image by the exhaustive membership check. Under the standard gate-description bound K <= 2^{O((s+1)log(n+s+2))}, this gives polynomial-in-N expected time whenever s log(n+s+2)=O(n), subject to the stated encoding bound.
evidence: Complete sampling-and-verification proof supplied here. The result is randomized and only covers circuit counts K polynomial in N; it does not satisfy the deterministic polylogtime-uniform AC0 refuter hypothesis of CJSW Prop. 4.3 and does not close G0001.

label: S0013
statement: Corrected image-counting bound. Fix n>=1, s>=0, g>=1. Consider ordered fan-in-two circuits with n named input wires, constants 0 and 1, at most s gates, each gate chosen from g binary operations and taking its two operands from the input, constant, and earlier-gate wires; the output is any such wire. Put W=n+s+2. There are at most W choices for the output wire. For each k<=s, there are at most (g W^2)^k ordered gate lists. Therefore the total number of descriptions, and thus distinct Boolean functions on the n inputs, is at most W sum_{k=0}^s (g W^2)^k <= (s+1)W(g W^2)^s. Proof: for any fixed k, each of its k gates has at most g choices of operation and W choices for each operand, since n+k+2<=W; after the gate list is fixed there are at most W output choices. Summing over k gives the first bound. Since gW^2>=1, each of the s+1 summands is at most (gW^2)^s, giving the second bound. This repairs the omitted output-wire factor for this explicit encoding; it does not imply polynomial-time range avoidance at the CJSW threshold, so G0001 remains open.

label: S0014
statement: Output-sensitive deterministic range avoidance. Let N>=1 and let L=(z_1,...,z_K) be an explicitly enumerable list of strings in {0,1}^N, with repetitions allowed and K<2^N. There is a deterministic procedure that outputs y outside the set of strings appearing in L using at most NK inspections of list bits, O(N+log(K+1)) working bits beyond the list enumerator, and N sequential scans of L. Proof: start with the empty prefix p, matched by q_0=K list entries. At stage i (1<=i<=N), scan L and count the entries whose first i-1 bits equal p and whose i-th bit is 0 or 1. These counts sum to the number q of entries matching p. Extend p by a bit whose count is at most q/2, breaking ties toward 0. Inductively, after i stages at most K/2^i entries match p. After N stages the matching count is an integer less than 1, hence zero; the resulting y=p is absent from L. Each of N scans reads at most K strings of N bits, so at most NK list-bit inspections suffice. Storing p and counters takes O(N+log(K+1)) bits beyond the enumerator's own state. For a circuit-image list this proves a deterministic construction conditional on a complete enumerator, with total time including N full scans; it gives no polynomial-in-N bound when that list is too large.

label: S0011
statement: PROOF. Put lo = sum_{i in F} min(w_i,0), hi = sum_{i in F} max(w_i,0). Restricted g is constant 1 iff V+lo >= t, constant 0 iff V+hi < t, where V = sum_{i not in F} w_i b_i. So g is non-constant iff V lies in [t-hi, t-lo), a set of hi-lo = W_F consecutive integers. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord: for integers |c_i|>=1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(N,floor(N/2)) of the 2^N sums of subsets of {c_i}. Apply it to 2V - sum w_i = sum w_i eps_i with eps_i = 2b_i - 1 (nonzero coefficients only; zero weights contribute constants) to get max_x Pr[V=x] <= C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N. Union over the W_F integer values gives the first inequality; C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives the second. For N=0 the bound is W_F and is trivially valid. CORROLLARY: E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_i |w_i| <= kKs/n. Since N >= s-k deterministically: if s >= 2k, 1/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt(2/s), so the bound is <= sqrt(2) kK sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n). If s < 2k, use the bound with c <= 1: kKs/n <= 2k^2K/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n) since k^2 <= n/2. Summing over gates gives the stated count.

Let W_F = sum_{i in F} |w_i| and N = |supp(w) \ F|. Then Pr_b[g|restriction is non-constant in the free variables] <= W_F * C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= W_F/sqrt(N) (N>=1). structure.proved_step: PROOF. Put lo = sum_{i in F} min(w_i,0), hi = sum_{i in F} max(w_i,0). Restricted g is constant 1 iff V+lo >= t, constant 0 iff V+hi < t, where V = sum_{i not in F} w_i b_i. So g is non-constant iff V lies in [t-hi, t-lo), a set of hi-lo = W_F consecutive integers. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord: for integers |c_i|>=1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(N,floor(N/2)) of the 2^N sums of subsets of {c_i}. Apply it to 2V - sum w_i = sum w_i eps_i with eps_i = 2b_i - 1 (nonzero coefficients only; zero weights contribute constants) to get max_x Pr[V=x] <= C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N. Union over the W_F integer values gives the first inequality; C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives the second. For N=0 the bound is W_F and is trivially valid. CORROLLARY: E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_i |w_i| <= kKs/n. Since N >= s-k deterministically: if s >= 2k, 1/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt(2/s), so the bound is <= sqrt(2) kK sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n). If s < 2k, use the bound with c <= 1: kKs/n <= 2k^2K/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n) since k^2 <= n/2. Summing over gates gives the stated count.

statement: LEMMA (kind LEMMA, repair attempt for G0013; not claimed to close G0001). Setup: w_1..w_m in Z^n, thresholds t_1..t_m, a set F of k free coordinates, complement R with |R| = n-k, and a fixed assignment b in {0,1}^R. Restricted gate g_j|_b(y) = [sum_{i in F} w_ji y_i >= t_j - S_j(b)], S_j(b) = sum_{q in R} w_jq b_q, for y in {0,1}^F. Claim: the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among {g_j|_b : j <= m} is at most sum_{i=0}^{k+1} C(2^k, i) <= (2^k+1)^{k+1} <= 2^{(k+1)^2}, independent of m and n. structure.lemma: SURVIVOR COMPRESSION (bounded weights, R0837). Let w_1..w_m in Z^n with |w_{j,i}| <= K, thresholds T_j, a k-set F, and a fixing b in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i not in F} w_{j,i} b_i] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct NON-CONSTANT functions among all g_{j,b} is at most D_k = 2Kk(2K+1)^k. PROOF: for fixed u in [-K,K]^F the values u.x (x in {0,1}^F) lie in an integer interval of length 2Kk, so at most 2Kk+1 distinct values; a non-constant table x -> [u.x >= tau] is determined by the cut among the distinct values, so at most 2Kk non-constant tables per u; the restricted weight vectors lie in [-K,K]^F, so at most (2K+1)^k choices of u; union bound. Consequence: the restricted top sum equals const + sum over at most D_k fixed tables of coefficient * table (exact identity).

label: S0021
statement: LEMMA (bounded-weight table count, complete proof). Let K, k >= 1, let U = [-K,K]^k, and let T_{K,k} be the set of NON-CONSTANT functions {0,1}^k -> {0,1} of the form x -> [u.x >= tau] with u in U and tau in Z. Then |T_{K,k}| <= 2Kk(2K+1)^k. PROOF: fix u in U. For x in {0,1}^k, u.x lies in [lo,hi] with lo >= -Kk and hi <= Kk, so hi - lo <= 2Kk. The table x -> [u.x >= tau] is constant unless lo < tau <= hi, and for tau in (lo,hi] the table is determined by tau, giving at most hi - lo <= 2Kk distinct non-constant tables per u. There are (2K+1)^k vectors u, so the union bound gives the claim. Consequence (exact identity): for any surviving bottom gates with weights in U and any top weights v, the restricted top sum equals a constant plus sum over T in T_{K,k} of c_T * T, with c_T the sum of v_j over gates whose restricted table is T.

label: S0026
statement: LEMMA (K = 1 repair of the SURVIVOR COMPRESSION step; does NOT close G0001). Statement: let n, k >= 1, F subset [n], |F| = k, weights w_j in {-1,0,1}^n for j = 1..m, integer thresholds T_j, and a fixing b in {0,1}^([n] minus F). Define g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i not in F} w_{j,i} b_i] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among all g_{j,b} (over all j and b) is at most 3^k (2k+2). PROOF: fix j, b. Put v = (w_{j,i})_{i in F} in {-1,0,1}^F and tau = T_j - sum_{i notin F} w_{j,i} b_i in Z. Then g_{j,b}(x) = [s(x) >= tau] with s(x) = v.x, and s(x) is an integer in [-k, k] for all x in {0,1}^F. Replace tau by tau' = min(max(tau, -k), k+1). If tau < -k then tau' = -k and both functions are identically 1, since s(x) >= -k. If tau > k+1 then tau' = k+1 and both functions are identically 0, since s(x) <= k. Otherwise tau' = tau. So g_{j,b} = [v.x >= tau'] with tau' in {-k, ..., k+1}, a set of 2k+2 values. Hence each restricted function is determined by the pair (v, tau') in {-1,0,1}^F x {-k..k+1}, which has 3^k (2k+2) elements. Counting these pairs bounds the number of distinct functions. Non-constant ones form a subset. QED. SCOPE: holds for all n, k, m with weights in {-1,0,1}. It is non-trivial only when 3^k(2k+2) < m, i.e. k below about log_3 m (about 0.95 log_2 n for m = n^1.5). At k = floor((1/2) log_3 n) the count is at most sqrt(n)(2 log_3 n + 2), which is below the number of surviving gates n log n in the window lemma regime. WHY THIS DOES NOT CLOSE G0001: G0001 asks for a bound on sum_l K_l (the total OBDD size over all levels for a constructible order), and this lemma bounds only the distinct restricted functions for ONE fixed set F of k variables, for a restricted range of k. It does not bound the number of distinct residual functions at all levels with 2^(n-k) assignments. Also, the lemma gives no saving at k ~ sqrt(n), where the refuted bound applies. The ratio of this bound to the trivial count, and the exact crossover k, are checked by cm (see the code run in this session).

statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (tightened restriction-count bound, repairs S0021). Let W in {-K..K}^{m x n}, t in Z^m, F a k-subset of [n], C = [n]\F, and for a fixing b in {0,1}^C let g_{j,b}(x) = [W_{j,F}.x >= t_j - W_{j,C}.b] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct NON-CONSTANT functions among {g_{j,b} : j, b} is at most K k (2K+1)^k. PROOF: fix a vector u in [-K,K]^F. The values u.x (x in {0,1}^F) lie in an integer interval of length L = sum_i |u_i| <= Kk, so they take at most Kk+1 distinct values v_0 < ... < v_r with r <= Kk. The table x -> [u.x >= tau] is constant iff tau <= v_0 or tau > v_r. For tau in (v_0, v_r] the table depends only on which v_i are >= tau, so there are at most r <= Kk distinct non-constant tables for this u. Every restricted gate has its direction u = W_{j,F} in [-K,K]^F, which gives at most (2K+1)^k directions. Union bound: at most Kk(2K+1)^k. This is sharper than the 2Kk(2K+1)^k in S0021 by a factor of 2. SCOPE: deterministic, every F, every fixing b, arbitrary thresholds, bounded weights. It is bookkeeping, not progress: at k = Theta(sqrt n) the bound is 2^{Theta(sqrt n)}, which exceeds m = poly(n), so it does NOT close or shrink G0001 / O-H.

statement: LEMMA (repair of G0046, all supports). Let w in Z^n have support S with |S| = s >= 1 and 1 <= |w_i| <= K on S. Let F be a uniform random k-subset of [n], b uniform on the coordinates outside F, and g = [w.x >= t] for any integer t. Then E_F Pr_b[g non-constant] <= (sqrt2*K + 2/sqrt(n)) * k/sqrt(n). statement: Fixed-advice pattern bound: For every finite set X, every integer s >= 0, and every fixed function D:{0,1}^s x X -> {0,1}, the family of Boolean labelings {x -> D(a,x): a in {0,1}^s} has cardinality at most 2^s. Proof: the map a -> (x -> D(a,x)) has domain {0,1}^s, of cardinality 2^s; the cardinality of its image cannot exceed the cardinality of its domain. Scope: fixed decoder; only the advice varies. This does not imply that a QE reduction's truth-table input is represented by the advice.

statement: Corrected decoder lemma: Let X be any finite set, R:X->{0,1}^N any map, L:X->{0,1} any labeling, and C-range any nonempty set of witness circuits. label: S0003
statement: statement: Canonical-witness consequence of universal witness correctness. Let X be a finite set, let A be an oracle, let C_T={C : tt(C^A)=T} be nonempty, and let D:X×C_T→{0,1} satisfy D(x,C)=L(x) for every x∈X and every C∈C_T. For any selected representative C_T^*∈C_T, D(x,C_T^*)=L(x) for all x∈X. Moreover, for every x, the value D(x,C) is constant as C ranges over C_T. Proof: fix x. For any C,C'∈C_T, the assumed correctness gives D(x,C)=L(x)=D(x,C'); selecting C=C_T^* gives the first assertion. Thus universal quantification over witnesses is equivalent, at the level of correctness alone, to correctness for one representative per nonempty truth-table class. This does not bound the cost of finding or evaluating C_T^*, and does not remove x as a decoder input.

statement: Selector-composition lemma. Let X be a finite input set, R:X→Y a reduction map, L:X→{0,1} a labeling, and C_T a nonempty witness set for each relevant T∈Y. Suppose a deterministic selector S(T) outputs some C_T∈C_T, and a deterministic decoder D(x,C) outputs L(x) for every x and every C∈C_{R(x)}. Then A(x)=D(x,S(R(x))) decides L on X. If R, S, and D have running times r, q, and t, respectively, then A runs in time at most r+q+t, plus the time to pass their outputs between procedures. Proof: for any x, put T=R(x). By the selector hypothesis S(T)∈C_T=C_{R(x)}. The universal decoder hypothesis therefore gives D(x,S(R(x)))=L(x). This holds for every x, so A is correct. Scope: this is a conditional composition lemma; it does not establish an efficient selector for the QE* witness sets.
proof: Fix x∈X and let T=R(x). The selector returns C=S(T)∈C_T. Since T=R(x), this is an admissible witness in C_{R(x)}. By the assumed decoder correctness, D(x,C)=L(x). Thus A(x)=L(x) for every x. The stated running-time bound follows by sequentially running R, S, and D and accounting for output handoff.
scope: Finite-domain implication for deterministic procedures with the stated correctness and selector assumptions. No selector construction, QE* reduction, or P≠NP consequence is proved.

statement: statement: Prefix-extension self-reduction. Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Define E(y,p)=1 iff p extends to a string z with W(y,z). If each E query costs at most q, then for any y with a W-witness, a deterministic selector finds one in at most b queries and O(bq+b) time. Proof: maintain that the current prefix p has a W-witness extension, initially true. Query E(y,p0); append 0 if true, and otherwise append 1. In the latter case a witness extends p by the invariant, and none extends p0, so one extends p1. Thus the invariant persists. After b steps, p is a full-length string and E(y,p)=1 implies W(y,p). This shrinks the exhaustive selector gap to the cost of extension queries; it does not bound that cost for QE* witness sets.

label: S0007
statement: statement: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and let C_y be nonempty for each y in R(X). There exists a decoder D:Y×C→{0,1} satisfying D(R(x),c)=L(x) for all x∈X and c∈C_{R(x)} if and only if L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y∈R(X), define D(y,c) to be the common value of L on R^{-1}(y), independent of c; define D arbitrarily outside R(X). Thus the condition is both necessary and sufficient. It isolates the interface needed for a fiber argument, but does not establish that QE* uses it or that a witness selector is efficient.

Sufficiency: for each y with nonempty fiber, set D(y,c) to the common value of L on that fiber; define D arbitrarily on other y. This characterizes the reduction-only interface; it does not show QE* has that interface or an efficient selector.

label: S0008
statement: statement: Adaptive-cost prefix selector. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and suppose an extension-query procedure E(y,p) correctly decides whether p extends to z∈{0,1}^b with W(y,z). If the i-th adaptive query costs at most q_i, then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic selector outputs such a witness using at most b queries and O(b+Σ_{i=1}^b q_i) time. Proof: initialize p=ε, which has a witness extension. For i=1,…,b, query E(y,p0). If true, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. In the latter case, by induction p had a witness extension and no witness extends p0, so some witness extends p1. Thus the invariant that p has a witness extension is preserved. At length b, p itself is a witness. The query count is b and the total cost is O(b+Σq_i). This gives an exact adaptive cost bound but does not bound those query costs for QE* witnesses or close G0001.

statement: Lemma (explicit-verifier prefix search). Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose a deterministic verifier V(y,z) decides membership in W in at most v steps. Given y for which some z satisfies W(y,z), the greedy prefix selector returns such a z using at most b extension checks. Implement each check for a prefix p by enumerating all suffixes u and testing V(y,p||u). The total number of verifier calls is at most 2^b-1, so the running time is O((2^b-1)(v+b)+b^2), including string handling. Proof: Initially the empty prefix has a witness. At prefix p of length i, test whether p||0 has a witness by enumerating its 2^(b-i-1) completions and applying V. If one succeeds, append 0; otherwise the maintained witness extending p must extend p||1, so append 1. Thus after b steps the resulting full string is in W. There are b checks, and their enumeration sizes sum to sum_{i=0}^{b-1} 2^(b-i-1)=2^b-1. The stated bound follows by charging at most v+b per verifier call and O(b^2) for prefix bookkeeping. Scope: this is an explicit upper bound for directly verifiable witness relations; it is exponential in b and does not establish the QE* resource bounds or close OBL-QE-W.

statement: Restricted witness-selector lemma. Let y be an input and suppose its witnesses are exactly the solutions z∈F₂^b of a given linear system A_y z=c_y. For any prefix p, extendibility is decidable by substituting p into the system and testing consistency by Gaussian elimination. Starting with the empty prefix, query extendibility after appending 0; choose 0 if consistent, and otherwise choose 1. Since the current prefix has a solution extension, one of these choices remains consistent. After b choices the resulting string is a witness. The selector uses at most b consistency tests and polynomial time in the input system size.
evidence: Direct invariant proof: before each choice the current prefix has a solution extension; the two possible next bits partition those extensions, so at least one branch remains consistent. Gaussian elimination decides each branch in polynomial time. This is a restricted subclass only; no link to SearchMCSP witnesses or closure of G0001 has been established.

statement: Black-box prefix-query lower bound. For every b>=0, consider hidden z in {0,1}^b and the oracle E_z(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of z. Any deterministic algorithm that identifies z for every hidden z requires at least b oracle queries in the worst case. Proof: each query returns one bit, so a decision tree of depth q has at most 2^q leaves. Correct identification of all 2^b possible hidden strings requires at least 2^b distinct leaves; hence 2^q >= 2^b and q >= b. The bound is attained by querying the successive prefixes along the hidden string, as in prefix self-reduction. Scope: black-box query complexity only; it gives no lower bound on the cost of computing a QE* extension predicate.
proof: Fix b and suppose a deterministic algorithm identifies every hidden z using at most q queries. Its interaction tree has branching factor at most two and depth at most q, hence at most 2^q leaves. Two different hidden strings cannot reach the same leaf, because the algorithm would then output the same string on both and be wrong on at least one. Therefore the tree has at least 2^b leaves, so q>=b. Querying prefixes incrementally identifies z in b queries, proving tightness.

Two different hidden strings cannot reach the same leaf, because the algorithm would then output the same string on both and be wrong on at least one. Therefore the tree has at least 2^b leaves, so q>=b. Querying prefixes incrementally identifies z in b queries, proving tightness.

label: S0014
statement: statement: Layered-DAG witness search. Let G=(V,E) be an explicitly supplied directed acyclic graph with layers V_0,...,V_b, edges only from V_i to V_{i+1}, source s in V_0, and accepting set A subseteq V_b. Backward marking decides whether s reaches A in O(|V|+|E|) time; if so, following marked successors outputs a path in O(b) additional time. Proof: mark A; for i=b-1 down to 0 mark v in V_i iff it has an edge to a marked vertex in V_{i+1}. By backward induction a vertex is marked exactly when it has a path to A. Hence s is marked iff a witness path exists. At each marked vertex before V_b choose a marked successor, which yields an accepting path. Each vertex and edge is scanned at most constantly many times. Scope: explicit layered-DAG representation only; no such representation is established for the QE* witness relation.

statement: statement: Depth-sensitive prefix selector lemma. Let Y be a finite set, b≥0, and W⊆Y×{0,1}^b. For each y and prefix p of length i≤b, define E(y,p)=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^b extending p satisfies (y,z)∈W. Suppose an exact deterministic procedure answers every E(y,p) query at depth i in time at most q_i. Then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic algorithm outputs such a witness in at most b queries and time at most Σ_{i=0}^{b-1}q_i+O(b), plus output handling. Proof: initialize p=ε; by hypothesis E(y,ε)=1. At depth i<b query E(y,p0). If it is 1, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. The invariant E(y,p)=1 is preserved: in the second case some witness extends p, and none extends p0, so every witness extending p must extend p1. After b iterations p has length b and E(y,p)=1, which by definition means (y,p)∈W. The time bound is the sum of the b query bounds and O(1) per query/update. If b=0, the premise E(y,ε)=1 directly gives (y,ε)∈W and the empty sum applies.

statement: statement: Exhaustive suffix implementation of prefix extension. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and let V(y,z) decide membership in W in time at most v for every y,z. At a prefix p of length i<b, E(y,p) can be computed by enumerating all 2^(b−i) suffixes and applying V, in time at most 2^(b−i)v plus enumeration overhead. Consequently, the prefix selector that tests E(y,p0) at depths i=0,…,b−1 finds a witness whenever one exists, using at most (2^b−1)v verifier time plus enumeration and selector overhead. Proof: For each tested p0 at depth i, exactly 2^(b−i−1) strings extend p0, so the verifier work summed over depths is v·Σ_{i=0}^{b−1}2^(b−i−1)=v(2^b−1). Each query is exact by exhaustive enumeration. The selector preserves the invariant that its current prefix has a W-witness extension: if p0 has one, append 0; otherwise, since p has one, a witness extends p1. After b choices the full string is a witness. For b=0, no suffix queries are needed and the initial empty prefix is already a witness under the premise. Scope: this is conditional on the stated verifier and gives an exponential exhaustive implementation; it establishes no useful QE* resource bound and closes no QE* reduction obligation.

label: S0017
statement: statement: Explicit-witness-list selector bound. Let b be a nonnegative integer and let W be a nonempty explicitly listed subset of {0,1}^b, with L=|W|. A deterministic algorithm returns a member of W using at most b prefix-extension queries, each answered by scanning the list, in O(b^2 L) bit comparisons and O(b) extension queries. Proof: initialize the empty prefix p. For each i=0,...,b-1, scan W to determine whether some w in W has prefix p0. If so set p:=p0; otherwise set p:=p1. Inductively p is a prefix of some member of W: this holds initially; if the scan finds an extension by 0 it remains true, and if not, the maintained witness must extend by 1. After b iterations p is a length-b member of W. Each iteration compares at most L strings against a prefix of length at most b, costing O(bL), hence the total O(b^2L). The algorithm is correct for all nonempty W, including b=0, where W={empty string} and no scans are needed.

statement: statement: Prefix-count selector lemma. Let Y be finite, b≥0, and W⊆Y×{0,1}^b. Define the prefix-count oracle C(y,p)=|{z∈{0,1}^b : W(y,z) and p is a prefix of z}|. For any y with C(y,ε)>0, a deterministic algorithm finds z with W(y,z) using at most b oracle queries: at each step, query C(y,p0), append 0 if the answer is positive, and otherwise append 1. Proof: maintain C(y,p)>0, true initially by hypothesis. If C(y,p0)>0, the invariant holds after appending 0. Otherwise, since every extension of p begins with either 0 or 1 and C(y,p)>0, C(y,p1)=C(y,p)>0, so it holds after appending 1. After b steps p has length b; its only length-b extension is itself, hence C(y,p)>0 implies W(y,p). This includes b=0, where the initial positive count already certifies the empty string. The lemma reduces witness selection to exact prefix counting; it gives no resource bound for implementing that counting oracle for QE* witnesses.

statement: statement: Prefix-extension selector interface lemma. Let b be a nonnegative integer, Y any set, W a subset of Y × {0,1}^b, and E(y,p)=1 exactly when there exists z∈{0,1}^b extending p with (y,z)∈W. For each fixed y with a W-witness, the following deterministic procedure outputs z with (y,z)∈W using at most b calls to E and O(b) additional bit operations: start with p=ε; for i=1,…,b query E(y,p0); if the answer is 1 set p←p0, otherwise set p←p1; output p. Proof: inductively, before iteration i, p is a length-(i−1) prefix having at least one W-extension. Initially this holds by the assumed witness. If E(y,p0)=1 then p0 has an extension; if it is 0, the maintained existence of an extension of p implies that every such extension begins with 1, so p1 has an extension. Thus the invariant holds after each iteration. At i=b, the length-b string p is its own only extension, hence (y,p)∈W. There is one E query per bit and only linear work to append/read bits. Scope: exact deterministic search conditional on an exact extension predicate; it does not bound E's computation time/space or prove that QE* supplies E within its resource limits.

label: S0020
statement: statement: Fixed-fiber advice-pattern capacity. Let F be any finite set, s>=0, and D:{0,1}^s x F->{0,1}. Define P_a:F->{0,1} by P_a(x)=D(a,x). Then |{P_a:a in {0,1}^s}|<=2^s. Proof: the map a |-> P_a has domain {0,1}^s, which has cardinality 2^s; its image therefore has cardinality at most 2^s. In particular, any labeling of F outside this family cannot be represented by this fixed decoder with s advice bits. Scope: a capacity bound for decoders whose varying input across F is only a; it does not imply label constancy, efficient advice construction, or a QE* reduction.

label: S0021
statement: statement: Constructive missing-label consequence of fixed-decoder capacity. Let F be a finite set with |F|=f, s>=0, and D:{0,1}^s x F->{0,1} be fixed. If s<f, there exists a labeling L:F->{0,1} that no advice string realizes, and it can be found by enumerating the 2^f labelings and rejecting those among P_a(x)=D(a,x), in at most 2^f * 2^s * f bit evaluations plus lexicographic bookkeeping. Proof: the image family P={P_a} has size at most 2^s, while the set of all labelings has size 2^f. Since s<f, 2^s<2^f, so P is a proper subset. Enumerate labelings in lexicographic order, compare each to all P_a, and return the first absent pattern; at least one exists by the strict cardinality inequality. This is a constructive finite decoder lower bound only. It does not apply to OBL-QE-W's decoder D(x,W), where x is an additional varying input, and closes no QE* obligation.

statement: Deterministic bounded-witness selector lemma. Let X,Y be finite sets, R:X→Y, and L:X→{0,1}. Suppose each relevant T has at least one witness w of length at most b(T), and a deterministic verifier V(T,w) accepts exactly the admissible witnesses in time at most v(T). Suppose D(x,w) runs in time at most d(x) and equals L(x) for every x and every admissible witness of R(x). Then L is decidable by enumerating all strings w of length at most b(R(x)), returning the first accepted witness, and applying D. The running time is at most (2^{b+1}-1)v(R(x))+d(x)+time(R), where b=max_T b(T) over the relevant outputs. In particular, this gives a polynomial-time decision procedure when these quantities and 2^b are polynomially bounded. Proof: for T=R(x), the enumeration includes an admissible witness by hypothesis; exactness of V ensures the selected string is admissible. The universal correctness assumption on D then gives D(x,w)=L(x). The time bound counts every tested string and the final decoder call. This lemma requires deterministic verification within the stated bound; witness length alone does not imply efficient selection.
proof: As stated in the step: exhaustive enumeration covers all strings of length at most b, exact verification returns an admissible witness because one exists, and universal decoder correctness gives the answer. Summing the verifier costs and decoder/reduction costs yields the bound.

label: S0023
statement: statement: Tight black-box query bound for prefix-extension search. For each integer b >= 0, let the hidden witness be z in {0,1}^b and give a deterministic algorithm oracle access only to E_z(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of z, for arbitrary binary strings p (including the empty string). If the algorithm must output z correctly for every hidden z, then its worst-case number of oracle queries is at least b. The bound is attained by querying the b prefixes 0, 1, ..., z_{<b}0 successively as in the standard bit-by-bit selector (for b=0, output the empty string with zero queries). Proof: The oracle E_z is exactly membership in the set of prefixes of z. Any deterministic algorithm making at most q yes/no queries has at most 2^q possible answer transcripts and hence at most 2^q possible outputs as functions of the transcript. Correctness for all 2^b possible z requires at least 2^b distinct output transcripts, so 2^q >= 2^b and q >= b. Conversely, after a known prefix p of z, query E_z(p0); append 0 on yes and 1 on no. This identifies each next bit in one query, yielding z in b queries. Scope: black-box query complexity only; the oracle may be computationally expensive, so this gives no QE* resource bound and does not show the extension predicate itself is hard.

statement: Hidden-singleton prefix-query complexity. For every integer b>=1, let an unknown witness w range over {0,1}^b, and let the only allowed query be E(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of w, for any binary string p of length at most b. Any deterministic adaptive algorithm that identifies w for every possible w requires at least b queries in the worst case; querying the prefixes of lengths 1,...,b achieves b queries.
proof: For the lower bound, consider the binary decision tree of a deterministic algorithm. Each query has two possible answers, so a depth-d tree has at most 2^d leaves. Correct identification of each of the 2^b possible witnesses requires at least 2^b distinct leaves, hence d>=b. For the upper bound, query the length-i prefix of the bits already recovered followed by 0, for i=1,...,b. A yes answer sets bit i to 0; a no answer sets it to 1, since the hidden witness is known to exist and its preceding bits have already been recovered. After b queries all bits are determined.
scope: Exact deterministic worst-case query complexity in the hidden-singleton prefix-membership oracle model. It does not establish that a QE* witness relation is hidden, singleton-valued, or inaccessible by other computations, so it does not close the QE* obligation.
diagnostic: The oracle property is relativizing and localizing; the argument is combinatorial and does not yield a natural property or algebraic circuit lower bound. No P!=NP progress is claimed.

statement:
statement_start: Conditional rank lemma for minimal unsatisfiable positive exact-one systems. Let E be a finite minimal unsatisfiable family of clauses, each on three distinct variables, and let A_E be its incidence matrix over F_3 on the occurring variables. If A_E z = 1 is solvable over F_3, then rank(A_E)=|E| and |E|≤n′−1.
proof: Suppose the rows are dependent: choose coefficients λ_i, not all zero, with Σ_i λ_i r_i=0, and choose j with λ_j≠0. A solution z to A_E z=1 gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. For any Boolean assignment x satisfying every clause other than j, the dependence gives λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i(r_i·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j in F_3, so r_j·x=1 mod 3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in clause j is in {0,1,2,3}; the only value congruent to 1 mod 3 is 1. Thus x also satisfies clause j, contradicting minimal unsatisfiability. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A_E)=|E|. Every row sums to 3=0 in F_3, so the nonzero all-ones vector on the n′ occurring variables lies in ker(A_E); rank-nullity yields |E|≤n′−1. For the cited four clauses on four variables, each column sum is 3=0 while the RHS sum is 4=1, so A_E z=1 is inconsistent; that example does not refute this conditional lemma.

statement:
statement_start: Let E be a finite inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable family of positive exact-one clauses, each on three distinct occurring variables, and let A be its incidence matrix over F_3. If Az=1 is solvable, then rank_F3(A)=|E| and |E|≤n'−1.
proof: Write the rows as r_i. Suppose they are dependent, with coefficients λ_i∈F_3 not all zero, and choose j with λ_j≠0. From Σ_i λ_i r_i=0 and Az=1, dotting with z gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. Inclusion-minimal unsatisfiability ensures E\{C_j} is satisfiable; choose a Boolean assignment x satisfying all its clauses. Dotting the row dependence with x gives 0=Σ_i λ_i(r_i·x)=λ_j(r_j·x)+Σ_{i≠j}λ_i, since r_i·x=1 for i≠j. Thus λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j, so r_j·x=1 in F_3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in C_j belongs to {0,1,2,3}; its only value congruent to 1 modulo 3 is 1. Hence x satisfies C_j too, contradicting that E is unsatisfiable. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A)=|E|. Each row has exactly three 1s, so A times the all-ones vector is zero in F_3. This vector is nonzero because n'≥3, hence nullity(A)≥1. Rank-nullity gives |E|=rank(A)≤n'−1. For the proposed four-clause instance on four variables, each column sum is 3≡0 while the four right-hand sides sum to 4≡1. Summing its equations would imply 0=1, so that instance violates the solvability premise and does not refute this conditional lemma.

statement:
statement: For every De Morgan formula Phi with each variable occurring at most once, and every restriction distribution under which each variable is live with probability p, if L(Phi|rho) is the number of variable-leaf occurrences after restriction and size-nonincreasing simplification, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= p L(Phi).
proof: Let I_i be the indicator that variable x_i is live. Since each variable occurs at most once, before simplification the number of live variable leaves is exactly sum_i I_i. The stipulated simplification does not increase the number of variable leaves, so pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i. Taking expectations and using linearity, E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = p L(Phi). No independence is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas; variable-leaf count; restrictions with uniform marginal live probability p; simplification must not increase formula size.

label: S0002
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L variable-leaf occurrences, each variable occurring at most once. Let rho be any random restriction, and for each leaf i let p_i be the probability that its variable remains live. If L(Phi|rho) counts variable-leaf occurrences after restriction followed by simplification that never increases that count, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_{i=1}^L p_i.
proof: For each leaf i define I_i(rho)=1 if its variable remains live and 0 otherwise. Before simplification the number of live variable leaves is exactly sum_i I_i because Phi is read-once. By the stipulated simplification rule, pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i(rho). Taking expectations and applying linearity gives E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = sum_i p_i. No independence among the live indicators is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas, variable-leaf occurrence count, arbitrary random restrictions with possibly different live probabilities by leaf, and simplifications that do not increase that count.

label: S0003
statement: statement: Let N≥2 and Φ be a formula tree with L input-variable leaf occurrences. Under any random restriction, suppose every input leaf remains live with probability p=N^{-a_N}, where a_N≥0. Let X be the number of surviving input-leaf occurrences before simplification, and X' any count after a simplification that only deletes leaves. Then E[X']≤pL=N^{a_N}p²L. In particular, if a_N→0, the pL bound is absorbed into N^{o(1)}p²L. Proof: write X=Σ_{j=1}^L I_j for the leaf survival indicators. Pointwise X'≤X, so linearity gives E[X']≤E[X]=Σ_j E[I_j]=pL. Since p=N^{-a_N}, pL=N^{a_N}p²L, and N^{a_N}=N^{o(1)} when a_N→0. No independence assumption is needed. This repairs the single-leaf obstruction only in the stated lower-marginal regime; it gives no bound on residual formula size or reused-gate leaves.

label: S0004
statement:
statement: Let C be a finite acyclic Boolean circuit DAG with g gate nodes, and let rho assign constants to any subset of its input variables. Perform semantics-preserving constant propagation by processing nodes topologically, replacing any gate whose output is determined by a constant and redirecting references to it. The resulting DAG has at most g gate nodes. If this DAG is unfolded into a formula tree, its gate-occurrence count equals the sum, over surviving DAG nodes v, of the number of occurrences of v in that unfolding.
proof: Process the original nodes in topological order. Each node is either retained as one gate or replaced by a constant; redirects change edges and create no nodes. Thus the resulting DAG has no more gate nodes than the original. In the unfolding, each tree occurrence is a copy of exactly one DAG node. Partitioning the tree's gate occurrences according to their source DAG node gives the stated sum.
scope: DAG gate count after constant propagation and the definitional identity for formula unfolding multiplicities. This does not bound the multiplicities or their expectation under any restriction, and does not close the route's almost-formula correlation obligation.

statement: LEMMA (anti-concentration over subset sums). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, x_j iid uniform in {0,1}, c = sum a_j x_j. For integers a and L >= 0: P(c in {a,...,a+L-1}) <= L*C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= L/sqrt(N). PROOF: Erdos (1945): for reals |a_j|>=1, any open interval J of length 1 contains the subset sums of at most C(N,floor(N/2)) subsets. Each integer v lies in the open interval (v-1/2, v+1/2), so #{S : c_S = v} <= C(N,floor(N/2)); sum over the L integers and divide by 2^N. For the second inequality use C(2k,k) <= 4^k/sqrt(pi k): if N=2k then pi k = pi N/2 >= N; if N=2k+1 then C(2k+1,k) = C(2k+2,k+1)/2 <= 4^{k+1}/(2 sqrt(pi(k+1))), so the ratio is <= 1/sqrt(pi(k+1)) <= 1/sqrt(2k+1). COROLLARY (bottom gate). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integers |w_j| <= B, R a set of r variables, F the rest, c = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j. Put lo = sum_{j in R} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in R} max(w_j,0). Then g is decided under the restriction (constant over all completions of x_R) iff c >= t-lo or c < t-hi. So g is undecided iff t-hi <= c < t-lo, an integer window of exactly L = hi-lo = sum_{j in R}|w_j| <= rB integers. Applying the lemma with N = N_F gives P_{x_F}(undecided) <= min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F)). Summing over the m bottom gates gives E[#undecided] <= sum_g min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F(g))). SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the bound is worst-case over weights with |w|<=B and integer; it needs many nonzero free weights (N_F large) and says nothing for sparse gates; it bounds only the bottom layer; no running time follows yet (the top gate is not handled). KNOWLEDGE vs ALGORITHMIC: knowledge = the restriction bound with its threshold r ~ sqrt(n)/B (explains the refuted fixed-p experiments: for r = pn the bound is ~pB sqrt(n) >= 1); algorithmic gain = none yet. NOVELTY: the Erdos theorem is classical; the new content is the application to restricted THR gates and the regime boundary. The exact per-gate check is run in the next computation.

structure.lemma: Restriction lemma for bottom THR gates (Erdos-Littlewood-Offord form): for integer weights |w_j| <= B, a set R of r variables, and x_F uniform on the rest, P(gate undecided) <= min(1, sum_{j in R}|w_j| / sqrt(N_F)) <= rB / sqrt(N_F), where N_F = #{j in F: w_j != 0}. In particular the undecided fraction is O(rB/sqrt(n)) when N_F >= n/2, so it tends to 0 for r = o(sqrt n). The regime r ~ sqrt(n)/B is the threshold where the bound stops being useful.
