structure.lemma: Theorem C (bounded-weight switching bound for one bottom THR gate). Setting: g(x)=[sum_i w_i x_i >= t] on {0,1}^n, integer weights, nz = number of nonzero weights, M = max|w_i| >= 1. Random restriction R_p: each variable free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Claim: for 0 < p <= 1/4, P(restricted g is non-constant) <= exp(-p nz/3) + 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Corollary: p = 1/(16 M sqrt(nz)) with sqrt(nz) >= 126 M gives P(non-constant) <= 1/4. Proof: Lemma A (Sperner): for nonzero integers a_1..a_k and uniform eps in {0,1}^k, P(sum a_i eps_i = v) <= C(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for every v (flip eps_i where a_i<0; the sets with a given sum form an antichain). Lemma B: given the free set F, the non-constancy window of the restriction lemma has W_F integers, so P(non-constant | F) <= W_F/sqrt(k) <= M s/sqrt(k), with s = number of free nonzero-weight variables and k = nz - s >= 1. Chernoff: P(s > 2 p nz) <= exp(-p nz/3). On s <= 2 p nz (and p <= 1/4) we have k >= nz/2, giving conditional bound 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Take the expectation over s.
structure.proved_step: Theorem C as stated in the lemma field, proof by Lemma A (Sperner), Lemma B (window count) and Chernoff; independent exact check submitted this turn (see experiment record)

label: S0010
statement:
LEMMA (Exact undecided probability under random restriction with uniform threshold). Let g(x) = [∑_{i=1}^n w_i x_i ≥ t] be a threshold gate with integer weights w_i, S = ∑ |w_i|. Let R_p be the random restriction: each variable is free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Let the threshold t be chosen uniformly from {t_min, ..., t_max} where the interval length L = t_max - t_min + 1 satisfies L ≥ S (in particular, t uniform on [-S, S] works). Then P_{R_p, t}[g|R_p is non-constant] ≤ p, with equality when L = S and the threshold range matches the possible sums exactly.

PROOF. For a fixed restriction ρ, let F be the set of free variables. The restricted gate is g_ρ(y) = [∑_{i∈F} w_i y_i ≥ t - ∑_{i∉F} w_i ρ(i)]. This is non-constant iff the threshold t falls in the interval I_ρ = (L_ρ, U_ρ] where L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i<0} w_i, U_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i>0} w_i. The length of I_ρ is U_ρ - L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F} |w_i| =: W_F. Since t is uniform over an interval of length L ≥ S ≥ W_F, P_t[g_ρ non-constant] = W_F / L ≤ W_F / S. Now take expectation over R_p: E[W_F] = ∑_i |w_i| · P(i free) = p S. Thus P_{R_p,t}[undecided] = E[W_F/L] ≤ E[W_F/S] = p. Equality holds when L = S and the threshold distribution is uniform over exactly S+1 consecutive integers covering the full range of possible sums. ∎

If R2 holds then P(nonconst) <= C' p sqrt(nz), which is the candidate per-gate bound and gives the k/sqrt(n) shape of G0001 when p = k/n. Support so far: numerical only (desk test in progress). structure.lemma: Lemma R1 (Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction, unbounded weights). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, each j free independently with prob p, F = free set, L_F = sum_{j in F}|a_j|, S_F = sum_{j not in F} min(a_j^2, L_F^2). Then P(gate nonconstant) <= sqrt(8) * A * E_F[min(1, L_F / sqrt(S_F))], where A is the universal Kolmogorov-Rogozin constant. Proof: condition on F. Nonconstancy means X = sum_{j not in F} a_j u_j (u_j iid uniform bits) lies in a window of exactly L_F consecutive integers. Apply Rogozin with L = L_F and L_j = min(|a_j|/2, L). Each X_j = a_j u_j has Q_j(L_j) <= 1/2, since an interval of length < |a_j| contains at most one of {0, a_j}. Hence sum L_j^2 (1 - Q_j) >= (1/8) S_F, which gives the bound.
structure.proved_step: Lemma R1 as stated in the lemma field: Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction of the unbounded-weight restriction probability to the expectation in F of min(1, L_F/sqrt(S_F)).

label: S0018
statement: Lemma (heavy-split restriction bound, repair of G0008). Setting: g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t], integer weights w_j, any integer t, n variables, nz = #{j : w_j != 0}. Fix tau >= 1 and H = #{j : |w_j| > tau}. Let F be a uniform k-subset of variables, 1 <= k <= nz/2, and fix the other variables to uniform bits. Then P[restriction of g is non-constant] <= k*H/n + A*(tau*k + 1)*sqrt(2/(nz - k)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality (cited; exact constant and statement to be source-checked). Proof: (1) Let E = {F contains a heavy variable}. P(E) <= E[#heavy in F] = k*H/n by a union bound. (2) On the complement of E, every j in F has |w_j| <= tau, so W_F := sum_{j in F} |w_j| <= tau*k. (3) Given F, the restriction is non-constant iff c := sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in the integer window [t - hi, t - lo), where hi, lo are the positive and negative parts summed over F; this window has W_F integer points. (4) Let r = #{j not in F : w_j != 0} >= nz - k. Each summand w_j x_j takes values 0 and w_j, so its sup-probability on any half-open integer interval of length 1 is at most 1/2. Kolmogorov-Rogozin with scales l_j = 1 gives sup_x P(c in [x, x+L)) <= A*L/sqrt(r/2) for L >= 1; with L = W_F + 1 this is <= A*(W_F+1)*sqrt(2/r) <= A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)) on the complement of E. (5) Combine: P(nonconst) <= P(E) + sup over the complement = k*H/n + A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)). QED (modulo source-check of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin statement). The bound does not depend on the maximum weight M.

Worst per-F ratio P*sqrt(r/2)/(W_F+1) = 0.306, consistent with A = 1. Worst ratio of averaged P(nonconst) to the full bound (capped at 1) = 0.875. Zero violations of the full bound. Finite evidence only; it does not establish A.

(3) Given F, the restriction is non-constant iff c := sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in the integer window [t - hi, t - lo), where hi, lo are the positive and negative parts summed over F; this window has W_F integer points. (4) Let r = #{j not in F : w_j != 0} >= nz - k. Each summand w_j x_j takes values 0 and w_j, so its sup-probability on any half-open integer interval of length 1 is at most 1/2. Kolmogorov-Rogozin with scales l_j = 1 gives sup_x P(c in [x, x+L)) <= A*L/sqrt(r/2) for L >= 1; with L = W_F + 1 this is <= A*(W_F+1)*sqrt(2/r) <= A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)) on the complement of E. (5) Combine: P(nonconst) <= P(E) + sup over the complement = k*H/n + A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)). QED (modulo source-check of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin statement). The bound does not depend on the maximum weight M.

label: S0021
statement: Lemma (exact unit-weight average, lane C). Let g(x) = [x_1 + ... + x_n >= t] with all weights 1. Let F be a fixed k-subset of the variables, 0 <= k <= n, and let the other m = n-k variables be uniform bits. Let t be uniform on the 2n+1 integers -n..n. Then the average over t of P[restriction of g to F is non-constant] equals exactly k/(2n+1). Proof: let c = sum of the m free bits, so 0 <= c <= m. Let s = number of ones in F, 0 <= s <= k. The restriction is non-constant iff c < t <= c+k, i.e. c in [t-k, t-1]. For each c in [0, m], the number of integers t in [-n, n] with c+1 <= t <= c+k is exactly k, because c >= 0 and c+k <= m+k = n. Summing over t and averaging over c gives k/(2n+1). QED. Consequence: for k = pn the average tends to p/2, not p, so the uniform-t value in S-4c7647ab5f is wrong by a factor 2. The lemma is an identity, not a bound. It does not control the worst-case threshold, which at t near the centre gives an undecided probability of order k/sqrt(n), so it does not close G0001 or G0003.

label: S0023
statement: LEMMA R (window bound, arbitrary integer weights, uniform in the threshold). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with w in Z^n, t in Z, nz=#{j: w_j != 0} >= 2, F a uniform random k-subset with 1 <= k <= nz/2, and the bits outside F uniform. Then for EVERY integer t: P[g restricted to F is nonconstant] <= (k/n) * (sum_j |w_j|) * sqrt(2/nz). PROOF. (1) Fix F. Put lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|, and c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j. The restriction is nonconstant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, i.e. c lies in a window of exactly W_F consecutive integers. (2) Let r = #{j not in F: w_j != 0} >= nz - k >= nz/2. Replace x_j by 1 - x_j for each j not in F with w_j < 0 (a bijection of bit strings). Then c becomes sum_J a_j y_j over r indices with a_j = |w_j| > 0. For each fixed value v, the sets J with sum_{j in J} a_j = v form an antichain (A strictly inside B forces a strictly smaller sum), so by Sperner P[c = v | F] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r). (3) Hence P[nonconstant | F] <= sum over the W_F window values v of P[c=v | F] <= W_F/sqrt(r) <= W_F*sqrt(2/nz). (4) P[j in F] = k/n gives E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_j |w_j|. Taking the expectation over F proves the claim. QED. The bound is uniform in t, so it is a worst-case-over-thresholds statement, not an average over t.

label: S0025
statement: LEMMA (exact threshold-averaged restriction count). Let w in (Z minus {0})^n, S_lo = sum_j min(w_j,0), S_hi = sum_j max(w_j,0), L = S_hi - S_lo = sum_j |w_j|. Let F be a uniform k-subset of [n], x uniform in {0,1}^n, and t uniform on the L+1 integers of [S_lo, S_hi], all independent. Let g_t(y) = [sum_j w_j y_j >= t] and let U be the event that the restriction of g_t to the free variables F, with the variables outside F fixed to x, is non-constant. Then P[U] = (k/n) * L/(L+1) exactly. PROOF: fix F and x, put c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j, lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|. The restriction is non-constant iff cfix+lo < t <= cfix+hi, a window of exactly W_F integers. Since c+lo >= S_lo and c+hi <= S_hi, the window lies inside [S_lo, S_hi]. Hence P_t[U | F,x] = W_F/(L+1). Taking E over F with P[j in F] = k/n gives E[W_F] = (k/n) L. SCOPE: averaged over uniform t only. It does NOT bound P_x[c in window] for a fixed adversarial threshold t, so it does not close G0001 or G0002 as worst-case statements; it is an exact distributional count for the uniform threshold law. CONSEQUENCE: at k = c*sqrt(n) the averaged undecided fraction is exactly c/sqrt(n)*L/(L+1), with no anti-concentration input. The Sperner-type bound of Theorem C is needed only for fixed t.

label: S0030
statement: LEMMA (gcd-refined window bound, one THR gate, per fixed free set). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F a set of variables, and out = complement of F. Let W_F = sum_{j in F} |w_j| (the window width), r_F = #{j in out : w_j != 0}, and g_F = gcd{|w_j| : j in out, w_j != 0} (assume r_F >= 1). Then, for uniform independent bits on out and any fixed assignment of F, P[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= (floor(W_F/g_F) + 1)/sqrt(r_F). PROOF. (i) Non-constancy: let lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0). The F-part of the sum takes its minimum lo and maximum hi, so the restriction is non-constant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, where c = sum_{j in out} w_j x_j. (ii) Sperner: write y_j = x_j if w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j if w_j < 0. Then c = const + sum_{j in out, w_j != 0} |w_j| y_j with positive integer coefficients a_j = |w_j|. For a fixed value v the set {S : sum_{j in S} a_j = v} is an antichain of subsets of the r_F free positions, so P[c = v] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) (the central-binomial inequality holds for every r >= 1). (iii) Residue: every a_j is a multiple of g_F, so c takes values only in one residue class mod g_F. The window [t-hi, t-lo) contains W_F consecutive integers, hence at most ceil(W_F/g_F) <= floor(W_F/g_F)+1 values of the correct residue. Summing (ii) over these values gives P[nonconst | F] <= (floor(W_F/g_F)+1)/sqrt(r_F). QED. Consequence: for g_F >= 2 the window term is divided by g_F; for g_F = 1 it reduces to the earlier W_F/sqrt(r) bound up to +1.

structure.lemma: L2-window lemma (per gate, conditional on F). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F subset [n] fixed, x_F fixed, x_O uniform in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let WF = sum_{j in F}|w_j| >= 1 and Neff(F) = sum_{j not in F, w_j != 0} min(|w_j|, WF)^2. Then P_{x_O}[g|F nonconstant] <= sqrt(2)*A*WF/sqrt(Neff(F)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality Q(S;L) <= A*L*(sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q(X_j;l_j)))^{-1/2} (0<l_j<=L). Proof: nonconstancy means the shift c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in a window of WF consecutive integers, so the probability is at most Q(c;WF). Take l_j = min(|w_j|, WF) <= WF. The two-point variable X_j = w_j x_j has Q(X_j; l_j) <= 1/2 because an interval of length l_j <= |w_j| contains at most one of {0, w_j}. So sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q_j) >= Neff/2 and the inequality gives the bound. The constant is scale-invariant in w.

label: S0034
statement:
PROOF. Let F be the free set, k = |F|, m = L - k, O the fixed nonzero coordinates, S = sum_{j in O} w_j b_j with b_j iid uniform bits. (1) For fixed F, the free sum V = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j takes every integer in [minV, maxV], with maxV - minV = k (unit weights: toggle one coordinate at a time). So g is nonconstant iff minV + S < t <= maxV + S, i.e. S lies in an integer interval of exactly k integers. (2) Writing -b_j = (1-b_j) - 1 for w_j = -1 gives S = Bin(m,1/2) + const, so max_a Pr[S=a] = q(m) := C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m. Hence Pr[nonconst | F] <= min(1, k q(m)). (3) q(m) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))) for m >= 2: for m = 2r, q = C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) (Wallis); for m = 2r+1, q(m) = q(2r)(2r+1)/(2r+2) <= q(2r). (4) If L >= 4 and k <= L/2 then m >= L/2 >= 2, m-1 >= L/4, so q(m) <= sqrt(8/(pi L)) <= 2/sqrt(L). (5) Average over k ~ Bin(L,p): E[min(1,k q(L-k)); k <= L/2] <= 2 E[k]/sqrt(L) = 2pL/sqrt(L) = 2p sqrt(L). The event k >= j, j = floor(L/2)+1 >= L/2, has probability <= C(L,j) p^j <= (eL/j)^j p^j <= (2ep)^j. Summing gives the claim. QED.
CONSEQUENCE: with p = delta/sqrt(n) (free set of size o(sqrt n) in expectation) the undecided probability of a bottom gate is <= 2 delta + o(1). For p constant the bound is trivial (>= 1). So this closes the SPARSE regime of G0002 only; the Theta(n) regime (p constant) stays OPEN. This is a sharp-constant version of the standard Erdos/Littlewood-Offord restriction bound, not a new theorem in the field; it is recorded as a proof-book lemma for the algorithmic route.

(3) q(m) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))) for m >= 2: for m = 2r, q = C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) (Wallis); for m = 2r+1, q(m) = q(2r)(2r+1)/(2r+2) <= q(2r). (4) If L >= 4 and k <= L/2 then m >= L/2 >= 2, m-1 >= L/4, so q(m) <= sqrt(8/(pi L)) <= 2/sqrt(L). (5) Average over k ~ Bin(L,p): E[min(1,k q(L-k)); k <= L/2] <= 2 E[k]/sqrt(L) = 2pL/sqrt(L) = 2p sqrt(L). The event k >= j, j = floor(L/2)+1 >= L/2, has probability <= C(L,j) p^j <= (eL/j)^j p^j <= (2ep)^j. Summing gives the claim. QED.
CONSEQUENCE: with p = delta/sqrt(n) (free set of size o(sqrt n) in expectation) the undecided probability of a bottom gate is <= 2 delta + o(1). For p constant the bound is trivial (>= 1). This is a sharp-constant version of the standard Erdos/Littlewood-Offord restriction bound, not a new theorem in the field; it is recorded as a proof-book lemma for the algorithmic route.

label: S0051
statement: LEMMA U (adversarial threshold, unit weights). Let n >= 2, p in (0,1), pn >= 2. Random restriction: each variable is free with probability p, otherwise fixed to 1 or to 0 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Single gate with w_i = 1 for all i and threshold t = ceil(n/2). Let a = number of variables fixed to 1, f = number free. The gate is undecided iff a < t <= a+f. Then P(undecided) >= 1 - 2*exp(-2*(pn/2 - 1)^2 / n). Proof: a is Bin(n, (1-p)/2) with mean (1-p)n/2; a >= t forces a - E[a] >= pn/2 - 1. a+f is Bin(n, (1+p)/2) with mean (1+p)n/2; a+f < t <= n/2 + 1/2 forces (E - value) >= pn/2 - 1. Hoeffding on each event gives the bound. Scope: one unit-weight gate, one threshold; it refutes the adversarial-threshold form of the p-bound (max_t P(undecided) <= p) for p >> 1/sqrt(n). It does not address random thresholds or general weights.

statement: LEMMA (random restriction, +-1 weights, ANY fixed threshold). Let n>=2, w in {-1,+1}^n, 0<p<=1/4. Random restriction: each variable is free (in F) independently with prob p; for i not in F the bit a_i is uniform in {0,1}, independent of F. For a FIXED integer t, let mn = sum_i min(0,w_i a_i) over i not in F plus sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), and mx analogously with max; gate undecided iff mn < t <= mx. Then P_{F,a}[undecided] <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) (about 4.24 p sqrt n). PROOF. Fix F, let s=|F|, k=n-s. (1) mx-mn = s, so the set of values of base = sum_{i not in F} w_i a_i that make the gate undecided is a set of s consecutive integers. (2) Substitute b_i = 1-a_i for the k' indices with w_i=-1: base = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} b_i - const, a sum of k independent uniform bits plus a constant. (3) Sperner/Erdos: max_x P(Bin(k,1/2)=x) = C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for k>=1 (even k: C(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m); odd k: the extra factor (2m+1)/(2m+2) <= 1 and 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) for m>=1; k=1 gives 1/2). Hence P(undecided | F) <= min(1, s/sqrt(k)) for k>=1, and <= 1 for k=0. (4) Average over F. Region A = {s <= n/2}: k >= n/2, so s/sqrt(k) <= s*sqrt(2/n); E[s] = pn gives contribution <= p*sqrt(2n). Region B = {s > n/2}: its probability is <= sum over |F|>=n/2 of p^{|F|} <= 2^n p^{n/2} = p * (2^n p^{n/2-1}) <= p * 2^n * 4^{-(n/2-1)} = 4p (using p<=1/4 and n/2-1>=0). Total <= p*sqrt(2n) + 4p = p*sqrt(n)*(sqrt(2)+4/sqrt(n)) <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) for n>=2. QED. NOTE: the window bound is for an ADVERSARIAL fixed t; the uniform-t version (proof-state lemma above) is weaker and elementary. The random-a assumption is needed: the OR-gate example with all fixed bits 0 (exact, cm-33cf0317f7794fa7) has P/p ~ 0.79 sqrt(n) at p=1/n, which is consistent with the bound.

label: S0072
statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (+-1 weights, single THR gate, hand proof). Let w in {-1,0,1}^n have s >= 1 nonzero entries, t in Z fixed, F a random free set (each variable free independently with prob p), and a_i uniform in {0,1} on the non-free nonzero variables. Then P(gate non-constant after restriction) <= sqrt(2s) * p. Proof: (1) Given F, with k = |F cap supp(w)|, m = s - k, the gate is non-constant iff c in [t - kp, t + kn - 1], where kp, kn are the free positive and negative counts; this window has exactly k integers, because the free sum ranges over the contiguous set [-kn, kp] in unit steps. Here c is the fixed contribution. (2) With a uniform on the m non-free nonzero variables, c + m_- ~ Bin(m, 1/2), so max_x P(c = x) = C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m <= 1/sqrt(m) for m >= 1. Hence P(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k/sqrt(s-k)). (3) For k <= s/2, k/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt2 k/sqrt s. For k > s/2 (s >= 2), sqrt2 k/sqrt s > sqrt(s/2) >= 1, so min(1, .) <= sqrt2 k/sqrt s. This also covers k = s (m = 0). (4) E[k] = sp, so P(nonconst) <= sqrt2 sp/sqrt s = sqrt(2s) p. The case s = 1 is trivial (P <= p). Equivalence: since free-sum steps are unit, nonconstancy is exactly the window event, so the statement is about non-constancy itself.

statement: Window lemma for a fixed threshold, with a uniform completion a on [n] minus F. Let K = the non-free indices with w_i nonzero, k = |K|, and W_F = sum over F of |w_i|. label: S0075
statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (bounded integer weights, single THR gate; generalises the +-1 lemma S0072 with B = 1). Setting: w in Z^n with s nonzero entries, |w_i| <= B for all i, t in Z fixed. F = free set, each variable free independently with prob p; each non-free nonzero variable gets a_i uniform in {0,1}. Claim: P(gate non-constant after restriction) <= B sqrt(2s) p for s >= 1. Proof. (1) Let k = |F cap supp(w)|, m = s - k, c = sum over non-free i of w_i a_i, X = sum over free i of w_i x_i. Non-constancy is min(c+X) < t <= max(c+X), i.e. c lies in a set of exactly max X - min X = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i| consecutive integers. (2) Erdos/Sperner: flip a_i to 1 - a_i where w_i < 0 (uniformity preserved), so c = (sum |w_i| a'_i) - const with |w_i| >= 1. For any half-open interval [y, y+1), the subset sums lying in it form an antichain (if A is a proper subset of B, the sums differ by >= 1), so there are at most C(m, floor(m/2)) of them. Hence max_x P(c = x) <= C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m <= 1/sqrt(m) for m >= 1. (3) So P(nonconst | F) <= min(1, W_F/sqrt(m)). (4) W_F <= B k. If k <= s/2 then m >= s/2 and B k/sqrt(m) <= sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s). If k > s/2 and s >= 2 then sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s) > B sqrt(s/2) >= 1, so the min is at most sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s). If s = 1, P(nonconst) <= P(k=1) = p <= sqrt2 B p. (5) E[k] = s p, so P(nonconst) <= sqrt2 B s p/sqrt(s) = B sqrt(2s) p. Corollary: with p = q/n and s <= n, the bound is B sqrt2 q/sqrt(n), the k/sqrt(n) shape of G0001 (per gate, in expectation, bounded weights only). Scope: single gate, bounded integer weights, fixed t, uniform fixed bits, i.i.d. free set. Does NOT close G0001, G0002, G0004 or G0009: no w.h.p. statement over m = n^1.5 gates, no unbounded weights, no top gate, no decision procedure, no running time. Barrier labels (provisional): not relativizing-relevant; a statement about linear forms under random restriction; not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense as stated; localizing not checked.

label: S0076
statement: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIT-FIXED-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F, k = |F|, m = n - k. Put s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i and mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). The subcube minimum and maximum of w.x are mn and mx, so non-constancy is equivalent to mn < t <= mx, i.e. s lies in a set I_F of exactly mx - mn = k integers (all |w_i| = 1). (1) Distribution of s given F: s = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} (1-a_i) - N_- where N_- = #{i notin F: w_i=-1}; the terms a_i and 1-a_i are i.i.d. uniform bits, so s is a fixed integer shift of Bin(m,1/2). Hence each point probability is at most C(m,floor(m/2))/2^m <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) (standard central binomial bound, valid for all m >= 1). Therefore P_a(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k sqrt(2/(pi m))). (2) Case k <= n/2: then m >= n/2 >= 1/2, so sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= 2/sqrt(pi n) < sqrt(2/n), giving P_a(nonconst|F) <= k sqrt(2/n). Taking expectation, E[k 1(k<=n/2)] <= E[k] = pn, so this part contributes at most p sqrt(2n). (3) Case k > n/2: bound the conditional probability by 1; by Markov, P(k >= n/2) <= E[k]/(n/2) = 2p. Adding: P <= p sqrt(2n) + 2p. QED. Consequence: for m' gates with the same (F,a) law, E[#nonconstant gates] <= m' p(sqrt(2n)+2), by linearity, with no independence needed.

statement: LEMMA (session R1046, CLAIMED, not self-reviewed). Let a_1..a_k be nonzero integers, x_i iid uniform {0,1}, S = sum a_i x_i. Then for every integer a, P(S=a) <= C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k. Proof: for a_i<0 put y_i=1-x_i, so S = c + sum |a_i| y_i with all coefficients >= 1. If Y is a strict subset of Y' then sum_{Y'} >= sum_Y + 1, so the subsets with a fixed sum form an antichain; Sperner bounds it by C(k,floor(k/2)). statement: Lemma U (unit-weight fixed-threshold restriction). Let n>=2, 1<=k<=n-1, N=n-k, and let t in Z be ARBITRARY (worst case over thresholds). Let g(x)=[x_1+...+x_n >= t] on {0,1}^n. Fix a set F of k free coordinates and draw the N other coordinates i.i.d. uniform; set c = sum of the fixed coordinates, so c ~ Bin(N,1/2). Then P_c[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= k/sqrt(N). PROOF. The restricted function is c + (sum of the k free bits), which takes values in [c, c+k]. It is constant 1 iff c >= t and constant 0 iff c+k < t, so it is non-constant iff t-k <= c <= t-1, a window of at most k integers. Hence P <= sum over the window of P(Bin(N,1/2)=c) <= k * M_N, where M_N = max_j C(N,j)/2^N. Claim: M_N <= 1/sqrt(N) for all N>=1. Let a_m = C(2m,m)/4^m. (i) For N=2m, M_N = a_m. Put f(m)=a_m^2(3m+1), f(0)=1. Since a_{m+1}/a_m=(2m+1)/(2m+2), f(m+1)/f(m) <= 1 iff (2m+1)^2(3m+4) <= (2m+2)^2(3m+1); the difference RHS-LHS equals m >= 0. So a_m <= 1/sqrt(3m+1) <= 1/sqrt(2m) = 1/sqrt(N). (ii) For N=2m+1, M_N = C(2m+1,m)/2^{2m+1} = a_{m+1} (because C(2m+2,m+1)=2 C(2m+1,m)), so M_N <= 1/sqrt(3m+4) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) = 1/sqrt(N). Combining, P <= k/sqrt(N). QED. COROLLARY: since N >= n/2 when k <= n/2, the bound is <= sqrt(2) k/sqrt(n); it shrinks with n only when k = o(sqrt n). SCOPE: unit weights only; uniform random fixed coordinates; the bound holds for every threshold t. It does NOT handle general integer weights (the Erdos-Moser/Halasz obstacle of G0002/G0004), the top gate, or running time. It is a special case of the open restriction obligation, not a closure of it.

statement:
statement: For n>=1, 0<=k<n, a fixed k-element set F, and g_t(x)=[sum_{j=1}^n x_j>=t] on {0,1}^n, choose the n-k coordinates outside F independently and uniformly. For every integer t, the probability that the restriction of g_t to F is nonconstant is at most min(1, k*sqrt(2/(n-k+1))).
proof: Put r=n-k and let C be the sum of the random outside coordinates. Given C=c, the restriction is nonconstant exactly when c<t<=c+k. Thus C must lie in a set of at most k integer values. Since C~Binomial(r,1/2), every atom is at most 2^{-r} binom(r,floor(r/2)) <= sqrt(2/(r+1)); summing over at most k values gives the second bound. Probability is also at most 1. For k=0 the interval is empty, so the probability is zero, as the formula states.

label: S0021
statement: LEMMA W (exact, general n, 0<k<n). PM on K_{n,n}, row-major order, top block a = rows 1..k, bottom block b = rows k+1..n. Let F(a) = {T subset of [n], |T|=k : a admits a perfect matching of rows 1..k onto T}, g_a(b) = PM(a,b). Then F(a)=F(a') iff g_a=g_a' as functions of b. Hence the level-kn width equals the number of distinct F(a). PROOF. (1) A perfect matching of K_{n,n} splits into a matching of rows 1..k onto some T with |T|=k and a matching of rows k+1..n onto [n]\T; so g_a(b)=1 iff some T in F(a) has b matchable onto [n]\T. (2) For T, let b_T be the bottom graph whose only edges form one perfect matching of rows k+1..n onto [n]\T. Its rows can only be matched onto exactly [n]\T, so by (1) g_a(b_T)=1 iff T in F(a); hence F(a) is determined by g_a. (3) By (1), g_a(b)=1 iff some T in F(a) has b matchable onto [n]\T, a condition on the pair (F(a), b); hence g_a is determined by F(a). Together (2) and (3) give the claim. QED.

label: S0024
statement:
statement: For n>=2 and 1<=k<=n-1, let X={(i,j): i<k} and Y={(i,j): i>=k} be the edge sets of K_{n,n}. Let M[a,b]=1 iff a (subset of X) union b (subset of Y) is a perfect matching of K_{n,n}. Then rank_F(M)=C(n,k) over every field F. Closes: none. This is a control-failure lemma and does not close G0001.
derivation: (1) In a union a+b that is a perfect matching, each left vertex i<k has degree 1 in a, since b has no edges at i<k, and the right endpoints of a are distinct. So a is valid iff a is an injection f:[k]->[n]; let S(a) be its image, |S|=k. (2) Symmetrically, b is valid iff it is an injection g:{k..n-1}->[n], with image T(b) of size n-k. (3) a+b is a perfect matching iff valid(a), valid(b) and T(b)=[n]\S(a). (4) Row a depends only on S(a). Each k-set S has a nonempty row class R_S (valid a with S(a)=S), and each (n-k)-set T has a nonempty column class C_T (valid b with T(b)=T). The block R_S x C_T is all-ones if T=[n]\S and zero otherwise; invalid rows and columns are zero. (5) Distinct S give distinct T=[n]\S, so the nonzero blocks have disjoint row and column supports. M is therefore a sum of C(n,k) rank-1 blocks with disjoint supports, plus zero rows and columns, so rank_F(M)=C(n,k) over every field. (6) For k=n/2, rank >= 2^n/(n+1). Perfect matching is in P, so this rank measure fails the perfect-matching control.
evidence: Hand proof above, re-checked step by step. Matches cm-40cf2c6f2271450d (GF(1000003), n<=4: 2,3,3,4,6,4) and cm-4a4d1d1af70b4712 (GF(2), n<=6, ALL_MATCH True, including n=5 k=2 -> 10 and n=6 k=3 -> 20). Not a proof of an oracle-free lower bound.

label: S0026
statement:
statement_start: For every deterministic one-pass streaming machine with S state bits and a one-bit input alphabet, each transition stage can be implemented by a Boolean circuit of size O(S 2^S).
statement: Lemma (truth-table transition simulation). Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine whose configuration at each read boundary is encoded by S bits, whose next configuration after reading one input bit is a total function δ:{0,1}^S×{0,1}->{0,1}^S, and whose input length is L. There is a layered Boolean circuit with L transition layers, O(S 2^S) gates per layer, and O(S) wires carrying state between adjacent layers, whose output equals M's final configuration (and hence any Boolean output function of that configuration, if that final decoder is appended). Proof: for each output coordinate j and each pair (u,b) in {0,1}^S×{0,1} with δ(u,b)_j=1, form the minterm that is 1 exactly when the S state wires equal u and the input wire equals b. OR these minterms to obtain output coordinate j. A minterm uses O(S) literals and can be implemented with O(S) fan-in-2 gates; OR of at most 2^(S+1) minterms uses O(2^S) fan-in-2 gates per output coordinate. Summing over S coordinates gives O(S 2^S) gates per layer. Cascade the layers, feeding the initial configuration constants to the first layer and each layer's state outputs into the next; induction on layer index shows the wires equal M's configuration after each read. Appending the decoder preserves the final output. The construction is exact for all input strings of length L. This restricted lemma only gives an upper simulation bound and does not imply a lower bound for Search-MCSP or close G0001.

label: S0027
statement:
statement: Let L be the YES language of an exact deterministic one-pass Search-MCSP machine on inputs of fixed length N. At a cut after t bits, define the suffix residual of prefix u in {0,1}^t by L_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in L}, and let R_t be the number of distinct such residuals. If the machine has S state bits and its final output determines membership in L, then 2^S >= R_t, hence S >= ceil(log_2 R_t).
proof: Suppose prefixes u and v reach the same state at the cut. Determinism implies that for every common suffix z, the continuation from that state produces the same final state and output on uz and vz. Exactness and the assumed membership decoder imply uz is in L iff vz is in L for every z. Therefore L_u=L_v. Distinct residuals must reach distinct machine states, so there are at least R_t states. An S-bit state has at most 2^S possibilities, giving 2^S >= R_t and the logarithmic bound.
scope: Fixed-length inputs; deterministic one-pass computation; the entire configuration relevant to future computation is included in the S-bit state; final output determines YES membership. Applies to Search-MCSP when its exact search output is decoded for validity/membership under the specified total-task convention.

statement:
statement: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut after t bits. For each prefix u in {0,1}^t, define its suffix residual F_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}. If R_t is the number of distinct residuals, then R_t <= min(2^t, 2^(N-t), |F|+1).
proof: There are at most 2^t prefixes and at most 2^(N-t) possible residual subsets of suffixes, giving the first two bounds. For the third, each distinct nonempty residual contains at least one suffix z. Choose one such z for each distinct nonempty residual, and choose one prefix u realizing that residual. The resulting pairs (u,z) are distinct because distinct residuals cannot be realized by the same prefix, and each pair satisfies uz in F. Thus the number of distinct nonempty residuals is at most |F|. There is at most one empty residual, so R_t <= |F|+1.
scope: Finite fixed-length Boolean language and any fixed prefix cut. For Search-MCSP the lemma applies to F equal to the YES truth tables, but supplies only an upper bound on residual width; it does not prove G0001 or an update-time lower bound.

statement:
statement: Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, fix a cut after t bits, and put p=2^t, q=2^(N-t), k=|F|. For each prefix u define F_u={z:uz in F}, and let R_t be the number of distinct F_u. Then R_t <= min(p,q,k+1,pq-k+1).
proof: There are p rows, so R_t<=p. Each row is a subset of a q-element suffix set, so R_t<=q. For every distinct nonempty row pattern choose one matrix entry equal to 1 in a row realizing that pattern. Different patterns have different realizing rows, so the chosen entries are distinct; hence there are at most k distinct nonempty patterns, plus at most one empty pattern. Thus R_t<=k+1. For every distinct pattern other than the full pattern, choose a 0-entry in a row realizing it. Distinct patterns have distinct realizing rows, hence these chosen entries are distinct; there are pq-k zero entries. Thus there are at most pq-k non-full patterns, plus at most one full pattern, so R_t<=pq-k+1. Combining the four bounds proves the claim.
scope: All finite fixed-length Boolean languages and every fixed prefix cut. For Search-MCSP this is only a residual-width upper bound; it proves no residual lower bound and no update-time lower bound.

label: S0036
statement:
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the row-major perfect-matching Boolean function on K_{n,n} has exactly 2^n distinct residual functions after the first n edge variables (the edges incident to the first row).
proof: A prefix of the first n variables specifies a subset U of columns adjacent to the first row. For any suffix assignment b to the remaining edges, the full graph has a perfect matching exactly when some j in U can be reserved for the first row and the suffix rows have a matching onto [n]\\{j}. Thus the residual depends only on U, so there are at most 2^n residuals. To distinguish any distinct U,V, choose j in their symmetric difference, and let b contain exactly a bijection from the remaining n-1 rows onto [n]\\{j}. Then the only possible perfect matching uses column j for the first row. The residual accepts precisely when j belongs to the prefix subset, so the residuals for U and V differ. Every subset U is realizable by a prefix assignment. Hence there are exactly 2^n distinct residual functions.

label: S0037
statement: statement_start: LEMMA (residual distinguishability forces streaming states). Let L be a language over strings split into prefixes and suffixes, and fix a prefix length l.

structure.lemma: LEMMA (residual distinguishability forces streaming states). Let L be a language over strings split into prefixes and suffixes, and fix a prefix length l. Define u ~ v iff for every suffix z, uz is in L exactly when vz is in L. Any deterministic one-pass machine that reads the prefix, stores a state, and thereafter processes the suffix exactly has at least as many distinct states after length-l prefixes as there are ~-classes. Proof: if u and v reach the same state, determinism implies that processing any common suffix z from that state yields the same acceptance outcome. Exactness therefore gives uz in L iff vz in L for every z, hence u ~ v. Thus each ~-class requires a distinct machine state. If the machine uses at most B bits of memory, it has at most 2^B states, so B >= ceil(log2 R_l), where R_l is the number of residual classes at the cut. Scope: deterministic exact one-pass recognition, fixed cut and encoding; this does not establish a large R_l for Search-MCSP or bound update time, and it does not close G0001.
structure.proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA (residual distinguishability forces streaming states). Let L be a language over strings split into prefixes and suffixes, and fix a prefix length l.

label: S0038
statement: statement: CONSTRUCTIVE RESIDUAL AUTOMATON LEMMA. Let L be a language over a finite alphabet Σ. For each prefix u, define its residual R_u={z∈Σ*: uz∈L}. Let ℛ={R_u:u∈Σ*}. If ℛ is finite, the machine with state set ℛ, initial state R_ε, transition δ(R_u,a)=R_{ua}, and accepting states {R_u: ε∈R_u} recognizes L and is minimal among deterministic exact automata. The transition is well-defined: R_u=R_v implies for every z, uaz∈L iff vaz∈L, hence R_{ua}=R_{va}. Recognition follows by induction on the consumed input: after prefix u the state is R_u, which accepts exactly when u∈L. For minimality, prefixes with distinct residuals are distinguished by some suffix z on which membership differs; any exact deterministic machine must therefore place them in distinct states. Consequently the minimum state count is |ℛ|, and any encoding needs at least ceil(log2 |ℛ|) bits. This gives an exact state lower bound but no transition-circuit/update-time lower bound.

label: S0044
statement:
statement_start: In a Boolean transition circuit with T fan-in-two gates, if every output is driven by a gate, at most 2T distinct input variables can feed those gates.
evidence: Each of the T gates has at most two input slots, so the union of variables feeding gates has size at most 2T. The output restriction matters: free output wires can copy arbitrarily many inputs without gates. This restricted lemma gives no bound for the unrestricted Search-MCSP machine, so it does not close G0001.

statement:
statement_start: For every Boolean circuit with n primary input variables and T gates, regardless of fan-out and with arbitrary output wires, the circuit has at most n+T distinct output Boolean functions.
evidence: Each output function is the function computed by a primary input or by one of the T gates. Thus at most n+T distinct functions can appear on output wires. Fan-out and repeated output wires can repeat a source function, but cannot create another function. This bound does not show that Search-MCSP transitions need many distinct next-state functions, so it does not close G0001.

label: S0014
statement: Formalization of S-54f648a904 (inclusion-exclusion for #F). Let F = C_1 and ... and C_m be a CNF over x_1..x_n. For S subset of [m] put L(S) = union of C_i over i in S, and N(S) = #{a in {0,1}^n : every literal of L(S) is false under a}. Then #F = sum over S of (-1)^|S| N(S). Moreover N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if L(S) contains no complementary pair {x, not-x}, and N(S) = 0 otherwise, where V(S) is the set of variables occurring in L(S). Proof: with f_i(a) = 1 iff C_i is falsified by a, [a satisfies F] = product over i of (1 - f_i(a)). Expanding gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| times product over i in S of f_i(a), and that product is 1 exactly when all literals of L(S) are false under a. Summing over a gives the identity. A consistent L(S) forces the values of V(S) and leaves n - |V(S)| variables free; an inconsistent L(S) has no satisfying-falsifying assignment.

structure.evidence: BOOKKEEPING ONLY (session R1455, turn 17). Standard inclusion-exclusion. Checked edge cases: an empty clause has f_i identically 1, so the terms for S and S with i removed cancel; a tautological clause is never falsified and is covered by N(S) = 0. It does not close G0001-G0012 or any obligation of Q-26be1ff4a1, and it is not progress toward P vs NP. Needs an independent review before it counts as VERIFIED.

structure.lemma: Reuse-elimination (naive): for an acyclic De Morgan circuit C with S non-input gates and r gates of fan-out >= 2, f_C has a De Morgan formula with at most 2^r * 2S leaves. Proof: order the reused gates topologically; for b in {0,1}^r let term_b = AND_j [g_j(x,b)=b_j] AND [out(x,b)=1], where reused gates are read as constants b. Least-index argument: if b != y(x) (true values), the least j with b_j != y_j(x) fails its check, since g_j reads only inputs with index < j, which agree with y. So exactly one term is consistent and OR_b term_b = f_C. Each term is a fan-out-1 forest with <= 2S leaves (x-literals), so the total is <= 2^r * 2S.

label: S0040
statement:
LEMMA (De Morgan leaf size, general). Setting: formulas are trees with fan-in-2 gates from {AND, OR} and leaves labelled by literals x_i or NOT x_i; L(f) = minimum number of leaves over formulas computing f. Parity_d(x) = x_1 XOR ... XOR x_d.
(A) L(NOT f) = L(f). Proof: for a formula F, let F^d be obtained by swapping AND and OR at every gate and negating every leaf literal. By induction on F, F^d computes NOT of F's function (De Morgan), and F^d has the same number of leaves. Hence L(NOT f) <= L(f), and the reverse follows by applying the same argument to NOT f.
(B) L(f XOR g) <= 2(L(f) + L(g)). Proof: take formulas F, G with leaves L(f), L(g). By (A), F^d and G^d compute NOT f and NOT g with the same leaf counts. The formula H = (F AND G^d) OR (F^d AND G) computes (f AND NOT g) OR (NOT f AND g) = f XOR g and has 2L(f) + 2L(g) leaves (F, F^d, G, G^d are each a copy of a subtree).
(C) For every j >= 0, L(parity_{2^j}) <= 4^j. Proof by induction. j = 0: parity_1 = x_1, one leaf, 1 = 4^0. Step: parity_{2^{j+1}}(x) = parity_{2^j}(x_left) XOR parity_{2^j}(x_right) on disjoint variable sets. By (B), L <= 2(4^j + 4^j) = 4^{j+1}. Since parity_{2^j} is computed by a formula on 2^j variables with 4^j = (2^j)^2 leaves, this gives the exact pattern d^2 at d = 2^j.
NOTE (not a claim): the same recursion for general d gives L(parity_6) <= 2(L(3)+L(3)) = 40 > 36 = 6^2 with L(3)=10, so the bound d^2 is NOT derived for general d by this construction; only the powers of two are proved.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: nothing about DAGs with reuse, constant-width state, or the S0001 conversion lemma (a reused DAG of size S with shared state -> formula of size poly(S)). S0001 stays REFUTED-as-stated / OPEN.

structure.closes: None of S0001. It closes the session's own open checkpoint: an exact general upper bound L(parity_{2^j}) <= 4^j, valid for all j, not only j <= 3.

statement:
statement: For every field F, n >= 0, and function f:{0,1}^n -> F, M_f(x)=sum_{a in {0,1}^n} f(a) product_{i:a_i=1} x_i product_{i:a_i=0}(1-x_i) is multilinear, agrees with f on the Boolean cube, and is zero as a formal polynomial iff f is identically zero. Its displayed representation has at most 2^n terms and O(n*2^n) literal factors.
proof: At Boolean input b only the summand a=b survives, so M_f(b)=f(b); multilinearity is immediate. If a multilinear polynomial P vanishes on the cube, induct on n. Write P=A+x_n B with A,B multilinear. The restrictions x_n=0 and x_n=1 vanish on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=0 and A+B=0, hence B=0. Thus P=0. Applying this to M_f proves the equivalence. The displayed sum has 2^n terms of n factors each.

label: S0002
statement: statement: Let R=Z[x_1,...,x_n]/(x_i^2-x_i:1<=i<=n). For every polynomial P in Z[x_1,...,x_n], its class in R is zero iff P(a)=0 for every a in {0,1}^n. Consequently, for any CNF φ, the class of its literal-product satisfaction indicator P_φ=∏_j(1-∏_{literal occurrences ℓ in C_j}(1-ℓ)), where ℓ=x_i for a positive literal and ℓ=1-x_i for a negative literal, is zero in R iff φ is unsatisfiable. Proof: Modulo x_i^2=x_i, reduce each monomial by replacing every positive exponent of x_i by 1; this gives a multilinear representative with the same Boolean evaluations. A multilinear polynomial vanishing on the Boolean cube is the zero polynomial, by induction on n: write it A+x_nB; restrictions at x_n=0 and x_n=1 imply A=0 and A+B=0 on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=B=0. Thus P's class is zero exactly when all evaluations vanish. On Boolean inputs P_φ is 1 precisely when every clause has a true literal, hence it vanishes on the cube iff φ has no satisfying assignment.

structure.proved_step: statement: Let R=Z[x_1,...,x_n]/(x_i^2-x_i:1<=i<=n). For every polynomial P in Z[x_1,...,x_n], its class in R is zero iff P(a)=0 for every a in {0,1}^n. Consequently, for any CNF φ, the class of its literal-product satisfaction indicator P_φ=∏_j(1-∏_{literal occurrences ℓ in C_j}(1-ℓ)), where ℓ=x_i for a positive literal and ℓ=1-x_i for a negative literal, is zero in R iff φ is unsatisfiable. Proof: Modulo x_i^2=x_i, reduce each monomial by replacing every positive exponent of x_i by 1; this gives a multilinear representative with the same Boolean evaluations. A multilinear polynomial vanishing on the Boolean cube is the zero polynomial, by induction on n: write it A+x_nB; restrictions at x_n=0 and x_n=1 imply A=0 and A+B=0 on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=B=0. Thus P's class is zero exactly when all evaluations vanish. On Boolean inputs P_φ is 1 precisely when every clause has a true literal, hence it vanishes on the cube iff φ has no satisfying assignment.

label: S0003
statement: statement: For every n>=0 and every multilinear polynomial Q(x)=sum_{S subseteq [n]} c_S product_{i in S} x_i over the integers, the Boolean-cube sum is sum_{a in {0,1}^n} Q(a)=sum_{S subseteq[n]} c_S 2^{n-|S|}. Consequently, if Q is the unique multilinear representative modulo (x_i^2-x_i) of a CNF satisfaction indicator, this weighted coefficient sum equals #SAT of that CNF. Proof: finite-sum interchange gives sum_a sum_S c_S product_{i in S}a_i = sum_S c_S sum_a product_{i in S}a_i. For fixed S, the monomial equals 1 iff all coordinates in S are 1; the remaining n-|S| coordinates are free, so exactly 2^{n-|S|} assignments contribute 1. The n=0 case uses S=empty and has one assignment. This is an identity over integers, not modulo a finite field, and asserts no efficient coefficient extraction from an arithmetic-circuit description.

statement: PROOF. (i) The projection K_G -> (+)_v T_3 onto vertex blocks is an isomorphism (edge coordinates are determined by endpoints), so dim K_G = 2n. The vectors (1,2,0) and (0,1,2) lie in T_3 (sums 3 = 0) and are linearly independent over GF(3), so their vertex-block images for all v form a basis of (+)_v T_3. Hence B is a basis of K_G. (ii) Vertices of H_B are the 2n vectors. Same-vertex pair x_v, x'_v: they share vertex-block coordinates 1 and 2 (supports {0,1} and {1,2}), so they are adjacent. Pair with u != v: vertex blocks are disjoint, so a shared coordinate must be an edge coordinate e; the coordinate of x_v on e is nonzero only if e is incident to v. A shared edge e must therefore be incident to both u and v, i.e. e=(u,v) in E. For such an edge, supports of x_u and x_v on e are {0,1} and {1,2}-type sets that overlap (both contain coordinate 1 when the pair uses (1,2,0) and (0,1,2); for the other combinations the supports {0,1},{0,1} and {1,2},{1,2} also overlap), so all four pairs between blobs of adjacent u,v are adjacent. Non-adjacent u,v have no shared coordinate. So H_B = G[K_2]. (iii) Let (T,{X_i}) be a tree decomposition of G of width k. Replace each bag X_i by X_i x {a,b} (2 copies). Bag size is at most 2(k+1), so width <= 2k+1. Coverage: a vertex pair (v,a),(v,b) lies in the bag of any bag containing v. An edge (u,a)-(w,b) of G[K_2] comes from edge uw in G, which lies in some X_i, so both appear in X_i x {a,b}. Connectivity of the occurrence sets is inherited from T. Hence tw(G[K_2]) <= 2k+1. The reverse inequality (min over ALL bases >= 2tw(G)+1) is NOT proved here; it is the owner's lower bound and is not re-verified in this step. Remark: this explains the earlier hill-climb stall for P3 and C4: the explicit B reaches tw 3 (P3) and tw 5 (C4), which the search had not found.

label: S0001
statement: PROOF. Each cross wire carries one bit from its source side to its target side. Evaluate C in topological order: a gate on side S_A needs only values from S_A or from cross wires; the value of a cross wire is a function of its source side's inputs and bits already received, so it is sent once, by its source party, as one bit. Each cross wire contributes at most one bit, so the transcript has at most kappa bits. Once all cross wires are transmitted, both parties know the output bit for their input pair; the party holding the output gate sends one more bit, so the total is at most kappa+1 bits. A deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; each leaf is a combinatorial rectangle on which the output is constant, so M is a sum of at most 2^c rank-one 0/1 matrices, rank_R(M) <= 2^c. Hence log2 rank <= kappa+1. The argument uses only the wire count, not any gate structure, and it holds for any partition of gates. Remark: the lab check uses the 0-based side assignment and counts each gate input once, matching the wire count above.

structure.evidence: physalis_code_run cm-33966d12d8364e00: 2420 random circuit/partition tests on small n, 0 violations; max(log2 rank - kappa) = 0.0; EQ, IP and parity controls satisfy log2 rank <= kappa (EQ rank 2^n, IP rank ~ 2^n-1 with kappa tracking n). The proof is by hand and is CLAIMED until another session reviews it.
structure.gap: Open: the aggregated bound over many partitions. A single partition gives log2 rank <= kappa(P)+1; summing kappa over a family of partitions counts a gate once for every partition it crosses, so sum_P kappa(P) is not bounded by |C| in general (reuse). Need an account that bounds the cumulative cost, or a counterexample showing the aggregate exceeds polylog(N)*|C|.
structure.lemma: Cut lemma. Let C be a Boolean circuit (fan-in <= 2, gates AND/OR/XOR/NOT) on inputs x_1..x_n, and let (A,B) be a partition of the input variables. Let the gates be split into sides S_A and S_B (each gate on the side it is assigned), and let kappa be the number of wires (gate-input edges, including input-variable edges) whose endpoints lie on different sides. Let M be the 2^|A| x 2^|B| communication matrix of f = C, with rows indexed by a in {0,1}^A and columns by b in {0,1}^B. Then log2 rank_R(M) <= kappa + 1.

label: S0008
statement: L-K1-PREFIX (closes G0005(a) for the prefix-cut family). Setting: f:{0,1}^N->{0,1} computed by a fan-in<=2 circuit C with gates G, inputs x_1..x_N in a fixed order. Define P(x_j)=j and P(g)=max of P over the inputs of gate g (so P(u)<=P(g) along every wire u->g, and 1<=P(v)<=N). Let W = number of wires (gate-input edges), Lambda(C)=sum over wires u->g of (P(g)-P(u)). For i in [1,N-1], M_i = communication matrix of f for A={x_1..x_i}, B=rest. CLAIM: (1) sum_{i=1}^{N-1} log2 rank_R(M_i) <= (N-1) + Lambda(C); (2) Lambda(C) <= W(N-1) <= 2|G|(N-1); hence for every input order, |G| >= (sum_i log2 rank_R(M_i) - (N-1)) / (2(N-1)). PROOF. Let L_i={v: P(v)<=i}. Input x_j is in L_i iff j<=i, so L_i restricted to inputs is exactly A. If g in L_i and u->g is a wire, P(u)<=P(g)<=i so u in L_i: no wire goes from the right side to the left side. Hence the cross wires for cut i are exactly the wires with P(u)<=i<P(g); call their number kappa_i. This is a legal gate split for (A,B), so S0001 (SURVIVED_REVIEW) gives log2 rank_R(M_i) <= kappa_i+1. Summing over i: sum_i kappa_i = sum over wires of #{i in [1,N-1]: P(u)<=i<P(g)} = sum over wires of (P(g)-P(u)), because 1<=P(u) and P(g)<=N. So the sum is <= Lambda(C)+(N-1). (2) holds since 0<=P(g)-P(u)<=N-1 and each gate has at most 2 wires. Corollary (CEILING): rank_R(M_i) <= 2^{min(i,N-i)}, so sum_i log2 rank <= N^2/4 and the bound gives |G| >= (N^2/4-(N-1))/(2(N-1)) = N/8 - O(1) at most. The method cannot give a superlinear bound for any N-input function using prefix cuts.

label: S0012
statement: S0002 (repair of S0001, kind LEMMA). Setting: Boolean circuit C of fan-in at most 2 over AND, OR, NOT, with input nodes x_1..x_(n+m); Alice holds x_1..x_n, Bob holds the rest; f(a,b) is the output. Assign every node (inputs and gates) to a party. Let kappa = number of DAG edges whose endpoints lie on different parties, input edges included. Claim: DCC(f) <= kappa+1 and log2 rank_Q M_f <= kappa+1, where M_f[a,b] = f(a,b). Proof: fix the schedule in topological order; each node is evaluated by its owner once its inputs are known. For every node that has at least one crossing out-edge, its owner sends its value once; the number of such sources is at most kappa. The output owner sends the output bit (at most 1 more). The protocol is deterministic, costs at most kappa+1 and computes f. A protocol of cost c has at most 2^c leaves, each a combinatorial rectangle on which f is constant, so M_f is a sum of at most 2^c indicator rectangles over the 1-leaves and rank_Q M_f <= 2^c. This is an upper bound, not a lower bound, so the barrier check does not apply. Gap: the aggregate G0001 (cut costs over many partitions) stays open. Evidence: cm-5d2f4c68ffda4c45 (exploratory check).

label: S0026
statement: LEMMA (subclass, cut width). Fix a variable order pi and a level l. Call a node prefix-side if its support lies in the first l variables. Let kappa_l be the number of prefix-side nodes with an edge into a non-prefix-side gate. Then the level width K_l (number of distinct residual functions C restricted to rho, for rho in {0,1}^l) satisfies K_l <= 2^kappa_l, because each non-prefix-side gate's value under rho depends on rho only through the constant values of the kappa_l crossing nodes. Hence the OBDD size for order pi is at most sum_l 2^kappa_l. COROLLARY: if kappa_l <= c log n for all l, then #SAT of C runs in poly(n, m) time by building the OBDD. This is the standard cut-width / OBDD-width technique and is not new; it is recorded only as a verified subclass.

structure.gap: G0001 is NOT closed: this is a single-order, log-cut-width subclass. The aggregate over many partitions remains open, and the multiplier family (G0013) shows that no OBDD-size bound can be polynomial for all poly-size circuits.

X = prefix-side nodes feeding a gate whose support is not inside P, k = |X|. o = 1 if the output support is inside P, else 0. Then K_l <= 2^k if o = 0, and K_l <= 2 if o = 1. structure.lemma: Single-order residual-width sum (identity order). C is a fan-in-2 circuit over x_0..x_{n-1} with gates G, output node out, computing f. For a node v let t(v) = bit_length of its support bitmask, so t(v) = 1 + max variable index in the support. Let Lambda(C) = sum over wires u->g of max(0, t(g) - t(u)). For l = 0..n let K_l = number of distinct residual functions f restricted to x_{<l} = rho, over rho in {0,1}^l. Then sum_{l=0}^{n} log2 K_l <= Lambda(C) + #{l : t(out) <= l}. Proof: fix l and P = {0..l-1}. Let X_l be the set of prefix-side nodes (support inside P) that feed a non-prefix gate. By the S0026 argument, if out is non-prefix then K_l <= 2^{|X_l|}; if out is prefix-side then K_l <= 2. Since supports grow along wires, t(g) >= t(u) for every wire u->g. Each w in X_l has a wire w->g with t(w) <= l < t(g), so |X_l| <= #{wires u->g : t(u) <= l < t(g)}. Summing over l, each wire with t(u) < t(g) is counted exactly t(g)-t(u) times, so sum_l |X_l| <= Lambda(C). Adding the at most one bit per level where out is prefix-side gives the claim. Scope: a single fixed variable order; Lambda depends on the order and can be about |C| * N for a bad order.

statement: LOCAL-BOUND-REPAIR (CLAIMED, bookkeeping; does not close G0001). label: S0044
statement: REPAIR of S0001 (single-split cut lemma, input wires counted). Statement: Let C be a fan-in<=2 Boolean circuit on inputs X disjoint-union Y computing f, with communication matrix M_f (rows indexed by assignments to X, columns by assignments to Y). Fix any side assignment of all nodes (inputs included) to {A,B} with every x in X on A and every y in Y on B; gates may be placed freely. Let kappa = number of EDGES (u,g) of C with side(u) != side(g), input nodes included. Then rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). PROOF: fix a topological order v_1..v_T (inputs first). Alice holds a, Bob holds b. Process v_1..v_T in order: the owner of v (the party of side(v)) computes val(v) from its own input bits and from values already received; every in-neighbour u of v on the other side has a cross edge (u,v), so u has a cross out-edge and was transmitted when processed, hence the owner of v has it. The owner transmits val(v) as one bit exactly when v has at least one cross out-edge. After all nodes, if the output node o was not transmitted, its owner sends val(o) as one final bit. Both parties then know f(a,b). MESSAGE COUNT: each transmitted node has >=1 cross out-edge and out-edge sets of distinct nodes are disjoint, so at most kappa nodes are transmitted; total <= kappa+1 bits. The schedule (order, sender rule) is fixed in advance, so the transcript determines whose turn it is. RECTANGLE: a deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; the inputs reaching a leaf form a rectangle A_l x B_l (standard, since each message depends only on the sender's input and the transcript); f is constant on each leaf because val(o) is in the transcript (either transmitted or the final bit). So M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of 1_{A_l} 1_{B_l}^T, a sum of at most 2^(kappa+1) rank-one matrices, hence rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. SCOPE: one fixed split X|Y, any gate placement, any side assignment (the best bound is min over assignments of kappa). This is the standard circuit-to-communication argument (folklore, not claimed as new); it is bookkeeping, it does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (aggregate over many partitions) or G0005(a). It is not a LOWER_BOUND and does not trigger the barrier check. Consistency check on the refuted case: for IP_2 with all gates on Alice's side the input edges b1->AND1 and b2->AND2 are cross edges, so kappa=2 and the bound 8 >= rank 3; the gate-only count gives kappa=0 and the false bound 2.

label: S0046
statement: MINLA LEMMA (limit of the single-order prefix route; does not close G0001/G0002). Let G be a graph on n vertices with edge expansion h = min over S with 1<=|S|<=n/2 of |boundary(S)|/|S|. For any linear order v_1..v_n let cut_k = number of edges with one endpoint in {v_1..v_k} and the other outside. Then sum_{k=1}^{n-1} cut_k >= h*floor(n^2/4). PROOF: for k <= n/2, S={v_1..v_k} has |S| = k <= n/2, so cut_k >= h*k. For k > n/2, T={v_{k+1}..v_n} has |T| = n-k < n/2 and cut_k = |boundary(T)| >= h*(n-k). So cut_k >= h*min(k, n-k). Summing, and using sum_{k=1}^{n-1} min(k, n-k) = floor(n^2/4) (checked: n=3 gives 2, n=4 gives 4), the claim follows. CONSEQUENCE: for a fan-in-2 circuit C of size s whose underlying graph (all nodes, inputs included, n <= s + #inputs) has constant expansion h, the telescoping sum Lambda_pi = sum_k cut_k of the prefix chain (the identity sum_l kappa_l = Lambda_pi from the prefix cut lemma) is at least h*floor(n^2/4) = Omega(s^2) for EVERY order pi. So min over orders of Lambda_pi, and with it the bound sum_l log2 K_l <= Lambda_pi + n, is Omega(s^2) for such circuits and cannot give O(s polylog s). SCOPE: the lower bound is for any graph; it applies to any circuit family whose underlying graph is an expander, provided the expansion is verified for that family. CORRECTION of S0042: with output on the left, C|rho is constant in y, so K <= 2 (not K = 1); the bound K <= 2^(kappa+1) is unchanged.

label: S0050
statement: PROOF. (1) By induction over a topological order, every node in P has a value that depends only on a, since P is closed under predecessors. (2) Let W be the set of wires leaving P; |W| = w(P). For any node outside P, its value is a function of its own inputs, which are either suffix inputs, outside gates, or wires in W. So for each suffix assignment b there is a function G_b with f(a,b) = G_b(z(a)), where z(a) in {0,1}^W lists the values carried by the wires in W. (3) Therefore f(a,.) = G_(.)(z(a)) is determined by z(a), which takes at most 2^(w(P)) values, so at most 2^(w(P)) distinct subfunctions occur. QED. Consequence: if every level l admits a closed prefix set with w_l <= W, then the OBDD has size at most n 2^W and #SAT of C takes time about n 2^W poly(s). For W = O(log s) this is polynomial.

(d) Expander-like circuits have w_l >= h min(l, n-l) for every closed or non-closed set, so the bound is 2^(Omega(n)) on those families, consistent with S0046. The repair works only for bounded cut-width classes. Hand-checked only; no computation.

Hence the OBDD for the order x_1..x_n has size at most sum_l 2^(w_l), where w_l is the boundary of a closed prefix set at level l.

statement: PROOF. Case 1, output on Bob's side. Induction in topological order: every Bob-side node value is a function of (y, z(x)), where z(x) in {0,1}^X is the vector of values of X-nodes (a Bob gate reads Bob nodes or X-nodes only). So row M[x,.] depends only on z(x); there are at most 2^|X| distinct rows, and rank <= number of distinct rows. Case 2, output on Alice's side: f(x,y) = out(x) does not depend on y, so rank <= 1. The +1 in the earlier statement is slack, not needed.

label: S0055
statement: PROOF OF L1. (i) By induction on topological order, every A-node is a function of x alone: x-inputs trivially; an A-gate's inputs are A-nodes because no B-node feeds an A-gate. (ii) Let S(x) in {0,1}^kappa be the values of the kappa cross nodes (A-nodes with a B-consumer), which are functions of x by (i). By induction every B-node is a function of (y, S(x)): its inputs are y-inputs, B-nodes, or A-nodes, and any A-node feeding a B-node is a cross node, hence a coordinate of S(x). So f(x,y) = G(S(x), y) for some G. If the output node is an A-node, then f = h(x) and M_f has rank <= 1 <= 2^kappa. (iii) For s in {0,1}^kappa let u_s be the indicator vector of {x : S(x) = s} and w_s(y) = G(s,y). Then M_f = sum over s of u_s w_s^T, a sum of at most 2^kappa rank-<=1 matrices over Q, so rank_Q M_f <= 2^kappa. QED.

label: S0056
statement: PROOF OF L2. Fix a topological order v_1,...,v_N of the circuit. Let c_1,...,c_kappa be the nodes of K in that order; each c_i is owned by Alice (A) or Bob (B). Protocol: for i = 1..kappa the owner of c_i sends the bit value(c_i), then the output owner sends f's bit if f is not in K, i.e. at most kappa+1 bits. Well-defined and deterministic: the speaker sequence depends only on the circuit and the side assignment, not on the inputs. Correctness: when the owner of c_i speaks, it knows its own input and all bits sent so far, and it can compute c_i. Induction on the topological order: any input of c_i is either an input node (owned by the speaker, since inputs lie on their own side), a node on the speaker's side (computed by the speaker by induction), or a node on the other side with a consumer on the speaker's side, hence in K, hence earlier in the order and already sent. So value(c_i) is a function of the speaker's input and the transcript so far. Thus the transcript determines all of K and f. Rectangles: for a fixed transcript tau, the set of x with tau consistent is a set X_tau, and similarly Y_tau for y; by the standard induction over rounds the set {(x,y): transcript = tau} equals X_tau x Y_tau. On a leaf f is constant (it is determined by tau). Hence M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of u_tau w_tau^T with u, w 0/1 vectors, so rank_Q M_f <= number of leaves <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. Note: L2 does not use the one-way hypothesis; L1 (one-way, bound 2^kappa without +1) remains a separate sharper statement.

statement: Proof: Alice and Bob process gates in topological order. Each cross edge carries one bit, sent by the side that owns its source once the source value is determined from that side's inputs and previously received bits. Total communication is at most kappa bits. The output bit adds 1, so the deterministic communication complexity satisfies D(f) <= kappa+1. A deterministic protocol of depth d partitions the matrix into at most 2^d monochromatic rectangles, each of rank at most 1, so rank_R M_f <= 2^d. Hence log2 rank_R M_f <= kappa+1.

statement: Proof: Protocol: each cross edge carries the value of its source gate, sent by the owner of the source once that value is determined. Each gate is evaluated by the side that owns it, using its own inputs and bits received so far. Total communication is exactly kappa bits, so the protocol tree has at most 2^kappa leaves. For each leaf, the set of (a,b) reaching it is a combinatorial rectangle R_l on which f is constant. M_f = sum over 1-leaves of the indicator matrices of R_l. Each indicator of a rectangle has real rank at most 1, so rank_R(M_f) <= number of 1-leaves <= 2^kappa. Hence log2 rank_R(M_f) <= kappa.

Then rank_R(M_f) <= 2^kappa, so log2 rank_R(M_f) <= kappa. The earlier +1 is not needed.

label: S0076
statement: L-K1-LOCAL-REPAIR (R1367, claude-haiku-5-5): fan-in<=2 Boolean circuit C over AND OR NOT, fixed topological order, variable order v_1..v_N. For level l let P = nodes with support inside first l variables, kappa_l = number of edges from P into non-P nodes, K_l = number of distinct functions C restricted to rho for rho in {0,1}^l. Claim: K_l <= 2^(kappa_l+1). Proof: if output not in P, each non-P node depends on rho only through the boundary values of P, so C|rho is determined by a vector in {0,1}^kappa_l, giving K_l <= 2^kappa_l. If output in P, C|rho is constant in the remaining variables, so K_l <= 2 <= 2^(kappa_l+1). Corollary: sum_l K_l <= sum_l 2^(kappa_l+1) bounds the OBDD size for this order; #SAT in poly time when kappa_l <= c log N for all l. Scope: one order, one level, fan-in 2. Standard cut-width/OBDD technique, verified subclass only. Does not close G0001.

label: S0078
statement: LEMMA (single split, standard): for a circuit C on X∪Y with κ wires from X-side nodes into Y-side gates, M[a,b]=C(a,b) has at most 2^κ distinct rows, so rank_Q M ≤ 2^κ and log2 rank_Q M ≤ κ. Proof: row a is determined by w(a) ∈ {0,1}^κ (crossing-wire values), since C(a,b)=D(w(a),b) for the Y-subcircuit D; equal w gives equal rows; rank ≤ number of distinct rows.

structure.lemma: One-directional cut bound: if all edges between L and R go from L to R and there are kappa of them, then the rank over Q of the communication matrix of the output (rows x_L, columns x_R) is at most 2^kappa. Proof: by induction on topological order, every R-gate value is a function of x_R and the kappa cross-edge tail values, which are functions of x_L; so f(x_L,x_R)=g(w(x_L),x_R) with w in {0,1}^kappa, giving at most 2^kappa distinct rows.

label: S0006
statement: PROOF. (a) Restricted gate = [R_j(x_A) + S_j >= t_j], R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i. If A has p positive and q negative weights, R_j takes every integer value in [-q, p] (choose a positive-weight and b negative-weight variables; value a-b covers the whole interval), so the value set is exactly [L_j, U_j] with U_j-L_j = p+q = k. The gate is non-constant iff U_j+S_j >= t_j and L_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. t_j-U_j <= S_j < t_j-L_j; this window contains k integers. (b) Erdos-Littlewood-Offord (Erdos 1945): for reals a_1..a_f with |a_i|>=1 and any real x, #{eps in {0,1}^f : |sum a_i eps_i - x| < 1} <= binom(f, floor(f/2)). Apply with a_i = w_ji (i in F) and x = s an integer: Pr_z[S_j=s] <= binom(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f), using binom(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(3r+1) and binom(2r+1,r)/2^(2r+1) = binom(2r+2,r+1)/2^(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(3r+4). Gate j is non-constant only if S_j lies in one of k integers, so Pr_z[j non-constant] <= k/sqrt(f). Summing over j by linearity gives E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(n-k). QED. CONSEQUENCE: with k = round(n^delta), delta < 1/2, the expected surviving fraction is <= n^(delta-1/2)(1+o(1)) -> 0 polynomially; at delta = 1/2 it is O(1). Consistency check (not a sharpness test): k/sqrt(n-k) = 1.155 (n=16,k=4), 1.118 (n=25,k=5), 1.080 (n=49,k=7), above the observed fractions 0.74, 0.72, 0.70 in cm-9e6b480beb584cee. SCOPE AND LIMITS: +-1 weights only (the MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer). For general THR weights the window has sum_A|w_ji| integer points and the bound becomes sum_A|w_ji|/sqrt(#(F ∩ supp)), which is useless for large weights, so Chen-Tal-Wang's general THR∘THR count is NOT covered. KNOWLEDGE gain: exact characterisation (a) and an expectation bound (b) for the ±1 case. ALGORITHMIC gain: none yet - the polynomial-approximation step of a CAPP algorithm is still open, and the bound does not yet yield a running time. Erdos-Littlewood-Offord is classical; the new content is the exact characterisation and the application to the restricted MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer.

Setting: bottom gates T_j(x)=[sum_i w_ji x_i >= t_j], j=1..m, w_ji in {-1,+1}, t_j integer (a MAJ over literals is of this form, negated literals absorbed into the threshold). Fix A subset [n] with |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k>=1, and let z be uniform in {0,1}^F. Let N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. label: S0012
statement: GENERAL-WEIGHT ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA (integer weights, S0007). Setting: w_ji, t_j integers; A subset [n], |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k; z uniform on {0,1}^F; L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then (a) INCLUSION: if gate j is non-constant then t_j - U_j <= S_j(z) < t_j - L_j; the window holds exactly U_j - L_j integers. (b) For f_j >= 1: Pr_z[j non-constant] <= (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j). (c) E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j) + #{j : f_j = 0 and t_j - U_j <= 0 < t_j - L_j}. PROOF. (a) The restricted gate is [R_j(x_A) >= t_j - S_j(z)] with R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i, whose values lie in [L_j, U_j]. Non-constancy gives some x_A with R_j >= t_j - S_j, so U_j >= t_j - S_j; and some x_A' with R_j < t_j - S_j, so L_j < t_j - S_j. These are the two inequalities. Integrality gives the count U_j-L_j. (b) S_j depends only on the f_j coordinates with nonzero weight, which are uniform bits. Each nonzero weight has |w| >= 1, so Erdos (1945) gives Pr[S_j in an open interval of length 2] <= binom(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j). Summing over the U_j-L_j integers in the window gives (b). (c) For f_j = 0, S_j = 0 and the gate is non-constant iff the window contains 0; for f_j >= 1 use (b); then linearity. QED. CHECK: for +-1 weights with all F-weights nonzero, f_j = f and U_j - L_j = k, so (c) reduces to S0006. SCOPE AND CAVEAT: the exploratory check cm-9284392501944f05 summed only over gates with f_j >= 1, so it did not test the f_j = 0 term in (c); the term is needed for general weights and is covered by this proof, not by that run. Progress: bookkeeping. The bound is in expectation, costs 2^k per surviving gate, and closes no obligation (G0001, G0002, G0007 stay OPEN).

label: S0017
statement: REPAIR of S0012(b), general nonzero integer weights (CLAIMED, for review). Setting as in S0012, with f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}. Claim: E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_j (U_j - L_j) * a_j, where a_j = C(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j) whenever f_j >= 1. Proof: (1) Window identity from S0012(a): gate j is non-constant iff S_j(z) lies in a set of U_j - L_j consecutive integers. (2) Union bound: Pr_z[S_j in window] <= (U_j-L_j) * max_c Pr_z[S_j(z)=c]. (3) Erdos Littlewood-Offord: S_j is a sum of f_j terms of integer absolute value >= 1, and the number of subsets with sum in any open interval of length 2 is at most C(f_j, floor(f_j/2)); so each point atom is at most a_j. (4) C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for f >= 1. Hence E_z[N] <= sum_j (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j). Scope: this is an expectation bound with the sum over gates; for f_j = 0 the gate is deterministic and the bound must be replaced by an indicator term, so the statement needs f_j >= 1 or a separate count of such gates. Exact check: cm-8dbbae68545b4cff (corrected window bound: 0 violations in 300 instances; worst ratio 0.707). Does NOT close G0007(ii) (deterministic bound) or G0001.

label: S0031
statement: LEMMA D (derandomised window bound, scope: +-1 weights on A and F, A fixed). Setting: disjoint A, F with |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i + sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i >= t_j], w_ji in {-1,+1}, t_j integer, j=1..m. For z in {0,1}^F let N(z) = number of j with g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A. CLAIM: a deterministic procedure computes z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f) using O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of O(f) bits. PROOF. (a) Let L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji); U_j - L_j = k. g_j is non-constant given z iff L_j + S_j < t_j <= U_j + S_j, S_j = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, i.e. S_j lies in an integer window of exactly k integers. (b) By S0006(b) (sign flip y_i = z_i or 1-z_i, Y ~ Bin(f,1/2), central binomial bound), for uniform z: Pr[g_j non-constant] <= k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f). (c) For a prefix b in {0,1}^p of z, let E(b) = sum_j Pr_{z''}[g_j non-constant | z_{1..p} = b], z'' uniform on {0,1}^{f-p}. Then E(b) = (E(b0)+E(b1))/2, so min(E(b0),E(b1)) <= E(b). The procedure sets b_{p+1} to the minimiser; E is non-increasing along the run; at p=f, E equals N(z*) because each term is then 0/1. E(empty) = sum_j Pr[...] <= m k/sqrt(f) by (b). Hence N(z*) <= m k/sqrt(f). (d) Cost: for a fixed prefix, Pr[g_j non-constant | prefix] = Pr[t_j - U_j - c_j <= S'_j < t_j - L_j - c_j] with c_j the fixed-prefix contribution and S' the free-part sum. S' has a distribution over [-f,f] computed by a DP in O(f^2) operations (exact, with weights 2^{-(f-p)}). Each step evaluates 2 candidates over m gates: O(m f^2) per step, O(m f^3) in total. QED. SCOPE AND LIMITS: (i) +-1 weights only; (ii) A fixed in advance (the adaptive choice of A, G0016, is still open); (iii) the bound m k/sqrt(f) is below m only when k < sqrt(f), so it gives no saving at k = sqrt(n) and m = n^1.5; (iv) no CAPP algorithm follows: the later cost is still 2^k times the surviving count. WHAT IT CLOSES: the deterministic-bound part of G0007(ii) and G0008(i) in the form 'a poly-time computable z with a deterministic surviving-gate bound', for fixed A and +-1 weights. It does not close the adaptive-A question, general integer weights (G0009(b)), or Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5). DEPENDENCY: relies on the S0006(b) window step (CLAIMED, not reviewed by this session). Hand check of steps (a)-(c) passed; exact enumeration cm-5cb23cf8bfcd43c4 (43680 cases, 0 violations) and derandomisation check cm-e0aa5fa35d4a4793 (400 instances; N(z*) = E_last <= E_root <= bound, E monotone, 0 violations) are exploratory computations and are not part of the proof.

S' has a distribution over [-f,f] computed by a DP in O(f^2) operations (exact, with weights 2^{-(f-p)}). Each step evaluates 2 candidates over m gates: O(m f^2) per step, O(m f^3) in total. QED. statement: LEMMA D2 (self-contained replacement of S0031 LEMMA D; supersedes it, no CLAIMED premise). Scope: disjoint A, F, |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; w_ji in {-1,+1} for i in A and i in F; t_j integers, j=1..m; g_j(x,z)=[sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= t_j]; N(z)=#{j: g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A}. CLAIM: a deterministic poly-time procedure outputs z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF. Step 1 (value set): V_j = {sum_A w_ji x_i} = all integers in [L_j,U_j], L_j=sum_A min(0,w_ji), U_j=sum_A max(0,w_ji), U_j-L_j=k (positive-weight subset sums cover 0..p, negative cover -q..0, union covers -q..p). So g_j non-constant given z iff L_j+S_j < t_j <= U_j+S_j with S_j=sum_F w_ji z_i, i.e. S_j in W_j = {t_j-U_j,...,t_j-L_j-1}, exactly k integers. Step 2 (sign flip): y_i=z_i if w_ji=+1, y_i=1-z_i if w_ji=-1. Then S_j = Y - r_j, Y=sum_F y_i ~ Bin(f,1/2), r_j=#{i in F: w_ji=-1}. So Pr_z[S_j in W_j] = sum over s in W_j of Pr[Y=s+r_j] <= k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f), using C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for all f>=1 (from C(2n,n)/4^n <= 1/sqrt(3n+1), n>=1, and checked at f=1). Step 3 (derandomisation): for a prefix b of z of length p, E(b)=sum_j Pr over the free suffix of [S_j in W_j]. E(b)=(E(b0)+E(b1))/2, so choosing the next bit minimising E never increases E; at p=f, E = N(z*) since each term is 0/1; E(empty) <= mk/sqrt(f) by Step 2. Hence N(z*) <= mk/sqrt(f). Cost: exact distribution of each suffix sum by DP, O(f^2) per gate per candidate, O(m f^3) total, integers of O(f) bits. SCOPE AND LIMITS: fixed A; +-1 weights only; bound is below m only when k < sqrt(f), so no saving at k=sqrt(n), m=n^1.5; no CAPP algorithm (cost still 2^k times survivors). label: S0034
statement: INTEGER-WEIGHT SURVIVOR LEMMA (G0009(b)). Setting: A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = |F| >= 1, integer weights w_ji with |w_ji| >= 1 for i in F (zero weights on A allowed), thresholds T_j in Z, gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, z in {0,1}^F. Let M_j = sum_{i in A} |w_ji| and N(z) = #{j : g_j(., z) non-constant}. CLAIM: (i) for each j, #{z : g_j(., z) non-constant} <= M_j * C(f, floor(f/2)); hence P_z[non-constant] <= M_j / sqrt(f). (ii) E_z N(z) <= (sum_j M_j)/sqrt(f) <= m k B / sqrt(f) if |w| <= B on A. (iii) The conditional-expectation fixing of Lemma S-DERAND gives z* with N(z*) <= E_z N. PROOF. (1) Window: g_j is non-constant iff min_x (A-sum) + S < T_j <= max_x (A-sum) + S, where S = sum_F w_ji z_i. This holds for any integer weights, with no gap condition. With L = sum_A min(0,w_ji) and U = sum_A max(0,w_ji), non-constancy is equivalent to T_j - U <= S <= T_j - L - 1. This is an integer window with exactly U - L = M_j integers. (2) Point masses: put eps_i = 2 z_i - 1 in {-1,+1}. Then S = s iff sum_F w_ji eps_i = 2s - sum_F w_ji. Since |w_ji| >= 1, Erdos's Littlewood-Offord theorem (1945: for reals |b_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(f, floor(f/2)) of the 2^f sums sum eps_i b_i) gives #{z : S = s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) for every integer s. (3) Union: #{z : S in window} <= sum over the M_j window integers of #{z : S = s} <= M_j C(f, floor(f/2)). Dividing by 2^f and using C(f, floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) (f >= 1) gives (i). Summing over j gives (ii). (4) Step (iii) uses only that N is an integer-valued function whose expectation is known; the DP for E_p has integer sums in [-fB, fB], so it costs O(m f^2 B) per evaluation and O(m f^3 B) in total. SCOPE: non-zero integer weights on F, arbitrary integers on A, fixed A. Zero weights on F reduce f to f' = #nonzero F-weights, giving 1/sqrt(f'). The ±1 lemma S0006 is the case M_j = k. The lemma says nothing about all z simultaneously, adaptive A, or Chen-Williams 2019.

structure.lemma: INTEGER-WEIGHT WINDOW LEMMA (extends S0006 from +-1 to integer weights; gap G0007(i)). Fix a gate j with integer weights a_i (i in A, |a_i| >= 1, |A| = k) and b_i (i in F, b_i in Z, f' = #{i in F : b_i != 0} >= 1). Let U = sum_A max(0,a_i), L = sum_A min(0,a_i), B = U - L = sum_A |a_i|. For z in {0,1}^F let S(z) = sum_F b_i z_i and N_j(z) = [g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A], g_j(x,z) = [sum_A a_i x_i + S(z) >= T]. Then (i) P_{z uniform}[N_j(z)=1] <= B / sqrt(f'). Proof: (1) Non-constancy needs L + S < T <= U + S, so S lies in an integer window of exactly B integers. (2) Sperner: flip y_i = 1 - z_i for b_i < 0 and y_i = z_i otherwise; then S = sum_{F'} |b_i| y_i + const, y uniform on {0,1}^{F'}. Two subsets T1 strictly contained in T2 have sums differing by >= 1, so the level sets {y : sum |b_i| y_i in an open interval of length 1} form an antichain; hence #{y : S = r} <= C(f', floor(f'/2)) and P[S = r] <= C(f',floor(f'/2))/2^{f'} <= 1/sqrt(f') (central binomial bound, f' >= 1). (3) Union over the B window integers. Hence E_z N_j(z) <= B/sqrt(f'). Summing over j: E_z N(z) <= sum_j B_j / sqrt(f'_j). For |a| = 1 this is k/sqrt(f') and recovers S0006. For weights bounded by W, B_j <= k W, so E_z N(z) <= m k W / sqrt(f_min). Derandomisation: the conditional-expectation fixing of S0006 applies unchanged, since each E_p is an exact DP over integer sums in [-W f, W f] (cost O(m f * W f) per evaluation). Scope: integer weights, A fixed in advance, expectation (not deterministic) bound for all z.
