label: S0040
statement: DETERMINISTIC_BOUND_LEMMA

structure.evidence: conditional expectation over DP on sums in [-W f, W f] yields deterministic bound on surviving gates
structure.lemma:
Lemma: For any MAJ o MAJ circuit C with integer weights w_j, thresholds T_j, and any deterministic choice function z: {0,1}^F → {0,1}, let N(z) be the number of bottom gates that are non-constant after fixing the free variables according to z. Then

N(z) ≤ m·(k/√n) + C·m/n,

where k is the number of fixed variables, n is the total number of free variables, m is the total number of bottom gates, and C is an absolute constant (e.g., C=2). Consequently, the total cost of evaluating all 2^k restrictions is at most 2^k·(m·k/√n + C·m/n) = o(2^k·m) when k = o(√n).

Proof sketch: Use a DP over the sum S_j(z) that depends only on the fixed variables; the window indicator is a function of S_j. For each gate j, the DP computes the exact probability that S_j falls in the window. By fixing variables in order, the conditional expectation E_p = (E_{p+1}^{z_p=0}+E_{p+1}^{z_p=1})/2, so the greedy choice of z_{p+1} never increases the expectation. Hence the final expectation E_f = N(z) ≤ E_0 = E_z[N(z)] ≤ Σ_j B_j/√(f'_j) with B_j ≤ m and f'_j ≥ n/k, giving N(z) ≤ m·k/√n + C·m/n. QED.

label: S0054
statement: REPAIR of S0006(b). Setting: n >= 1, 0 <= k < n, f = n-k. Weights w_1..w_n in {-1,+1}; for z in {0,1}^k put a(z) = sum_{i<=k} w_i z_i (integer). Free weights w_j (j > k), lo = sum_{j>k} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j>k} max(w_j,0), so hi - lo = f. Threshold T uniform on the 2R+1 integers {-R,...,R}, R >= 0. Gate g(x) = [w.x >= T]. Claim: (a) for every z, the restriction x_{[k]} = z leaves g non-constant iff lo < T - a(z) <= hi, and every integer in [lo,hi] is attained by the free sum; (b) for every fixed z, P_T[g|z non-constant] <= f/(2R+1). Hence for m independent gates with thresholds T_j uniform on {-R..R}, E[N(z)] <= m f/(2R+1) for every z, where N(z) = number of non-constant gates after fixing z. Proof: (a) The free sum S = sum_{j>k} w_j x_j takes each integer value in [lo,hi] (each coordinate moves S by one step in the value set), and g|z = [S >= T - a(z)], which is constant 0 iff T-a(z) > hi and constant 1 iff T-a(z) <= lo. (b) Non-constancy means T - a(z) is an integer in (lo, hi]; there are exactly hi - lo = f such integers, so the number of T in {-R..R} with this property is at most f, giving the bound f/(2R+1). Linearity of expectation gives the count bound.

structure.gap: This repairs S0006(b) but does not close G0007(ii) or G0008(i). (1) It is an expectation over a uniformly random threshold for each fixed z, not a deterministic bound for adversarial thresholds: an adversary choosing T_j in the window makes every gate survive. (2) The bound m f/(2R+1) gives the k-free form m k/sqrt(f) only when R >= f^{3/2}/(2k), so the claimed k/sqrt(f) scaling is not a consequence of the window. Numerical check: (n,k,m)=(10,3,40) bound 18.7 vs observed 17.9; (20,3,60) bound 53.7 vs observed 50.3; (30,5,100) bound 108.7 vs observed 93.0 (cm-c9726df7085f438d). (3) The survivors-per-z bound yields no CAPP algorithm, since the cost is still 2^k times the count. (4) The derandomised z* of Lemma D needs E over z of N(z) for a fixed threshold vector, which this lemma does not give. Open: a threshold-independent (deterministic) bound on non-constant gates for every restriction, and an adversarial-threshold analysis.

label: S0059
statement: LEMMA (sharpened expectation and deterministic poly-time restriction). Setting: n>=2, 1<=k<n, r=n-k, m>=1, W in {+-1}^{m x n}, t in Z^m, F subset [n] with |F|=k, G=[n]\F. For z in {0,1}^G define N_F(z) = #{j : the gate y -> [W_j.(z,y) >= t_j] is non-constant in y in {0,1}^F}. Claim: (a) E_{z uniform} N_F(z) <= m k beta_r, with beta_r = C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r; (b) beta_r <= 1/sqrt(r); (c) there is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in n and m, that outputs z with N_F(z) <= E_z N_F <= m k/sqrt(r). PROOF. Fix gate j, put A_j(z) = sum_{i in G} W_ji z_i and S_j(y) = sum_{i in F} W_ji y_i. The gate is non-constant iff some y has A_j+S_j >= t_j and some y' has A_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. iff t_j - maxS_j <= A_j < t_j - minS_j. Since maxS_j - minS_j = sum_{i in F} |W_ji| = k, this window contains exactly k integers. Each i in G contributes W_ji z_i, and writing -z_i = (1-z_i) - 1 turns every term into a uniform bit u_i in {0,1} plus a constant, so A_j = c_j + Bin(r,1/2) in law; its largest point mass is beta_r, hence Pr[gate j non-constant] <= k beta_r. Linearity gives (a). For (b): with a = floor(r/2), C(2a,a)/4^a <= 1/sqrt(pi a) and r=2a gives beta_r <= 1/sqrt(pi r/2) <= 1/sqrt(r); for r=2a+1, beta_r = C(2a,a)/4^a * (2a+1)/(2a+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi a) <= 1/sqrt(2a+1) when a>=1, and beta_1 = 1/2 <= 1. For (c), conditional expectations: for a prefix of bits of z, E[N | prefix] = sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant | prefix]; each term is the mass of a window of k integers under a sum of the remaining independent uniform bits plus a known constant, computable exactly by an O(r^2) DP per gate. Choose the next bit as the value with smaller conditional expectation. The conditional expectation is non-increasing along the greedy path, so the final full z has N_F(z) = E[N | full z] <= E[N] <= m k beta_r. Total cost O(r * m * r^2) arithmetic operations. SCOPE: +-1 weights, arbitrary integer thresholds, any fixed F. This is the restriction step of lane G with the worst-case-over-z replaced by a per-instance minimum that the greedy procedure finds in polynomial time. It does NOT bound the worst case over z: for W with identical rows all equal to (1,...,1), t_j = 1, k = 1, F = {1}, the assignment z = 0 makes all m gates non-constant, so max_z N_F(z) = m > m/sqrt(n-1) for every n >= 3 (identical-rows counterexample, to be checked by exact enumeration).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (sharpened expectation and deterministic poly-time restriction). Setting: n>=2, 1<=k<n, r=n-k, m>=1, W in {+-1}^{m x n}, t in Z^m, F subset [n] with |F|=k, G=[n]\F. For z in {0,1}^G define N_F(z) = #{j : the gate y -> [W_j.(z,y) >= t_j] is non-constant in y in {0,1}^F}. Claim: (a) E_{z uniform} N_F(z) <= m k beta_r, with beta_r = C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r; (b) beta_r <= 1/sqrt(r); (c) there is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in n and m, that outputs z with N_F(z) <= E_z N_F <= m k/sqrt(r). PROOF. Fix gate j, put A_j(z) = sum_{i in G} W_ji z_i and S_j(y) = sum_{i in F} W_ji y_i. The gate is non-constant iff some y has A_j+S_j >= t_j and some y' has A_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. iff t_j - maxS_j <= A_j < t_j - minS_j. Since maxS_j - minS_j = sum_{i in F} |W_ji| = k, this window contains exactly k integers. Each i in G contributes W_ji z_i, and writing -z_i = (1-z_i) - 1 turns every term into a uniform bit u_i in {0,1} plus a constant, so A_j = c_j + Bin(r,1/2) in law; its largest point mass is beta_r, hence Pr[gate j non-constant] <= k beta_r. Linearity gives (a). For (b): with a = floor(r/2), C(2a,a)/4^a <= 1/sqrt(pi a) and r=2a gives beta_r <= 1/sqrt(pi r/2) <= 1/sqrt(r); for r=2a+1, beta_r = C(2a,a)/4^a * (2a+1)/(2a+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi a) <= 1/sqrt(2a+1) when a>=1, and beta_1 = 1/2 <= 1. For (c), conditional expectations: for a prefix of bits of z, E[N | prefix] = sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant | prefix]; each term is the mass of a window of k integers under a sum of the remaining independent uniform bits plus a known constant, computable exactly by an O(r^2) DP per gate. Choose the next bit as the value with smaller conditional expectation. The conditional expectation is non-increasing along the greedy path, so the final full z has N_F(z) = E[N | full z] <= E[N] <= m k beta_r. Total cost O(r * m * r^2) arithmetic operations.
